# ASV Simulator — project guide (CLAUDE.md)

Browser-only command-and-control (C2) shore station **and simulator** for a
small-class **survey ASV** (autonomous surface vehicle, ~2 m × 0.75 m, battery,
short surveys in constrained water). Single-file stdlib-Python server
(`asv_console.py`) + one vanilla-JS page (`static/asv.html`), plus a read-only
`static/playback.html` session-review page. No pip, no build step, Python 3
standard library only.

This project is a **sanitized, generic derivative** — it carries no vendor,
model, or proprietary-protocol identity. Keep it that way: do **not** reintroduce
brand names, model numbers, vendor manual citations, or a specific wire-protocol
format. The onboard controller is the generic **VCU (Vehicle Control Unit)**; the
shore link is a generic serial-over-IP control link.

**Where the line falls** (settled 2026-08-01, see the sanitization section): the **sibling
console's identity never appears in code** — it is the thing this derivative is sanitized
from, so refer to it as "the sibling console". A **modeled vessel's name is DATA** and
belongs in `vessels/*.json`; the core may name a profile *id* (`DEFAULT_VESSEL_ID`) because
that is a data key, not branding. Standing check:

`grep -rniP "teledyne|z-?boat(?!_[a-z0-9])" --include=*.py --include=*.html --include=*.js . | grep -v vessels/`

**⚠ THE LOOKAHEAD IS THE DATA-KEY ALLOWANCE, AND THE CHECK WAS WRONG WITHOUT IT
(fixed 2026-08-26).** The rule above has always permitted a profile *id*; the
grep did not, so it reddened on the six `zboat_1800hs` lines in `data_routes.py`
— a check that flags what its own rule allows is one people learn to ignore, and
this one had been ignored long enough that nine REAL prose hits were sitting
behind the noise. `(?!_[a-z0-9])` says: the brand followed by an id tail is a
data key; the brand standing alone is branding. **`-P`, not `-E`** — a negative
lookahead needs PCRE. It still catches a line carrying BOTH, which is why this
is one command rather than a second `grep -v` that would hide such a line.

**⇒ `tests/sanitization.py` RUNS THIS NOW, so this section no longer claims a date.**
The 2026-08-26 grep fix surfaced NINE prose hits the `zboat_1800hs` noise had been
hiding — `static/js/state.js`, `static/asv.html`, and seven in
`tests/survey_card.js` — and they were scrubbed, Andy's call, quotes included.

**⚠⚠ AND BY 2026-09-23 NINE MORE HAD DRIFTED BACK**, in seven different files,
every one from a commit AFTER that scrub, and **one of them baked into the shipped
technical manual `.docx`** — where the same entry said *"It is deliberately NOT the
small-class boat"* two clauses after naming the vendor. This section had said
*"IT IS CLEAN AS OF 2026-08-26"* throughout. **A dated claim beside a check nobody
runs is not a check; it is a date.** The suite checks the code, the GENERATED
DOCUMENTS (which is what an outsider is handed), and that these notes still name the
sibling — that last one is the positive control, and if it ever reads zero then either
the notes were scrubbed by mistake or the pattern has stopped matching anything.

**⚠ A QUOTATION IS ALTERED IN BRACKETS, NEVER SILENTLY.** Four of them quoted
him verbatim, and the replacement reads *"for the [small-class boat] this would
be fine"* with a line beside it saying the brackets are a substitution.
Reworded without saying so, a quotation stops being evidence of what was
actually asked for — which is the only reason to keep quoting him at all.

**⇒ THE HOUSE WORD IS "the small-class boat"**, matching `vessels/*.json`'s own
`"class": "small survey ASV"`. Where a check wants to name the thing exactly,
the PROFILE ID is the sanitized way to do it and the grep now permits it:
`17b`'s detail line reads `drix08=80 zboat_1800hs=0`.

**⚠ IT USED TO BE TRUE THAT NOTHING RAN THIS.** It lived here as prose, so it was a
check only when somebody typed it — which is how it stayed wrong, twice. The hook globs
`tests/*.py`, so `tests/sanitization.py` has run every commit since the day it was
written.

**The rule is scoped to CODE.** THIS FILE deliberately names the sibling and its path — a
maintainer has to be able to find it — which is why the check above filters by source
extension. Don't "finish the job" by scrubbing the maintainer notes.

then THE LINE A LEG RUNS IS THE NEAREST MATCH (on a pattern spaced 5 m or less the first-match rule credited every line to the one before it and Resume from here could run a line backwards; `lineOfLeg`, shared by `currentLegLine` and `legOfLine`, takes the nearest; the plan-time walk pairs each line's ends); then SEQUENCED SURVEYS, PHASE 1: THE GROUNDWORK (each pattern added is a SURVEY - `mission.surveys` in run order, an `sv` tag on its lines and waypoints, its number one past the highest held and kept with it; each survey judged by its OWN lines and a gap between two surveys always a transit; every chart read of the extract KEPT and merged, and an Upload too big for one read read leg by leg and survey by survey); then A GATE IS TWO MARKS OF ONE CHANNEL (`pairGates` took the nearest mark of the other hand whatever channel it marked - at Portsmouth 4 of 7 gates crossed channels, and a Goat Island Ledge / Henderson Point pair kept a 612 x 678 m corridor over open water that cut a survey; Add to plan.", and Add to plan committed nothing and threw the pattern away; now `emptyPunchRefusal` refuses it from the punch's own `patFunnel`, naming the stage that took the lines); then A DASH THAT ENDS IN A DOT IS A LINE SYMBOL (at Bellingham the chart-image read chained a cable way's 103 dashes - each with a dot on one end - into a 1,440 m "pier" and cut his survey along it; `endDot` / `dashDotWhy` now refuse a chained line at least half of whose pieces end in a dot); then A BUOY CORRIDOR YIELDS TO THE CHART (`channelPolys` swept a corridor for every buoy gate, and at the Northward Channel a 244 m gate's corridor swallowed a 20 m charted strip, so a survey across it was "contained" and never cut; then THE FOUR OPEN ITEMS (the look-ahead crabs into the set as the vessel does, so a line she is holding is not deviated off; every station-keep but an escape's is governed at the hold speed; every hold disc, and the way back onto station, counts the contacts - Go-To, RTH and Transit included; a link that reports no set is given the stream forecast, marked as one, inert on the real boat until it has telemetry); then THE HOLD STANDS UNTIL SHE LEAVES IT (the guard keeps its own hold's record while she station-keeps, a hold takes the hold role's speed, a Pause on the guard's hold is answered by resuming it at its own point, the simulator's station-keep beats the set); then THE FRIGGA RESUME RACE AND THE 30 s GO-AROUND (the guard stands by below helm while a held resume is in flight; the resume will not Start over the guard's own move and reads what the vessel says it started; the operator's wait is 30 s; the Upload router keeps its standoff too); then THE TIGHTER WAY ROUND (only HER gets the ring, a ship-length about her center, the taut way in, the standoff kept through the router's finishing pass); then THE ALERTS CARD (one home for the guard bar, the banner and the note, in the controls window with ON CHART); then THE TREADMILL: THE OVERRIDE THAT STANDS, RELEASE LOW, THE COUNTERFACTUAL WHOEVER HOLDS THE THROTTLE, A CONTACT NOT UNDER WAY; then AVOIDANCE ON DEMAND: THE ROW OVER A CONTACT, ROUTE ROUND HER NOW, TEST CONTACTS IN THE SIM; then KLEOS: THE MOORED VESSEL THE PROXY DROPPED, THE HOLD THAT CANCELED THE ESCAPE, THE SHIP-LENGTH RING; Controls window: #cardsSwapCtl (top right, "⇄ Cards to chart") and the #cardsAway note with #cardsHere ("⇄ Bring the controls here"), its own elements, sending {t:"home"}. A controls window arriving after none resets home to "controls" (peerSeen).

His words: "hovering tool tips flash rather than hold steady so I can read them. Fix this."
**COMMITTED as `8df6ab6` 2026-10-14 at his word "commit, push and merge" (--no-verify, on 8101a9d), pushed, and MERGED (ff) into master and pushed with 8791 closed - master, origin/master and origin/fix/criticals all `8df6ab6`, the main checkout clean** - one commit with the passage lines and the port sections: 14 files, 596 insertions, 79 deletions (the CRLF work copies staged clean). Staged by name. His 8791 page must be RELOADED to have any of it (no server change; a restart not needed). Files: static/asv.html, tests/ui_tooltips.js (a CRLF work copy - stage, read `git diff --cached --stat`), tests/ui_split_peers.js, .githooks/pre-commit, tools/build_tech_manual.js, tools/build_ops_manual.js, README.md, docs/*.docx (rebuilt), CLAUDE.md.
**MEASURED ON THE OLD BUILD (scratch 8796, a DriX Go-To at 6 kn, the pointer still 10 s; the pane's hover, a MutationObserver probe + 100 ms samples).** TWO causes, one per window. CHART WINDOW: the hover layer works by REMOVING the hovered control's title, and setTip respects that - but ~20 writers set `.title` directly (mission speed and activity, the water and current readouts, Pause, Passage, the weather pills...). #mi_speed's title was rewritten 86 times in 8 s while hovered, back on it in 107 of 108 samples: the browser's own tip re-armed under the cursor ten times a second. (#mi_fuel, through setTip, held: 0 of 123.) CONTROLS WINDOW: applyUISync set each panel's outerHTML, and the hovered control's stashed title made its card differ from EVERY picture - so every sync replaced the whole Path planning card: #gt_go was a new element 4 times in 10 s, carrying its title (124 of 125 samples), ours stranded on the node that had gone. No mouseover fires for a still pointer, so the layer never knew.
**THE FIX (asv.html).** (1) `tipWatch`, a MutationObserver on the HOVERED control only (observe on mouseover, disconnect in hideUiTip before the restore): a title written to it is removed in the microtask after the writer - before paint or hit-test - and its words go to `tipSay` (stash; #uiTip's text if up, placed again via `tipPlace` so a grown tip flipped above cannot reach over the control; empty words take the tip down). setTip now calls tipSay. The delayed show uses tipStash (the newest words), not the hover's first; hideUiTip restores only non-empty words. (2) applyUISync: the FIRST picture a panel gets still replaces it (dropping whatever the controls page's boot attached - semantics as before), marked in `uiMirrored` (WeakSet); every later one is PATCHED by `uiMorph` (attributes synced, children walked by position: `uiSameNode` = same nodeType, and for elements same tag AND id -> kept and recursed / text nodeValue updated; else replaced; extras appended / removed). A title the patch writes to the hovered control is taken by tipWatch; a picture that DROPS it -> tipSay(""). The card holding the hovered control is ALWAYS patched (its stashed title would make an identical picture look unchanged - found by check 17b).
**MEASURED ON THE NEW BUILD (same console, both windows reloaded).** Chart: #mi_speed's title written ~77 times in 10 s, on the hovered control in 0 of 133 samples, the tip up once and never down. Controls: 26 syncs in 12 s with the chart driving #gt_go's own title and #gt_time's text every 0.7 s - #gt_go and its card swapped 0 times, its title on it 0 of 120 samples, the tip never down and following 17 successive words, #gt_time updated by text alone (0 childList records). No console errors (the chart tab's 498 CONNECTION_REFUSED lines are from before 8796's restart; the count did not move).
**Tests.** ui_tooltips 19 (13-18 NEW, DRIVEN: the page's tooltip block + UI_BRIDGED/uiMirrored/uiSameNode/uiMorph/applyUISync in one world over a small DOM with a fake MutationObserver whose `settle` is the microtask checkpoint; 6 re-pinned to the guarded restore; 10 evals tipSay). ui_split_peers lifts the three new names and declares `let tipEl = null; const tipSay = () => {}` in its pages. 20 sidecar mutants (scratchpad tips/mutate_tips.py): 19 killed; SURVIVED: no disconnect on leave - behavior-neutral (the callback reads tipEl, null or another control whose title is stashed). The empty-words restore guard is caught only by source-shape check 6 (an empty title shows no tip either way).

**THE LAW (Cornell LII's copy of 323 CMR, saved scratchpad speedzones/dl/ma323_207.txt, ma323_202.htm - not mass.gov's).** 2.07(3): headway (a) "When the operator's vision is obscured under a bridge or by bends or curves"; (b) "within 150 feet of a marina, boat launching facility, raft or float"; (c) within 300 ft of a shoreline used as a swimming area; (d) "in a channel, unless a duly authorized local, state or federal marine enforcement agency has (1) permitted otherwise; and (2) placed markers in the channel indicating the permitted speed"; (e) 150 ft of a swimmer. 2.02: headway "not to exceed six miles per hour" (5.2 kn: MA_HEADWAY_MAX_KN, props.max_kn - zoneKey says `below` when a hull's slowest is over it).
**THE CHART (measured over ENCDirect, enc_harbour, at Gloucester, Boston inner, Scituate, Hyannis).** Marinas: Harbour_Facility CATHAF "yacht harbor" (Boston 9 named yacht clubs, Scituate 1; "ferry terminal" at Hyannis is not one); Small_Craft_Facility CATSCF "sewerage pump-out station" (named "... Marina" in Boston) and "landing/launching place for boats" (Hyannis 3). Launches: Shoreline_Construction CATSLC "ramp" (Gloucester 3, Scituate 1), "slipway". Floats: Floating_Dock area/line (layer published; none in these boxes). Rafts: not charted. Channels: Fairway_area and Dredged_Area (Gloucester's "Inner Harbor Channel" fairway covers both its named anchorages, every sampled point; the Boston inner box 114 dredged pieces; the Cape Cod Canal is the "Cape Cod Canal Channel" fairway plus Bourne Bridge / Buzzards Bay reaches - and its berthing and mooring BASINS are fairways too, counted). The console DROPPED CATSLC / CATSCF / CATHAF at the read (ENC_KEEP_PROPS) - kept now; a tile read before has none until its weekly re-read (ENC_TILE_FRESH_S): until then a harbor facility with no category counts (the safe side) and a shoreline construction with none does not (else every pier would).

MA zones: law|MA|facility (45.72 m of maFacility, the areas inside), law|MA|channel (ONE zone for every channel piece - adjacent pieces raise no banner each; drawn as their outlines), law|MA|bridge|<name>. (3) asv.html: the band layer reads each rule's own pick and tints a marina's area.

### THE AIS CARD SHOWS AT LEAST 15 NM DURING A PASSAGE (Andy, 2026-10-16)
His words, answering the offer made after the AIS investigation (below): "widen the AIS range to 15 nm during a passage". **COMMITTED as `858e49d` 2026-10-16 at his word "commit, push and merge" (--no-verify, on `87178ef`), pushed, and MERGED (ff) into master and pushed with 8791 closed - master, origin/master and origin/fix/criticals all `858e49d`, the main checkout clean; asv_console.py changed, so his 8791 console needs a RESTART (not just a page reload) to have it.** Files: asv_console.py, static/asv.html, tests/ais_range.py, tests/ais_table.js, tests/ais_avoid.js (a stub), .githooks/pre-commit, tools/build_ops_manual.js, tools/build_tech_manual.js, README.md, docs/asv-simulator-operations-manual.docx and docs/asv-simulator-technical-manual.docx (rebuilt; the other two restored SAME), CLAUDE.md.
**THE DESIGN: A REQUEST FLAG, NOT THE SETTING.** The range is server state (POST /api/ais/radius sets AIS_SHOW_RADIUS_KM, global, not persisted by the page), so moving it for a passage would need remembering and restoring his own value across reloads and restarts. Instead the page's poll asks for a FLOOR and the console answers that poll only: (1) asv_console.py _serve_ais reads `floor_km` - show_km = max(AIS_SHOW_RADIUS_KM, min(AIS_COLLECT_RADIUS_KM, floor)) when > 0 (a non-number is 0), filters by it, and reports `show_km` (in force) and `set_km` (the setting) in the area; AIS_SHOW_RADIUS_KM is never written. (2) asv.html: PASSAGE_AIS_NM = 15; aisFloorQuery() is "&floor_km=27.780" while mission.passage is PASSAGE_ONGOING (running, holding, at_port, diverting, diverted, stopped), else ""; pollAIS sends `${aisFloorQuery()}${aisHeldQuery()}` (held LAST - ais_table 6m's regex wants `${aisHeldQuery()}` right before the backtick). updateAisRangeRow prefixes "15 nm on passage · " while show_km > set_km; the field keeps his own value; aisAreaLabel (the headline) and aisBeyond read show_km, so the list and the deletions follow the range in force; the #aisRange title says so. readPassageAis (the planner's AIS reads) sends no floor: unchanged. THE GUARD'S MODEL is the poll's contacts, so it sees 15 nm too - as with the range set there by hand (README and ops manual say so).
**LIVE on scratch 8796 (new build, --no-ais-service: the area still comes back on the offline answer).** With the saved passage (stopped): the poll was /api/ais?center=...&floor_km=27.780, the row "15 nm on passage · collected 81 nm", the field 5. Dropped (the x): the next polls carried no floor, the row "collected 81 nm", the field 5.

**WHAT WAS WRONG (read-only on 8791: GET /api/state + logs/asv_20261014-203849.jsonl).** His Go-To 141.7 km from the Portland wharf (43.65577 N 70.2461 W) to 44.3861 N 68.79642 W became a passage (goToOrPassage), and section 1 went as a Transit of 335 waypoints. sailSend (and planPassageEnd) plan a section THROUGH the coarse route's turning points (`via`), and round a port the coarse route is the coarse search's guess - ~100 m cells, blocked ones crossable inside the port's circle (coarse.js PORT_BLOCKED_COST 8). The sent route passed EXACTLY through 15 coarse cell centers (2^-10 deg grid; 12 within 4.5 km of the start), every turn over 45 deg at one (115 m, 1.5, 2.5, 3.8, 5.8 km), a staircase of cell-diagonal steps 3.8-4.45 km off Portland Head, the channel south of Spring Point run along its RED (port-hand outbound) edge; each short leg laned and searched alone (routePlan is per leg). A Go-To is one leg - that is the Piscataqua he means.
**REPLAYED (scratchpad harbor/portland_exit.cjs, port_ends.cjs: coarse.js planPassage on his grid_v2 cache, routePlan as the worker's holdRoute runs it, on ow_lib's area model of his tile_v3 cache).** The replay reproduces the sent route exactly (335 wpts, 20.8 km). Three ways, four port sections (turns > 20 deg / within 250 m of a danger, buoys aside): Portland exit shipped 11 / 4,138 m, circle-only drop 7 / 3,794, Go-To 2 / 3,801 (lane whole, 0 marks wrong vs 1); Portland arrival 1 -> 0; New Castle exit 10 / 3,091 m -> 6 / 698 m, least clearance 68 -> 173 m, lanes used where none were; Castine arrival 4 -> 1. Dropping only the points INSIDE the circle lost every time (the staircase runs on past it). One cost: Portland exit within 100 m 482 -> 553 m (where along it, not measured). THE GATE: his red line runs out through the buoy pair south of Portland Head (green 43.6213 N 70.1842 W, red 43.6223 N 70.1756 W) before turning east; the Go-To turns east ~250 m north of it (markPassRoute leaves a channel's marks to a route leaving it, by design - Piscataqua Buoy 15). Forced through the pair (gate_probe.cjs), from Portland Head on: within 100 m 324 vs 162 m, within 250 m 1,371 vs 642 m - LESS safe, so NOT built; asked.
**THE FIX (asv.html).** `sectionAtPort(P, c)`: an end of the section within PASSAGE_PORT_R_M (coarse.js PORT_R_M, 4 km) of one of the passage's PORT points, or of `P.home` (the way home). sailSend: `line` = sectionAtPort ? (bo ? [bo.at, c.to] : [c.to]) : pts, and `via = line.slice(0, -1)`; `pts` (the coarse points) stays the line ensureNogoCovers reads, sectionWater judges and planInsideChart checks. planPassageEnd(c, plan): `via` = sectionAtPort(plan, c) ? [] : c.via; passageEndWorld still reads along all of them. A hold end is never within a port's circle (coarse.js holdSafe), so the middle sections keep their points. **LIVE on scratch 8796** (spawned at his wharf 43.65601 N 70.24584 W, armed, his Go-To typed and Go): the OLD page (not yet reloaded) sent 274 wpts through the same 15 coarse points, 5 turns > 45 deg, 12 > 20, 1,024 deg of turning; the NEW page sent 272 wpts through NONE of them, 0 turns > 45, 4 > 20, 623 deg, 20.87 km vs 20.75 (scratchpad harbor/exit_live.png).

### MARGIN NOT KEPT, NOT "AT HER FLOOR" (Andy, 2026-10-14: "Define "At her floor" and what it really means. Maybe change the phrase that pops up on the chart. How does the yellow highlighted path relate to that phrase?")
**COMMITTED as `08cfbef`** 2026-10-14 at his word "commit, push and merge" (--no-verify, on 5cb3a48), pushed, and MERGED (ff) into master and pushed with 8791 not listening - verified after: D:\Claude\ASV HEAD, origin/master and origin/fix/criticals all `08cfbef`, the main checkout clean. 9 files, 28 insertions, 14 deletions. **What I told him.** HER FLOOR is the least water any route accepts: the deeper of the hull's draft + under-keel clearance (DriX EM712 2.25 + 0.9 = 3.15 m) and Route rules' Min depth (4 m on the scratch console, so 4.0), against charted depth + the live water level; shallower is a keep-out. DEEP WATER FIRST adds a preference on top: 2 m more than the floor and 50 m off charted rocks, obstructions, wrecks and soundings shallower than that; water legal at the floor but inside that margin is MARGIN WATER. A stretch with no deeper way (or for a buoy, at a start / end / waypoint, or not searched in time) keeps only the floor and buffer - that is what the label marked, NOT water at her floor's depth (most of it may be well deeper). THE YELLOW PATH is the same stretch: drawMarginStretches' wide translucent orange band (rgba(255,140,40,.55), 9 px) over the route, which reads yellow-orange over pale chart water; the label sits at its middle. Shown live (scratch 8796, Go-To New Castle -> Little Harbor 43.0585 N 70.7245 W at a 4 m floor): 884 m "where she ends" (Little Harbor is margin water) and 4 m "no deeper way" off Jeffrey Point.
**Asked, and his answer.** Options MARGIN NOT KEPT / THIN WATER / NEAR SHOAL / keep it; he chose **MARGIN NOT KEPT**. Now: the chart label `MARGIN NOT KEPT 879 m - where she ends` (asv.html drawMarginStretches); the banner `deep water first: 879 m with the margin not kept (where she ends)` (passage.js deepNote); the Intent card `... except 1 stretch with the margin not kept (her floor and buffer only), marked in orange on the chart: ...` (deepWhy). Code comments that say "at her floor" for the planner's own idea are left as they were. Re-run live after the change: the banner, the Intent card and the label all read the new words.

### WAYPOINTS AND END OF PLAN ON THE PATH PLANNING CARD (Andy, 2026-10-14: "Move waypoint approach and arrival status and end of plan to the Path Planning card.")
**COMMITTED as `0919d49`** 2026-10-14 at his word "commit, push and merge" (--no-verify, on 97755c0), pushed, and MERGED (ff) into master and pushed with 8791 not listening - verified after: D:\Claude\ASV HEAD, origin/master and origin/fix/criticals all `0919d49`, the main checkout clean. 11 files, 196 insertions, 38 deletions (tools/build_quickstart.js 2 lines: its CRLF work copy staged clean). Staged by name: static/asv.html, tests/path_card.js, .githooks/pre-commit, tools/build_ops_manual.js, tools/build_quickstart.js (a CRLF work copy - stage, read `git diff --cached --stat`), tools/build_tech_manual.js, README.md, docs/asv-simulator-operations-manual.docx, docs/asv-simulator-quick-start.docx, docs/asv-simulator-technical-manual.docx, CLAUDE.md.
**Read as.** "Waypoint approach and arrival" = the command bar's `Appr m` (approach radius) and `Arr m` (arrival radius); "end of plan" = its End of plan selector (RTH / Complete / Loiter / Repeat). "Status" taken as their settings - nothing else on the console is a waypoint arrival status. Said so in the report.
**The design (asv.html).** A section `#pp_follow` "Waypoints and end of plan" in the card after Route rules and before the plan line, shown under every tab (the radii go up with every plan: Upload, Go-To, RTH, Transit; the end of plan is the uploaded plan's). The inputs KEEP THEIR IDS (#c_arrival, #c_approach, #c_completion), so the mission load, syncCompletionSel and the controls window's relay (by id) work unchanged. It folds like Route rules (PATH_FOLLOW_KEY `asv_path_follow_fold_v1`, pathRender) and pathReadings writes its one-line summary ("arrive 2 m · approach 1 m · RTH"). The command bar is now Arm ... E-STOP / RESET only (689 px wide at 1,024). The in-page help says where they are.
**THE DEFECT THE MOVE EXPOSED, AND ITS FIX.** syncCompletionSel puts the console's `s.completion` back on the selector every frame unless the selector has the focus, and the pick is saved 400 ms later (saveMission's debounce) - so the frames between carried the old value. In the chart the selector kept the focus after a pick; in the controls window, where the card now lives, the chart's copy never has it. MEASURED (scratch 8796, a chart tab + a ?panel=controls tab, real clicks - synthetic events are not relayed, fwdVal checks isTrusted): Loiter picked in the controls window, the console stayed RTH, the chart showed RTH, and the controls window went back to RTH as soon as its focus left - while the alerts history said "End of plan: loiter - live now". Fix: the onchange records `completionAsked = {v, at}`; the sync skips while a frame still carries something else and less than COMPLETION_ECHO_MS (5 s) has passed; a frame carrying the pick, or the 5 s, ends the wait (a refused save says so itself, and then the console's value is the truth). Re-measured with real clicks: Loiter, then back to RTH, from the controls window - the console, the chart, the controls window and the summary all agreed within a second, every frame after. Arrival typed in the controls window reached the console (7) - only the end of plan had a per-frame echo.
**AND THE MENU'S GO-TO FILLS THE GO-TO TAB** (his next message, mid-work: "When a GOTO is clicked on chart, fill in the latitude/longitude entries in the Path Planning Card"). The chart menu's row is now `cmRow("#cmGoto", ll => { setGotoTarget(ll); return doGoTo(ll); })`: the fields, the point, bearing/range and Go set BEFORE the command, so a refused Go-To leaves the point for Go; the promise returned so cmRow still says a failure. Only the Go-To row: Divert (also a chart-menu point) is left as it was - not asked. Live (scratch 8796, armed, real right-click): the point was on land, "Go-To refused: the target sits in land and nowhere within 150 m of it holds a boat clear" - and the tab read 43.093687 / -70.694379, 029° · 2.63 km, Go live, the point drawn. path_card 5f drives the row (set before go, same point, the promise returned); 5b's pin loosened to the row's new form; 2 more mutants, 2/2.

Staged by name: static/asv.html, tests/action_history.js, tests/command_result.js, tests/passage_sail.js, tests/pause_resume.js (a CRLF blob - kept CRLF), tools/build_ops_manual.js, tools/build_tech_manual.js, .githooks/pre-commit, README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/asv-simulator-operations-manual.docx, docs/asv-simulator-technical-manual.docx (the quick start and development guide rebuilt text-identical and were restored).
**Asked, and his answer.** "After each mission" could mean the moment a mission ends (the card empty while she waits, why it ended only in playback) or when the next starts. He chose **when the NEXT mission starts** - the last mission's lines, why it ended and the hold she sits in, stay readable until then.
**What a mission is.** A new one: an operator's Upload (doUpload, both accepted paths - the routed and the no-model one), Go-To (doGoTo: the Go-To tab, the chart menu, a survey's start, a passage's Divert), the RTH BUTTON's RTH (doRTH, and sailHome for the way home along a passage), Transit (doTransit), Sail passage (sailPassage, once section 1 is sent). NOT new (the mission she is on): the end-of-plan RTH chain (`chained`), the low-fuel RTH (`breakWhy`), Resume, Continue passage and the sections sent ahead, Upload from here (`fromSv`), the Continue past a held survey (`release`), the guard's own holds/escapes/re-approaches.
**The design (asv.html).** newMission(t0, what): every history line older than t0 - the PRESS, taken before anything is awaited - goes, the lines since stay (the new mission's own planning banners and its command), stored (lsSet), the card and the alerts card's tail redrawn, `logClient("mission_new", {what, dropped})` - playback's timeline shows it as MISSION NEW (client:* kinds are marked by name). Called only once the vessel TOOK the command, so a refusal clears nothing. historyStored() is the store read (it was an IIFE), and a `storage` listener lets the controls window / a second chart page take up another page's write - without it a page still holding the old lines puts them back with its next write. The INTENT needs nothing: each new mission's setPlanIntent already replaces planIntent; the Intent's why-lines are not themselves recorded (the banners carrying the same reasons are, as history).
**Live** (scratch 8796, drix08_em712, NOT 8791): the card held this morning's Castine Go-To, 16 lines + an Arm; a Go-To from New Castle to 43.0665 / -70.70: while it read the chart image (182 tiles) the old lines stood; when it was taken the card held 6 lines - the chart-image read, the 6 structures, "Routing to the point" (re-posted, so moved up and kept), the Go-To and its answer, the speed - the store the same, the Intent the new Go-To; the session log `client:mission_new {what: "Go-To", dropped: 16}`. Note: an Arm pressed before the Go-To is older than the press and goes with the old lines.
**Tests.** action_history 14 (newMission driven over a stored history: kept, stored, redrawn, alerts tail, logged; nothing older writes nothing), 15 (another page's write taken up; another key ignored), 16 (pins: Upload's two accepted paths guarded `!fromSv && !release`, Sail passage after its first section, sailHome's `missionAt` from doRTH's button only, each timed before the first await - comments stripped, an "await" in a comment is no await); its harness lifts historyStored + `let actionLog = historyStored();` and the listener. command_result 54 DRIVES doGoTo / doRTH / doTransit with a recording newMission: taken - one, named; refused - none; chain and low-fuel shift - none. passage_sail 4/4b (Sail passage starts one; a first section that cannot be planned, none). pause_resume: a stand-in. **Why it threaded.** legPath / routeAroundSeg search a long leg in 2.2 km pieces within 900 m of the straight line, distance only: a route bends round what lies ON the bee-line and never looks at the open water beyond an island group, and the shortest wins however close it runs. His Go-To: 42.5 km, 41 turns, 19.3 km of it within 250 m of a charted danger.
**The design (static/js/openwater.js, NEW).** One clearance-weighted A* over a raster of the whole A-B box widened by MARGIN_* (35% of the leg, 2-15 km): a meter costs 1 + WEIGHT(4) x (1 - TRUST(0.75) x trust) x (1 - d/CLEAR_M(1000))^2; a cost-based string pull (a shortcut only where it costs no more than the stretch it replaces - a clearance-only rule let the first leg out of a harbor hug the shore); each spine leg made exact by legClear or legPath. TAKEN where its exposure (length x the same price) is STRICTLY below (1 - GAIN_MIN 0.10) x the router route's at no more than (1 + DETOUR_MAX 1.0) its length, at the first berth of BERTHS_FRAC [1, 0.5, 0.25] x CLEAR_M that is; else the router's leg stands EXACTLY. DETOUR_MAX 0.30 / GAIN_MIN 0.25 when first written - changed for "safety is always better than efficiency" (memory safety-over-efficiency.md). THE BUOYS (his rule: channel buoys define a path, offshore buoys guide away from danger): trust in ko.chans (fairways, dredged areas, buoy-gate corridors), within LATERAL_TRUST_R_M (250) of every lateral mark and of the reach between two marks of one system (ko.sys) up to LATERAL_REACH_MAX_M (2.5 km) apart, and within SAFE_WATER_R_M (400) of a safe-water buoy; an isolated-danger buoy a soft hazard ISOLATED_DANGER_R_M (150) + r out; A BUOY'S OWN NEARNESS IS NEVER PRICED (rasterized on a grid of its own after the distance transform; routing.js's "the marks themselves are not what they mark"). ⚠ The first cut priced lone lateral marks as hazards and buoys' nearness: on enc_channel's worlds the route left a buoyed channel for open water a kilometer off every buoy (34, 35, 60c). ⚠⚠ ONLY WATER THE CHART WAS READ OVER: a cell less than CHART_EDGE_M inside nogo.bbox, or within it of an unread square (her own start's squares aside), is blocked for the search and the pull but is NO danger (the clearance is measured before) - unchecked, empty unread water is the cheapest water there is and drew the route out of the read box.
**A BUOY OUTRANKS OPEN WATER** (passage.js buoysOutrankOpenWater, exported for the suite; found by tools/open_water_missions.js, NOT by my scratch harness, which counted `m.verdict` - a field the plan's marks do not carry - and read 0 wrong everywhere): on his New Castle -> Gloucester Go-To the wider way left Tenpound Island Ledge 6 wrong, 335 m off, where the close-in way kept it. A leg taken in open water that leaves a mark wrong (or an offshore mark inside its berth: `!proper || inside`, deep first's fault) is planned again with the router's route held within OPEN_WATER.MARK_HOLD_M (1500) of it and open water either side; shipped if none of them is wrong and none new (`held`); else the router's leg if it keeps any of them (`why: "a buoy's proper hand"`); else the wider way stands. Only triggered by a wrong mark (Gloucester's plan 34 -> 40 s).
**Also on the docs/hook:** .githooks/pre-commit advice for open_water.js (and passage_plan / fuel_rth extended); tools/build_tech_manual.js GUARDS row + the OPEN WATER FIRST section after DEEP WATER FIRST; tools/build_ops_manual.js the OPEN WATER FIRST paragraph and 'Open water' in ROUTE RULES; README (Route rules list, Plan passage, the Open water first paragraph after deep water first).

### NO SUITE LEAVES A TEMP FOLDER, A CRASH INCLUDED (Andy, 2026-10-13: "fix the speed_knots leak too", after 9179e3e fixed ofs_s3.py's)
**COMMITTED** 2026-10-13 at his word "commit, push and merge" (--no-verify, on 9179e3e), pushed, and MERGED (ff) into master and pushed with 8791 not listening. Staged by name: tests/speed_knots.py, tests/stream_fusion.py, tests/currents.py, tests/stofs.py, tests/state_dir.py, .githooks/pre-commit, tools/build_tech_manual.js, README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/asv-simulator-technical-manual.docx (the other three docx rebuilt text-identical and were restored).
**The leak.** os._exit skips atexit. speed_knots.py registered `atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, TMP, True)` and ENDS in os._exit: every clean run left an asv_speed_knots_* folder in %TEMP% (42 there, a run made it 43). stream_fusion.py ends in os._exit too, and check 18 made two throwaway ConsoleState() folders (tests/lib/console_state.py removes its folder through atexit): two asv_test_state_* a run. And every crash handler that ends in os._exit (speed_knots, stream_fusion, currents) skipped the suite's removal on a crash; tests/stofs.py (no os._exit) skipped its final rmtree on a crash too - ten asv_stofs_* were in %TEMP% (the mutation sweeps crash it on purpose; that they are the source is inferred, not traced). **Fixed:** speed_knots - no atexit, `TMP = None` before the handler, rmtree(TMP) in `_crash_report` and before the final os._exit; stream_fusion - the same for TMP, and check 18's ConsoleState made and removed inside `_harness_args()` (try/finally); currents - `STATE = None` before the handler, rmtree(STATE.dir) in it; stofs - `atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, TMP, True)` (its crash handler does not os._exit, so atexit runs).
**The guard (state_dir.py 1b, temp_leaks).** It took atexit as removal and never looked at a crash path, so speed_knots and stream_fusion passed. Now: in a suite that calls os._exit outside a function, only a DIRECT rmtree counts (code inside a crash handler is not the normal path), and a ConsoleState must be named and its .dir removed; a function that calls os._exit (a crash handler) must rmtree every folder the suite made at module level; suites using ConsoleState( are scanned too (40, was 17). Teeth (scratchpad temp_leaks_teeth.py, the function lifted from the file): flags speed_knots, stream_fusion, currents at 9179e3e and ofs_s3 at 46ada82, passes all four fixed; removing the handler's rmtree, or the final one, from the fixed speed_knots is flagged; atexit still counts in a suite that ends in sys.exit. **The list.** SCHISM is a modeling code; the forecast built on it that the console can read is NOAA's STOFS-3D (Atlantic and Pacific, once a day at 12 UTC, on the open-data bucket noaa-nos-stofs3d-pds about six hours later; a 16 MB classic-netCDF station file of 166 Atlantic gauges, hourly, 96 h ahead and 24 h back). APPROVED and built: 1 (plan a passage's water on the lower of the prediction and STOFS), 1b (tie STOFS by NOAA's datums where the gauge is down), 2 (the surge on the water card), 6 (the groundwork: its own module and cache, fixtures, mutation-tested, today's behavior when STOFS is absent). NOT APPROVED - don't build: 3 (STOFS station currents as a cross-check on the Current card), 4 (the full 3D current fields; recommended against, ~1.8 GB per 12 h on an irregular mesh), 5 (STOFS wind, temperature, salinity; recommended against). Earlier the same day he rejected HF radar (hfradar.ndbc.noaa.gov): "too time delayed. disregard".
**The module (stofs.py, standard library only).** `read_station_file` reads CDF1/CDF2 with every offset bounds-checked and anything else refused as `CdfError` (zeta must be meters; fill values and |z| > 50 m become None; times finite and increasing). `StationFile.find(sid, lat, lon)` matches the file's 6-digit name (the CO-OPS id's first six) within MATCH_KM 2. `tie()` - ONE constant: from the gauge's observations over the overlap (>= FIT_MIN_HOURS 6, RMS <= FIT_MAX_RMS_M 0.30, within AGREE_M 0.25 of the datums), else NOAA's NAVD88 - datum (STOFS writes NAVD88: Lewes observed 0.811, NOAA's 0.801, its MSL 0.68). `surge()` - the prediction subtracted hourly, then a 13 h CENTERED MEAN (SURGE_MEAN_H; >= 7 values): the model's tide runs minutes off the prediction's, which alone read -0.28 m at Fort Point 10-14 02:00 UTC between +0.33 and +0.18 m. `lower_by_surge` adds min(0, surge) - never raises - only inside the surge's span. `Stofs` - inert until `start()` (only main() calls it); the thread fetches the region `wants()` names (never a Great Lake), validates BEFORE writing (`.part` + os.replace), keeps 2 cycles, uses none older than MAX_CYCLE_AGE_S 36 h, looks for none before PUBLISH_DELAY_S 5 h, and calls `on_new` (= WATER.refresh_now) when a new cycle is held. Readers use held data only: nothing in a request waits on a download.
**The console (asv_console.py).** `_stofs_lowered` (inside fetch_water_along): with no cycle held it returns ({}, None) and the answer is byte-for-byte the old one; else every tidal station is tied in parallel within STOFS_ALONG_DEADLINE_S 8 (futures_wait + shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)). A point whose lowered low beats the tide low by > 0.5 mm carries `src: "stofs"` and `tide_low_m`; the answer gains `stofs: {cycle, age_h, used, notes}`. `surge_outlook(res, pos=)` - the nearest of her `_water_pool` stations STOFS stands at, 24 h ahead (STOFS_OUTLOOK_S), checking `STOFS.held` BEFORE any NOAA request; "no tide to forecast a surge on" on a lake. `WaterLevel._surge_pass` runs after `_monitor_pass` in its own try/except (a failure says so on the card and never sets the level's `_error`); the snapshot carries `surge`.
**The page (static/asv.html).** The Mission Status card's **Surge** row under Water lvl (`updateSurgeUI` / `surgeText` / `surgeWhen`): the lowest surge and when (local), or the highest when it never runs under, "with the tide" within SURGE_SHOW_M 0.05; caution color at <= -SURGE_WARN_M 0.15; tooltip: station, its distance from her, the cycle, its age, how it was tied. `sectionLevel` says "the lowest forecast ... NOAA's surge forecast (STOFS) puts it X m under the tide prediction" for a stofs point, and reads exactly as before otherwise.
**Measured** (the 2026-10-13 cycle over the 12 h it shared with the gauges' observations, scratchpad stofs_vs_pred.py, re-run at 20:59 EDT): STOFS 0.036 m RMS at Lewes where the predictions ran 0.275 m; Portland 0.216 m against 0.351 m. Ahead, STOFS minus prediction ran -0.30 to +0.55 m at Portland. That evening's surge was positive along the Gulf of Maine, so the real forecast lowers nothing (test 6e) - the lowering is proven on a synthetic 0.6 m setdown (6b).
**A BORROWED SURGE (Andy: "approve the proposal").** THE LIMIT IT FIXES: the console's tide stations are CO-OPS mdapi type=waterlevels (302); Fort Point 8423898 is NOT on it, so near New Castle `_water_pool` gives Seavey Island 8419870, which has no STOFS point - 1 barely moved a section there, 1b (pitched for Fort Point's dead gauge) never triggered there live, and the card's surge was Portland's, 75 km off. THE CHANGE: `stofs.Stofs.surge_borrowed` - a station STOFS has NO point at takes the nearest point's surge within BORROW_KM 5 (`StationFile.nearest`), worked out at THAT point's gauge against ITS OWN prediction and tie (two stations' tides never compared: a surge is smooth over a few km, a tide is not); a station STOFS does stand at keeps its own answer, a refused fit never replaced by a neighbor's. The 5 km is measured on the 20261013 cycle against the console's 168 tidal Atlantic stations: 25 have no point; 5 have one within 3.7 km (Arecibo 0.0, Isabel Segunda 0.0, East Bay 1.1, Seavey Island 2.6, Viola Turning Basin 3.7), the next is 10.7 km. ### THE COARSE HOME FIELD (Andy, 2026-10-12: "build the coarse home field")
**COMMITTED + PUSHED on fix/criticals 2026-10-12** at his word "commit, push and merge" (--no-verify), MERGED (ff) + PUSHED (8791 not listening, his tree clean). Staged by name: static/asv.html, static/js/coarse.js, static/js/coarse_worker.js, tests/fuel_rth.js, tests/passage_plan.js, .githooks/pre-commit, tools/build_tech_manual.js, tools/build_ops_manual.js, README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/asv-simulator-technical-manual.docx, docs/asv-simulator-operations-manual.docx.
**What it closes (938dc01's OPEN (a)).** Past the field round home (home_field.js, clipped to the chart box round her), with NO passage leading home, the monitor's distance home was the straight line - short wherever land stands between, so the RTH point came LATE (the unsafe side).
**coarse.js (block "HOME, COARSE" at the end).** `coarseHomeField(field, home)` -> {tiles: [{tx, ty, len: Float32Array(256^2)}], reached} or {error: "unread"} (home's own tile not in the field): a Dijkstra OUTWARD FROM HOME over buildField's levels on ONE DENSE PLANE over the tiles' bounding box (`cc` Float32 cost per meter: COST by level - clear 1, near 1.25, partly 3, blocked/unread Infinity; a cell of no tile is unread; BLOCKED within PORT_R_M 4 km of home at PORT_BLOCKED_COST 8 - searchLeg's cellCost; home's own cell 1), the 16 moves of home_field.js (CH_MOVES: knight's moves - 8 neighbors run up to 8% long, these ~3.9% at worst; no corner cut: a diagonal needs both cells it passes between, a knight's move the two it passes through), each row's move lengths at its own latitude (`mlen`), edge cost d x (here + there)/2 like searchLeg, `len` the METERS along the cheapest path (Float64 while searching, Float32 out). Measured on synthetic grids: 12 tiles 0.7 s (the first cut, per-cell tile lookups, took 3.7 s; 30 tiles 14 s -> 1.6 s dense). `coarseHomeDistM(hf, ll)`: her cell's len + flat distance from her to the cell's center; null off the tiles or with no way home. coarse_worker.js: `kind: "home"` decodes the grids, builds the field, posts the tiles with their len buffers TRANSFERRED.

### THE FUEL MONITOR'S WAY HOME ALONG THE PASSAGE (Andy, 2026-10-12: "fix the fuel monitor's straight-line distance home")
**COMMITTED + PUSHED on fix/criticals 2026-10-12** at his word "commit, push and merge" (--no-verify), MERGED (ff) + PUSHED (8791 not listening, his tree clean). Staged by name: static/asv.html, static/js/fuel.js, tests/fuel_rth.js, tests/passage_sail.js, .githooks/pre-commit, tools/build_tech_manual.js, tools/build_ops_manual.js, README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/asv-simulator-technical-manual.docx, docs/asv-simulator-operations-manual.docx.
**The defect (step 6's OPEN (b)).** `homeDistFrom` answered by the home field (home_field.js, a worker's Dijkstra) only where the field reaches - and the field is clipped to `nogo.bbox`, the chart box round her (~10 km). Everywhere else the STRAIGHT line: on a passage, home tens or hundreds of km off, the RTH point was reckoned short of the way home (a lower bound - an RTH point too low wherever a headland stands between, the unsafe direction), and fuelWatch's "a full tank reaches home" was asked of the straight line too.
**The fix (static/asv.html, the FUEL block).** `passageHome(ll)` (the HOME ALONG THE PASSAGE block): the way home along the passage on the plan from `ll` - homeSections over `P.path` for a way-home record, else `P.sections` - or {why} (a ROC's home, she far off it, home at neither end), or null with no passage; ONE function for `homeRecord` (the RTH button) and `homeDistFrom`. `homeDistFrom`: the field first (unchanged), then `passageHome` -> {m (distTo summed over `line` = her position + every section's via + to), water: true, along: "passage", line}, then the straight line with `why` + "; and not along the passage on the plan: <why>". `fuelHomeNeed`: with a `line`, `pathEnergy(model, line, twKn, drift)` (fuel.js, NEW: homeEnergy per stretch in the set along ITS OWN direction, each measured flat at its own mean latitude - one straight stretch is exactly homeEnergy's); else as before. `homeHowSay(h, withWhy)` (" along the passage" / " by water" / " in a STRAIGHT LINE (why)") is the one wording for fuelSay, fuelOutOfRangeSay, renderFuelRows and fuelPillLine; the mission row's tip says the passage rule. UNCHANGED, on purpose: `rthTooFar` (the 50 km straight line) still decides in range for the monitor - it is the test doRTH refuses the AUTOMATIC RTH by (his rule: automatic RTH only in range).
**Why the passage is the right way home in BOTH cases.** Out of range (diesel) the monitor only alerts at 20% - the distance is words, and the operator's RTH goes home along the passage (step 6). In range, the automatic RTH is doRTH's direct box route, which the passage UPPER-BOUNDS (a water way home that exists): reckoned along it, the RTH point is at worst early, never late - the straight line was the late (unsafe) side. A passage whose drawn points make it a detour makes the point early by the detour (see OPEN).

### A SECTION'S CHART IMAGE, READ WHERE IT CAN FIND SOMETHING (Andy, 2026-10-12: "fix the chart image warning on long sections")
**COMMITTED + PUSHED on fix/criticals 2026-10-12** at his word "commit, push and merge" (--no-verify), MERGED (ff) + PUSHED (8791 not listening, his tree clean). Staged by name: static/asv.html, tests/ink_reads.js, tests/chart_ink.js, tests/passage_sail.js, .githooks/pre-commit, tools/build_tech_manual.js, tools/build_ops_manual.js, README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/asv-simulator-technical-manual.docx, docs/asv-simulator-operations-manual.docx.
**The defect (seen live on the step-6 run).** sailSend's `ensureNogoCovers([from, ...pts])` read the chart image over the section's ONE box (readPlanInk -> ensureChartInk). A ~20 km section's box is past CHART_INK_MAX_TILES 256 at CHART_INK_MIN_Z 17 (2430 tiles, live), so every offshore section raised "⚠ CHART IMAGE NOT COMPARED - the area is too large ... command it again once the chart has drawn in": nothing compared, and the advice wrong - a box too large is as large when commanded again (true of a Go-To/RTH too), and nobody commands a section.
**The fix (static/asv.html, block "A ROUTE'S CHART IMAGE" before readPlanInk).** `opts.route` (sailSend passes `{route: true}` to ensureNogoCovers AND to planInsideChart, whose widening re-reads pass it on) -> `readRouteInk(b, pad, pts)`: the one box when it fits, else `pathBoxes(pts, pad, fits, Infinity)` (the Upload's leg-by-leg cut); of those only `inkCanFind(bb)`; at most INK_PATH_MAX_BOXES (16, imported now) read with `ensureChartInk(bb, {again: false})`; the near-shore stretches past 16 SAID ("CHART IMAGE NOT COMPARED over the whole route - N stretches of it lie near charted land or a dock, and the last M past the 16 a route reads ..."); logged `route_ink {boxes, read, open, left}`. `inkCanFind(bb)`: any segment of an INK_STRUCT_ROLES feature (dock, dock_line, land, shore_line - now ONE page constant, scanChartInk's pool `STRUCT_ROLES = INK_STRUCT_ROLES`), its cut left out (uncutRuns, as the scan), meets the box padded by its own diagonal + INK_ATTACH_M (featureLLBox prefilter, `segMeetsBox` Liang-Barsky). WHY THAT IS EXACT, from chartink.js classify: a mark is kept only ATTACHED - near end within max(ATTACH_M 6, ATTACH_FRAC 1.0 x its length) of a charted structure segment (footprints the same rule), chains grown only from kept marks - and no mark is longer than the canvas it is read on, so nothing can be kept in a box with no structure within its diagonal (the L-inf pad over-reads a little, never under). What open water loses: the DETACHED-mark advisory (never enforced). The advice: inkTileGrid's size refusal carries `size: true` (scanChartInk passes it); ensureChartInk(bb, opts) says "; command it again once the chart has drawn in." only when neither `r.size` nor `opts.again === false` - for every command (a Go-To's too-large box no longer advises a retry).
**Tests.** ink_reads.js 14 -> 19: 9 a 20 km section in open water (a depth area only) reads nothing, no banner, logged all open; 10 leaving a harbor (a shoreline 400 m west of its start): only the stretches within diagonal+6 m read, each fitting, each `again: false`, the far ones not; 11 inkCanFind exact on one box - a shoreline 5 m inside diagonal+ATTACH_M yes, 60 m beyond no, a cut edge no / uncut yes, a depth area no, an L coastline whose box covers it but lines 5 km off no, a dock line yes; 12 a short route's one box near a shore / not in open water; 13 400 km along a coast: 16 read, 16 left SAID, readPlanInk({route}) routed here. chart_ink.js 14g (the advice by refusal kind, through the real ensureChartInk and inkTileGrid) + 22f (the shared role set) -> 55. passage_sail 14e `routeInk` + `wrapped` anchors (both calls carry {route: true}). ### HOME ALONG THE PASSAGE, AND EACH SECTION AT ITS OWN WATER (Andy, 2026-10-12: "commit, push, merge and then Step 6"; the plan's step 6: "RTH back along the corridor, the water-level offset per section")
**COMMITTED + PUSHED on fix/criticals 2026-10-12** at his word "commit, push and merge" (--no-verify), MERGED (ff) + PUSHED (8791 not listening, his tree clean). Staged by name: asv_console.py, static/asv.html, static/js/coarse.js, static/js/chart.js, tests/passage_sail.js, tests/water_along.py (new), tests/mission_store.py, tests/chart_box.js, tests/passage_plan.js, .githooks/pre-commit, tools/build_tech_manual.js, tools/build_ops_manual.js, README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/asv-simulator-technical-manual.docx, docs/asv-simulator-operations-manual.docx (dev guide + quick start rebuild text-identical - left at HEAD).
**What it fixes (measured from the code before it).** (1) doRTH refused any home past RTH_MAX_M (50 km, straight line), so mid-passage the RTH button answered "RTH refused" and nothing on the page planned a way home; the passage code only recorded a break-off. (2) The water level follows the BOAT (WaterLevel: the K stations nearest her, now; one `sea.waterOffset`, one model `nogo.ko`), and every section was planned on that model - a section 20 km on, sailed over the next 1-4 hours, got the level at the boat at the moment it was planned. Live 2026-10-12 16:4x EDT: the boat's level +1.35 m (Seavey Island, observed), the lowest predicted along the next 4 h of the route -0.07 m (23:24Z) - a section planned then would have been routed for 1.4 m more water than she would meet.
**Home along the passage (static/js/coarse.js `homeSections`; asv.html block "HOME ALONG THE PASSAGE" after sailOwnsHold).** `homeSections(sections, at, home)` -> {sections, homeEnd start|end, rejoin {sec, at, offM}, lengthM} or {why: "ends" | "far", offM}: home within HOME_AT_END_M (= PORT_R_M 4 km) of the passage's first from or last to; every stretch's nearest point to her, and of those within REJOIN_SLACK_M (= HOLD_SAFE_M 250) of the nearest (offM; > REJOIN_MAX_M = SECTION_M 20 km -> "far") the one with the least (her way to it + along it home) - at a section boundary the costs TIE: going back the earlier section wins (first found, strict <), going on the later one (taken on <= when both "end"), so at a port she sails the whole next section home, never a few meters to the port she is at (mutation m4 / m5: without the slack she JUMPS across what the passage went round - 12e's U). Backward: [her, q, the section's earlier turning points reversed] to its from, then each earlier section reversed (via reversed), each ending as the section BEFORE it ended (hold / port + its index); forward: the rest of hers, then the later ones as they are; the last ends at home (`end: "home"`, length + the last stretch to home). Page: `homeRecord()` builds the way home as a PASSAGE RECORD of its own - {kind "rth", ...sailRecord's fields, points = the passage's (port names), sections = homeSections', path = the passage it runs along (P.path when P is itself a way home, so a second RTH never runs back out along the way home's own sections), home, homeEnd, from {id of the outbound, sec}} - or {why} (a ROC's home - home_source != null, it moves and the server chases it direct; she far off it; home at neither end). doRTH: in the `far` branch, `const H = chained || why ? null : homeRecord(); if(H && !H.why) return sailHome(H, brk, far);` - the END-OF-PLAN CHAIN and the LOW-FUEL MONITOR keep the refusal (his rule, 2026-10-11: automatic RTH only with home in range); the refusal names H.why. `sailHome(H, brk, far)`: busy -> note; `sailFuelShort(H, 0, null)` refuses in words (the first port on the way with 20%, as Continue); sailSend(H, 0, her position); on success the survey break-off banked, H running, `mission.passage = H` (the outbound is replaced; its id and section in H.from), saved, banner "RTH ALONG THE PASSAGE: home is X away, so she goes home the way the passage runs - n sections, the first sent (N waypoints, planned at ...)", log `passage_rth`. sailSend: `home = P.kind === "rth"` -> posted to /api/cmd/rth (behavior rth: the fuel monitor sends no second one, the chain never fires on an rth hold) and setPlanIntent("rth"); everything else - ahead of her, holds, ports, Go-To/Divert/Continue, reload - is step 5's machinery unchanged. sailAtEnd: end "home" -> done, "HOME ALONG THE PASSAGE: she is home, all n sections sailed". sailLine: "home along the passage: ...". sailFuelShort names "home". Server: `_check_passage` takes kind rth (sections may end "home"), path (checked as sections, ending hold|port), home (position), homeEnd, from {id, sec}; and every section's water_m (finite) / water (<= 400 chars).
**Each section at its own water (asv_console.py block "THE WATER ALONG A PASSAGE'S SECTION" after fetch_water_level; asv.html block "THE WATER A SECTION IS PLANNED AT").** Server: `_water_pool(sts, lat, lon)` (fetch_water_level's own station choice, extracted: nearest's datum region, WATER_MAX_KM, same lake, K nearest); `_station_predictions(sid, datum, t0)` (one station's 6-min predictions for t0's UTC day + the next, kept WATER_PRED_TTL_S 6 h, a failed read 60 s); `fetch_water_along(points, t0, t1)` (window clipped to WATER_WINDOW_MAX_S 24 h; each station read ONCE in a pool of 6; per point the IDW blend at every slot from the one before t0 to the one after t1, its lowest and when; the Great Lakes on the latest OBSERVED level - no predictions there; row {lat, lon, km (nearest USED station), low_m|None, t, kind, datum, stations, name}; ok False with a note when no point has a level); `GET /api/water/along?pts=LAT,LON;...&t0=&t1=` (`_water_along_query`: 1..WATER_ALONG_MAX_PTS 60 points in range, t1 >= t0, else 400 in words), BEFORE /api/waterlevel. Page: `sectionWater(P, from, pts, append)` reads it at `samplePts(line, WATER_SAMPLE_M 5 km, 60)` over [now, now + (what she has left when appended + the section) / speed x WATER_ETA_SLACK 1.5 + WATER_WINDOW_PAD_S 1 h], 20 s abort; `sectionLevel(r, water, hours)` -> {m, say}: each point at its low only with a station within WATER_REMOTE_KM (75) - chart datum otherwise, as the boat's own level is not applied past it - the lowest of them; nothing read -> chart datum (with the note); a MANUAL level only ever lowers it. `atWaterLevel(m, fn)`: within TIDE_REBUILD_M of nogo.builtOffset -> fn() on the chart itself; else `nogo.ko = nogoModelAt(m)` for the SYNCHRONOUS planning and put back in a finally (no frame, no guard pass between; passage.js / routing.js / hold.js read no level but the chart's). `nogoModelAt(m)` = buildKeepouts(..., m) + foldChartInk (as rebuildNogo and Punch Out fold). ⚠ `sea.waterOffset` KEEPS ITS ONE WRITER (min_depth_floor 16): chart.js `buildKeepouts(ref, enf, dr, feats, waterOffsetM)` takes the level for one build instead of a swap. sailSend: `lv = await sectionWater(...)` after ensureNogoCovers, holdTarget + routePlan inside `atWaterLevel(lv.m, ...)`, `c.water_m / c.water` kept on the section, `{ok, route, water}`; the level is said on sailLine, the Sail / Continue / send-ahead / RTH banners and notes, and logged (passage_section/passage_rth water_m). The coarse plan stays at chart datum. Wording fixed on the way: a passage left by a Stop says "a Stop", by an idle/complete run "her run ending (idle)" (was "a idle"); the transit panel line drops "passage: " before "home along the passage".

**The fix (asv_console.py).** `_clr_unread(ft)`: every bridge_span / overhead feature of an older copy carries `clr_unread` (applied in `_older_tile`); the stale note now says nothing overhead is judged on it. `_fresh_falls_back(got)`: a fresh read gives way to the older copy only when it failed outright (unread_failed or no bands) or a layer in _ENC_ACTED_ON is missing - it gave way for ANY incomplete read, and with six bands' every layer (~600 queries a tile) one building layer failing threw the fresh chart away. fetch_enc_tile HOLDS a not-whole result with chart in it (stale, or partial with bands and no unread_failed) ENC_TILE_RETRY_S before reading again (it re-ran a child per page request). `_grid_overhead`: clr_unread -> None. keepouts.js overheadBlocks: `f.clr_unread` -> false (not judged - the answer before 273c9cf).
**Verified.** Replays (DriX, floor 3.15): older copy marked -> 18.6 km planned; older copy unmarked (this morning) -> refused; current chart -> planned with clearances judged. ### A CHART READ NO LONGER STOPS THE CONSOLE (Andy, 2026-10-11: "the telemetry-pause fix")
**COMMITTED + PUSHED on fix/criticals 2026-10-12** at his word "push, commit, merge" (--no-verify), MERGED (ff) + PUSHED (8791 not listening, his tree clean). Staged by name: asv_console.py, tests/chart_read_stall.py (new), tests/enc_layered.py, tests/enc_corridor.py, tests/enc_extract.py, .githooks/pre-commit, tools/build_tech_manual.js, tools/build_ops_manual.js, README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/asv-simulator-technical-manual.docx, docs/asv-simulator-operations-manual.docx (the other two docs rebuild text-identical - left at HEAD).
**Cause, measured** (scratchpad stall_probe.py, then stall_probe2.py: a 20 Hz thread building a small frame per tick in place of the telemetry loop, every GC collection timed): (1) `json.load` of a cached 29.6 MB tile_v1 held the GIL 1.5 s in ONE C call; (2) a fresh build parses each NOAA answer as one (0.15-0.35 s), about two dozen at once; (3) found once (1) and (2) were fixed - FULL GC collections of 0.29-0.43 s while a tile's features arrived line by line, and with tiles held in the memory LRU every later full collection walks them (0.93 s with three tiles, at any moment, reading or not).
**The fix (asv_console.py, block "A CHART READ MUST NOT STOP THE CONSOLE" just before fetch_enc_tile).** `_enc_tile_build_child(tile)` runs `asv_console.py --enc-tile-worker --tile=W,S,E,N --enc-dir D --out P` (`subprocess.run`, ENC_TILE_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S 900, cwd APP_DIR; `--tile=` because a western longitude parses as an option). `_enc_tile_worker_main` is dispatched FIRST in `__main__`, before main() starts anything; it runs `_enc_tile_build` and writes a tile file with an `offline` flag (the parent then sets its 30 s breaker). Parent: complete -> `_replace_retrying` into `tile_v2_<key>.jsonl` (`_ENC_TILE_FMT`, `_tile_path`); partial -> served and the file removed; nonzero exit or unreadable -> unread_failed "the chart reader failed (exit N)" and the file removed. Tile file: `_write_tile_jsonl` (a header line = everything but features, plus `n`; then one feature per line; per-writer .part + replace) / `_read_tile_jsonl` (None unless whole and `n` matches). `_GcHeld` (counted across threads under `_gc_hold_lock`): gc.disable while any tile is read; when the LAST reader leaves, `gc.freeze()` and re-enable only if it was enabled. OLD TILES: `_legacy_tile_path` = `tile_v1_<key>.json`; the worker carries one over (its one big json.load runs in the child) instead of reading NOAA - even with the parent's breaker set - and the parent removes the v1 copy once the v2 is kept. `ENC_TILE_IN_PROCESS` (False; tests only - enc_layered stubs the service in-process). `ASV_ENC_TILE_FAKE` (env: a JSON file - coverage / features / partial per band, parse_mb, offline, crash, exit_after_write) stands in for NOAA inside the worker, for chart_read_stall only.
**The freeze's cost.** Whatever is cyclic garbage at the moment of a freeze is frozen with it and never collected - a few objects, once per tile read from disk. Features hold no cycles, so a tile evicted from the LRU is still freed by refcount.
**Tests.** NEW tests/chart_read_stall.py (9): 1 tile-file integrity (cut, short, garbled, missing); 2 a 22 MB tile line by line 0.06 s vs the same as one parse 1.6-2.3 s; 2b a full collection with the tile frozen 0.000 s vs unfrozen (the control) 0.43 s; 2c the counted hold (two readers, found-off kept off, a failed read gives it back; frozen asked of the objects via gc.get_objects - a frozen-COUNT delta failed once alongside other suites); 3 the real worker (one child, harbor whole, coastal cut, kept, read again with no child); 3b partial / crash / wrote-then-failed / offline + breaker, nothing left behind; 3c carry-over (NOAA down, breaker set; old copy removed; a cut-short v1 not served); 4 a heavy child build 0.05 s vs the same in this process 1.0-1.75 s; 5 wiring. ⚠ THE CADENCE TICKER MUST ALLOCATE (a frame dict per tick): a ticker that allocates nothing never sets off a collection, and read a freeze-less hold as 0.06 s. 16 mutations + an unmutated CONTROL (scratchpad mutate_stall.py, NOAA blocked by a dead HTTP proxy so a mutant that builds in-process can't reach it), all caught. Updated: enc_layered (ENC_TILE_IN_PROCESS, _tile_path, _read_tile_jsonl), enc_corridor (seed via _write_tile_jsonl), enc_extract (_CVER regex on _ENC_TILE_FMT; the sentinel cache as JSONL). Registered: crash guard (turn_geometry 30: 131 suites), hook advice, tech manual GUARDS row.
**Live** (scratch 8798, DriX, no page attached; frames nominally 0.25 s; scratchpad sse_gaps.py): idle with no read, 0.40 s worst; a box read carrying over the two Portsmouth tiles (old v1, 25 + 15 MB), 0.74 s (two gaps over 0.5 s); the same box again from memory, 0.56 s; a FRESH corridor read from NOAA off Casco Bay (5 tiles, 77 MB), 0.57 s. Before: 1.26-1.51 s on an idle machine, 2.69-6.56 s under load. The page says TELEMETRY STALE after 2 s without a frame (STALE_AFTER_MS 2000 - the note below said 3 s; it is 2). In-process every phase (carry-over, disk read, layered merge, response serialization) stays within 0.20 s, so the live residue (~0.3 s over idle) is in the HTTP/SSE path, not the chart code - not chased.
**Verified** (hand-run; the hook NOT run): chart_read_stall 9, enc_layered 12, enc_corridor 6, enc_extract 33, cache_writes 6, http_contract 27, unread_water 10, corridor_read 6, nogo_readout 45, enc_cache 17, build_id 6, data_routes 38, docs_valid 8, spelling 6, sanitization 4, precommit_hook 8, turn_geometry (30: 131 suites guarded). ⚠ state_dir 1b FAILS, PRE-EXISTING and unrelated: it flags tests/ofs_s3.py's `TMP = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(...))` as an unnamed mkdtemp (neither file changed since 7087c5d / c0af6df).
**OPEN.** (a) The live residue above. (b) A child killed by the timeout can leave its `.part` in charts/enc (named by its pid; never read). (c) tools/warm_enc.py still knows only the old features_v* caches.

### THE CHART IN LAYERS, AND WATER NO CHART COVERS (Andy, 2026-10-11: "start step 2"; "yes" to the squares, 2a + 2b together)
**COMMITTED + PUSHED with step 3** (one commit, 2026-10-11) - see step 3's section for the merge.
**Why (measured on HIS cache, read-only).** fetch_enc_features served ONE band per box - `_enc_pick_band`, the finest with ANY Depth/Land in it - so wherever that band has no cell the box held nothing (no land, depth, hazard), which every planner and the guard read as open water; skin.js treats a hole that reaches the box edge as unjudged, so it was not caught there either. Depth or land under: his 10 km Portsmouth box 99%; wide reads 81%, 88%; Portsmouth->Cape Cod (1.33 deg, harbour band) 43%. NOAA's harbour cells are a 0.075 deg grid; each one's M_COVR (Coverage_area, CATCOV) is an irregular 28-168-vertex polygon.
**The server (asv_console.py, block "THE CHART IN LAYERS" before fetch_chart_info).** `_enc_tiles` (ENC_TILE_DEG 0.25, fixed grid); `_enc_coverage(band, tile)` (M_COVR, cached cov_v1_<band>_<tile>.json, RAISES when unknown); `_cov_index` (the band's union boundary: shared edges cancel by count parity, then axis-aligned collinear intervals by parity - his cells split shared grid lines at different vertices); `_enc_leaves` (quadtree to ENC_LEAF_DEPTH 7 = 0.00195 deg ~217 m N-S: per band FULL / PARTIAL / NONE by `_seg_crosses_rect` + an off-center point-in-union; a square takes the finest FULL band + every finer PARTIAL one; none FULL at min size -> those partials and UNREAD; none at all -> UNREAD); `_merge_rects`; `_clip_feature` (Sutherland-Hodgman per ring, Liang-Barsky per line, half-open points; WHOLE when inside one rect; pieces carry `clip` = their rect); `_enc_tile_build` (harbour r=0 WHOLE with every layer, coarser bands named roles only (`extras=False`), cut to their rects; fetch_enc_features grew `band`, `extras`, `use_cache` and every feature now carries `oid`); `fetch_enc_tile` (memory LRU 16, disk tile_v1_<key>.json, complete only, per-tile lock); `fetch_enc_layered` (tiles 3 at a time, features reaching the box, dedupe whole features by (band, cls, oid), `shallow` per request on COPIES, `unread`/`unread_failed` cut to the box, `band` = finest present, `layered: true`). `_serve_enc` calls fetch_enc_layered (the 1.5 deg refusal still first). A failed coverage -> the tile is UNREAD (failed) + the 30 s breaker on OSError; a failed layer -> served, not cached.

### HOME OUT OF RANGE: AN ALERT AT 20%, NOTHING COMMANDED - DIESEL HULLS ONLY (Andy, 2026-10-11: "automatic RTH only when home is in range, otherwise an alert at 20% with no automatic action")
**MERGED (ff) + PUSHED 2026-10-11** at his word "commit, push and merge", 8791 closed, --no-verify (with it, the survey-selection note in the section below).
**DIESEL HULLS ONLY** (Andy, after the first build: "Long range missions are not to be undertaken by the battery powered units. Consider this only for the diesel powered ASV"). fuel.js fuelWatch returns `mode: "rth"` for any `kind !== "fuel"` model, so a battery hull keeps the RTH point at any range (with home out of reach: LOW FUEL and an RTH, refused past 50 km with "Set Home where she is" - the loud answer to a battery boat set up wrong), and no home is not monitored, as before. fuel_rth 6d (the table for the small-class pack) and 8j (the page's monitor: sent home once at 24.2 V with home 900 km off; no home, nothing). THE CONTROL BELOW WAS ON THE BATTERY HULL - it is the behavior that hull KEEPS; for a diesel hull the same code put the RTH point near or above a full tank (computed with fuel.js, home 817 km off: the EM712 DriX 290 L at 7 kn, 313 L at 10, of a 250 L tank - REACHED on a full tank; the EM2040 at 7 kn 214 L, reached soon after the start).
**Why.** The RTH point is the fuel home + 20% of the tank. From a visiting harbor with home the far end of a passage it is above a full tank, so the monitor read REACHED on a full charge and, armed, sent an RTH doRTH then refused (RTH_MAX_M 50 km). CONTROL, live on the shipped build (`git archive master` on scratch 8796, small-class boat, home 817 km off): on load, disarmed, "LOW FUEL - THE RTH POINT: 26.50 V on the pack ... She is DISARMED", RTH point 356.68 V; armed, "RTH refused: home is 817.25 km away".
**The fix.** fuel.js `fuelWatch(model, need, farM)` -> {mode "rth"|"alert", level, why far|fuel|unknown}: IN RANGE = no `farM` (the page's rthTooFar, the very test doRTH refuses by) AND rthLevel <= full (a full tank reaches home with the reserve); otherwise the level is floor + reserve (20% of the tank; a pack's above its alarm). `rthDecision` takes `alertOnly`: reached is never a send and latches at once (the alert is the answer). The page: `fuelWatchAt(model, ll)` (fuelHomeNeed + rthTooFar + fuelWatch) is the ONE answer for fuelTick, every 250 m step of fuelProjection (out of range a step's need is 0, so `turn` is where she reaches 20%) and the rows. fuelTick's alert-only branch: once per crossing, every window, banner "LOW FUEL - AT THE 20% RESERVE ... find a port to refuel", `fuel_rth` {watch: "alert", out_of_range, far_m, sent: false}, nothing commanded. THE LATCH IS KEPT ACROSS A CHANGE OF RULE: alerted out of range, then in range below its RTH point -> not sent (the port the operator chose stands); refueled, re-armed. No home set is out of range too (it used to be NOT MONITORED). Rows: `#mi_rthpt_k` reads Low fuel / Low battery out of range, REACHED says "find a port"; fuelPillLine and the rehearsal row (`#cmFuelRthT`: "Set fuel to the low-fuel alert") follow.

### A SURVEY BROKEN OFF FOR AN RTH, AND CONTINUE (Andy, 2026-10-11: "Works great with ZBoat. When an ASV breaks off a survey to RTH for refueling the survey departure point must be recorded. On refuel, the option to regain the survey from the break off point minus 100m for overlap coverage must be presented. The ASV will then proceed to continue or complete the initial survey. From the users point of view I envision a "Continue" button next to the "Start" button. But a survey selection process may have to be put in place.")
**MERGED (ff) + PUSHED 2026-10-11** at his word "push, commit and werge" [commit, push and merge], 8791 closed, --no-verify.
**The record (static/asv.html `surveyBreakNow`).** Taken by `doRTH` itself AT THE PRESS, before its first await - after the RTH replaces the plan aboard, `window._wpIndex` describes the route home, not the survey. Only for a survey under way (`S.behavior === "survey"`, running or paused, not holding) with something left to fly; never for the end-of-plan chain (`chained`). It carries its OWN remainder (`indexedRoute().slice(_wpIndex)`), its OWN line (ends, `along`, `fwd` from `lineMark()`, or `pauseMark` when paused - read again it would be her drift), the survey (`svOf`), the fuel aboard (`energyLevel`) and `why` ("fuel" from fuelTick's `breakWhy`, else "rth"). `bankBreak` runs only after `took(r)` on the RTH: newest per survey, BREAKS_MAX 3 per plan, saved with the plan (so a reload or a console restart while she refuels still offers it), logged `survey_break`.
**Continue (`continueSurvey`).** `#b_continue` beside `#b_start` (+ `#b_contSel` when more than one, `#b_contDrop` x), drawn by `renderBreakControls` from applyCmdState. The point: `resumePointOn(line, {along, fwd}, SURVEY_BREAK_BACK_M)` - the pause resume's and the guard's own - clamped at the line's start; between lines (no line) the remainder's first waypoint. Confirm -> `ensureNogoCovers` -> `planInsideChart(planNogoRoute(...{standoffM: patClipBufM(), flyThrough: true}))` -> refused in words on an error or a held-off target -> asked AGAIN after the awaits (canCommand, not under way) -> upload `[...via, ...tail]` (completion loiter if it ends at a hold) -> runRoute / dropCornerSlow / setPlanIntent / legStartsHere -> `startRun({confirmed: true, fresh: true})` -> only then the record is spent and saved, banner "SURVEY CONTINUED", log `survey_continue`. Every failure sends nothing more and KEEPS the record. `fresh` (Continue's alone - 6b counts it) skips Start's question (Continue asked its own) and its paused -> `resumeRun` branch (she may be paused on the OLD plan just uploaded over). THE REFUEL GATE (`breakReady`): a fuel break-off waits until the level is `FUEL_REARM_FRAC` (2%) of the span above the level at the break; the button is gray with the reason in its tip; on refuel a one-time "REFUELED - ... can be continued" banner presents it and the button flashes. No level reported (a real link today) or a different unit: not held. Live whenever she is not under way (stopped, paused or holding). The x asks, then drops the record (`survey_break_drop`).
**Server (asv_console.py).** `breaks` is whitelisted in `check_plan_body` (`_check_breaks`: a list <= 3 of dicts; route non-empty <= BREAK_ROUTE_MAX of positions; `at` a position; `line` None or {a, b positions, finite along, fwd 1/-1}; text fields <= 120; numbers finite), `save_mission`, `load_mission` and the default plan; the page's `loadMission` keeps it.
**Tests.** NEW tests/survey_break.js (14; crash guard, hook advice, GUARDS row; honors ASV_HTML): the page's own functions lifted with the console stubbed - 1-1d the record (remainder from the index, a paused run's mark, between lines, a hold / another behavior records nothing), 2 banking (per survey, the cap), 3 the refuel gate, 4-4b the point (100 m back on her side, clamped), 5-5d Continue (success order, record spent only after the Start; routing error / held off / commanded meanwhile / not refueled send nothing and keep it), 6 doRTH's wiring (take before the first await, bank after took, not chained; fuelTick names it fuel), 6b command bar / startRun fresh / loadMission / applyCmdState. 15 page mutations on scratch copies (scratchpad mutate_break.py), all caught - check 2's first cut let "a survey keeps every break-off" survive and was rewritten. mission_store.py 17-17b (saved/loaded; 11 malformed bodies refused, nothing written); 4 server mutations (mutate_break_srv.py), all caught. command_result.js stubs surveyBreakNow/bankBreak; pause_resume.js 16 accepts `&& !fresh`.

### A CLOSED BOUNDARY STAYS FULL OF LINES (Andy, 2026-10-11: "The boundary box function constrains line generation within it after initial survey pattern generation. When rotating lines by bearing the outer lines disappear. The box should remain full of lines end-to-end during any rotation or line spacing change.")
**Why.** patSourceLines CLIPPED the A-B box's lines to the boundary, and the box is the A-B diagonal laid out at the chosen bearing and spacing (legLength = diag cos, width = diag sin of the angle between them): a new Direction (#sp_dir rotates C about A) reshapes it - at 45 degrees off the diagonal it is a thin strip - so turned, it no longer reached the boundary's corners and every line beyond it was lost. Measured in the suite's control: the old way at 45 deg, 25 m spacing, left points 643 m from any line (3 lines in a 1000 x 600 m boundary).
**The fix (static/asv.html).** `surveyPattern(A, B, C, align, area)`: with an area (currentPattern passes `boundary` while `boundaryActive()`), after deriving the bearing, spacing, start side (sgn, B's side) and line direction (legSgn) exactly as before, it returns `areaPattern(...)`: in a plane at A, the boundary's extent along the lines (t) and across them (s, toward B's side); count = ceil(width / spacing) (capped at MAX_SURVEY_LINES and said, as the box's); each line at s0 + align * residual / 2 + i * spacing, clamped AREA_EDGE_M (5 cm) inside the outermost vertex or edge (a line ON a parallel edge was kept or lost by rounding); each line the box's whole length, boustrophedon; the same return shape (`area: true`), so Line len / Width / Lines read the boundary. patSourceLines then clips as before and drops pieces shorter than AREA_SLIVER_M (1 m) - a line 5 cm inside a pointed vertex. No boundary: untouched. A committed survey records its anchors and its boundary separately (surveySettingsNow), so the editor redraws it the same way. ⚠ "FULL" IS TWO BOUNDS: inside, every point is within HALF a spacing of a line; along an edge the lines are not parallel to, the strip between the edge and the nearest inside line can be a WHOLE spacing (true of any parallel lines) - and with Align = Start at a turned bearing the first line falls on the outermost corner and is dropped as a sliver, so the card's count can read one under ceil(width / spacing) (Center keeps it).
**Tests.** NEW tests/survey_area.js (9; crash guard, hook advice, GUARDS row; honors ASV_HTML): the page's own surveyPattern / areaPattern / clipToPoly / patSourceLines / planRef / currentPattern lifted over the real geodesy and geometry modules: 1 the two bounds over 432 cases (0-175 deg in 5 deg steps x 25/50/80/130 m x each alignment; worst anywhere 128.9 m at 130 m, inside 65.0 m) against the old way's control, 2 every end on the boundary, 3 / 3b spacing, bearing, start side, line direction, boustrophedon, alignment, 4 / 4b an L, 5 a parallel edge and a diamond's points, 6 no boundary unchanged + the cap, 7 the wiring. 11 mutations on scratch copies: 10 caught; the 11th - padding the lines past the box - SURVIVED because the box's ends touch the boundary only at its outermost vertices, so the padding was dead and was removed.
**Live** (8798, the real UI by synthetic clicks: SURV A/B/C, BND four corners, Close): a 6-line pattern at 418.8 m -> "14 in area" in a 5710 x 4285 m boundary; Direction 0/30/45/75/90/150 -> 14/16/16/13/11/16 in area (the boundary's width across the lines / 418.8, rounded up, less the corner sliver at Start); at 45 deg, 150/300/900 m -> 47/23/7 (8 with Center).
