### THE MISSION'S FUEL AND THE RTH POINT (Andy, 2026-10-11: "In the mission status card add projected fuel usage for mission. Use the DriX Fuel Planner and the Transit Calculator projects for reference. Estimate for BEN and ZBoat until we have hard data. Monitor for available fuel to RTH. This point is to be calculated by projected having 20% fuel on arrival home. Send Alert and shift mission to RTH when fuel hits value.")
**What.** The Run block carries `#mi_fuel` (label Fuel, or Battery on an electric hull: "~38 L · 176 L (70%) left", or "at home" when the run ends in an RTH) and `#mi_rthpt` ("51 L · 1.8 L above", "51 L · reached in 3.19 km" where the plan brings her down to it, "REACHED · ..." red); the breakdown is in their tips (the card is 196 px wide - the first cut wrapped to 3-4 lines). The energy pill's tip carries the RTH point too (the Run block hides without a plan). `fuelTick` runs on EVERY state frame (inside a try in onState - a fault is said once and never takes the guard's frame down): at the point it alerts (banner, alerts card, history, session log `fuel_rth`) and calls `doRTH({why: "⚠ LOW FUEL, at the RTH point (... aboard)"})`, whose standing banner then begins with the reason (the alert itself is replaced within half a second by the RTH's progress banners - the reason had to ride the one that stays). ONCE per crossing (fuel.js `rthDecision`: latch; re-armed only 2% of the span above it), from the supervising window only (every window alerts); an RTH the operator then changes STANDS; reached while disarmed / E-STOP / the guard's escape it is said and she is sent the frame she can be (`fuelTick` asks the send BEFORE "already said" - the first cut returned on `alerted` first and never sent a boat armed after the alert; fuel_rth.js 8c); already on her way home, latched and nothing sent. REHEARSAL (sim): the chart menu's "Set fuel to the RTH point" (`#cmFuelRth`, gated `canSpawn()`) posts `/api/cmd/energy {level}` - a NEW sim-only branch (Engine/SimVcu `set_energy_level`; 409 under the override or on a real link, 400 for a non-number) - just below the point.
**The model (static/js/fuel.js, pure).** The SIM'S OWN burn law off the vessel file's `power` block - fuel L/h = idle + (full - idle)(v/high)^exp, clamped; battery V/s = idle + load v/high, NOT clamped (both exactly as asv_console.py's tick and state() write them). A leg's TIME is its length over the ground speed (`legGroundMs` - moved into targets.js, the CPA route clock now asks the same function) and its FUEL that time at the through-water burn - the Fuel planner's engine.py and the Transit Calculator's fuel.py do the same. The reserve is 20% of the TANK, not of what is aboard (both reference projects; Transit's mutate.py fails a load-based floor). ⚠ A BATTERY'S EMPTY IS ITS FACTORY ALARM (`battery_v.warn`), not the gauge's 0% (`empty`): 20% of the gauge on the small-class boat arrives at 19.7 V, below the console's critical band and the 23 V alarm at which the maker says to bring her back to shore. `measured` is read off the file's source ("MEASURED..."): the DriX's are, BEN's and the small-class boat's are not.
**The way home (static/js/home_field.js, home_field_worker.js).** MEASURED: one 3.5 km RTH up the Piscataqua held the page's thread 1.6 s in the planner (a longtask observer round the RTH button), and the guard runs on that thread - so the planner cannot be asked from every frame or every step of a mission. Instead a 16-neighbour Dijkstra (sides, diagonals, knight's moves - 8 alone run up to 8% long; no blocked corner cut) outward from home over the planner's own conservative raster (`rasterKeepouts` at `nogo.buffer`), Float64 (a Float32 field read a 0.7 seed as stale and propagated nothing - and a 32-bit field hangs the run), 1M cells in ~0.56 s. ALL of it in the worker, the raster too (it held the thread 374 ms on the page for ~900k cells); the model goes over once per generation (`nogo.ko` is a new array on every rebuild: `homeKoGen`), and a build is one message. The grid: home + boat + plan + 1.5 km, clipped to `nogo.bbox`, >= 5 m cells, <= 1.5M cells; rebuilt when home, buffer or model change or a point leaves it. Where it does not reach (building, outside it, a closed basin) the STRAIGHT LINE stands and the rows say "straight line" (amber). Against the real planner: 3.63 km by the field vs the 3.69 km the planner laid (the lanes keep right); the reserve covers it. ONE estimate (`fuelHomeNeed`: field distance at the TRANSIT speed, the set along the straight line home) for the monitor AND every 250 m step of the card's projection.
**The small-class boat's drain, refitted (vessels/zboat_1800hs.json `power.source`).** From the maker's Z-Boat and Q-Boat User's Guide, January 2017 - his copy is `Downloads\Z-Boat and Q-Boat Users Guide_Jan17.pdf` (p. 3 spec table: survey 3-3.5 kn, "up to 4.5 hours, depending on configuration"; p. 8: start 26-27 V, 23 V alarm = bring her back to shore, 18 V complete failure; p. 13: "30 minutes to 90 minutes" on three 24 V 10 Ah NiMH packs). Drain 0.0006 / 0.0025 -> 0.0001 / 0.0011 V/s: 90 min full -> 23 V at 3 kn (it was 32 min, which put a home 3.6 km away beyond reach on a FULL pack - the card read "REACHED" at 26.5 V), 49 min at 6 kn, 3.6 h to 18 V. ⚠ The file's source line names no vendor (sanitization: the house word is "the small-class boat" in code and generated docs; his quote is altered in brackets, "[the small-class boat]"; vessels/ and these notes are exempt).
**Tests.** NEW tests/fuel_rth.js (17; registered: crash guard, `.githooks/pre-commit` advice, GUARDS row; honors ASV_HTML): 1 lifts the server's burn/drain lines and runs them in Python (BOTH copies of the burn line - tick and state() - must be there and identical, or a mutated one passes on the other), 2 the hulls' figures, 3 a leg in a set by hand, 4 the reserve, 5 the turn point vs the closed form, 6 the decision table, 7-7c the field (never short, <= 3%, no corner, a pier home, a closed basin), 8-8d the page's own fuelTick driven frame by frame, 9-9d the wiring. 21 mutations on scratch copies, all caught (the 32-bit field by a HANG). energy_chartinfo.py 13-13c (the sim `level`; 3 mutations caught). target_cpa.js passes `legGroundMs` into its cpaTrack sandbox; ais_avoid untouched.

### THE AIS CARD KEEPS ITS OWN ORDER (Andy, 2026-10-10: "The jumpy characteristic of the AIS card has returned. Structure this cards contacts by order of acquisition then do not reshuffle. Once a vessel is out of selected range, one line through it in red. allow the user to scroll contacts. Allow the user to drag contacts to selected position. Like the top position. Allow the user to delete a contact, but bring it back if it comes back into range. Do not disturb current running console.")
**Why.** renderAisTable sorted the rows by range (or the clicked column) on EVERY update, so every 8 s poll moved rows as ranges changed; it drew at most AIS_MAX_ROWS (60), and the grace sweep removed a contact on its second missed update. In the order of acquisition a cap would cut the NEWEST contact, so the cap went too.
**The fix (static/asv.html, asv_console.py).** (1) THE LIST'S OWN STATE: `aisList` = `order` (keys in acquisition order, the last AIS_LIST_MAX 400 kept) + `removed` (key -> armed), persisted as `asv_ais_list_v1`; `last` (memory only) holds each contact's newest report. `aisListUpdate(liveRows, c, heard, farRpts)` is the one door: newcomers are appended at the END (a batch first seen together nearest first), nothing reorders, and it returns rows `{k, r, state, beyond}` - live / out (held, past the range) / lost (held, inside it, dimmed 0.45) - with `beyond` true for EVERY row past the range, a live one included (the server serves the simulator's test contacts wherever they are placed, `_ais_test_snapshot`). (2) REMOVAL: `aisRemove` (the row's x) arms her only if the feed answered (`aisHeard`: state ok/empty) and she is not in range; an answered poll that finds her out of range (absent, or reporting beyond it) arms her; armed and in range again, she is acquired again at the bottom. A failed, erroring or warming-up poll (all arrive empty) is never her leaving. (3) THE OPERATOR'S ORDER: only the grip (`.aisGrip draggable`) drags, so the rest of the row stays selectable; delegated listeners bound once in ensureAisSkeleton; `aisMoveTo(k, before)`; a header click is `aisSortOnce` - one sort written into `order`, no arrow, never re-applied. (4) A HIDDEN CARD STILL ACQUIRES: renderAisTable's hidden branch runs aisListUpdate (no CPA, nothing drawn) - the first build acquired only while the card was drawing. (5) ONE THAT SAILS OUT: the server stops sending her in `vessels` the moment she crosses, so the page's last report was from just INSIDE the line and she read "not reporting". `/api/ais?...&held=k1,k2` (`aisHeldQuery`: order keys not in the last live set, <= 400) and, at sea, the COLLECTED contacts named there and past the show radius come back in `beyond`, ranged, apart from `vessels` - the guard's model (`aisVessels`) is untouched; `aisBeyondRpts` refreshes `last` for held keys. Caught LIVE on 8798: the narrowing test passed only because those last reports were already beyond the narrowed range. (6) THE LINE: `AIS_OUT_LINE`, a 2 px #d9534f gradient on every cell (one unbroken stripe, which a text-decoration is not), keyed on `beyond`; CPA/TCPA "–" when not live; the headline counts `nIn` in range, out of range, not reporting. No row cap: the card scrolls (the `.rsz` panel is the scroller since the split-windows work; `.rszbody` uncaps the body's 46vh).
**Designs not taken.** Dead-reckoning a held contact by her sog/cog to decide out vs not reporting (a guess where the server knows); returning everything collected past the range (hundreds per poll in a busy port); persisting `last` (a reload shows a held contact again as soon as `beyond` or `vessels` reports her; her slot is kept meanwhile).
**Tests.** ais_table 50: 6-6m drive the page's own list functions (and its renderer with the card hidden) through update sequences - order, held/out/lost, removal both ways, unanswered polls (6h), hidden acquisition (6i), live-beyond (6j), removed-beyond then range widened (6k), sailed out with and without the server's report (6l), the poll's `held`/`beyond` wiring (6m), drag and the one-shot sort (6f), persistence (6g); 21/21b/22/22b/22c are source checks (no sort, no cap, the headline lifted and run, one removal path, the stripe, grip-only drag). 25 page mutations, all killed (TEETH table in the suite). ais_range 28: 12 and 12b (the server's `held`/`beyond`), 3 server mutations killed. ais_avoid's sandbox stubs `aisHeldQuery`/`aisBeyondRpts` (its 12b lifts pollAIS, which threw into its catch).
**Live** (8798, scratch state dir, test contacts ALPHA/BRAVO/CHARLIE/DELTA): the first batch nearest first, DELTA (0.3 nm, acquired later) last; at 1.5 nm five real contacts struck in place, "16 vessels in 1.5 nm · 5 out of range"; CHARLIE (test, 2.0 nm, live) struck with her CPA; x on her removed and armed her, widening to 3 nm brought her back at the bottom; NEVER ON SUNDAY dragged to the top (same node, drop line shown, saved); the panel at 260 px scrolled to 120 held through a poll; a reload kept the order; a reload at 1.5 nm (no memory) struck six rows from `beyond` alone, the poll carrying `&held=` with ten keys.
**Verified** (hand-run; the hook NOT run, nor tests/precommit_hook.py): ais_table 50, ais_avoid 156, clearance_guard 82, guard_resume 54, survey_order 13, page_strict 4, page_log_posts 5, storage_banner 9, target_cpa 24, ui_split 26, ui_split_peers, ui_tooltips 12; ais_range 28, completion_modes, env_water 12, estop_chain 20, http_contract 27, live_speed 11, storage_watch 13; docs_valid 8, sanitization 4, spelling 6. Only the operations and technical manuals rebuilt; their new text read back with python-docx.
**2026-10-13: OUT OF RANGE IS DELETED, NOT STRUCK** (Andy: "for the AIS card delete the out of range vessels instead of the red line solution"). Built on its own branch `fix/ais-out-of-range` in worktree `D:\Claude\ASV-ais` (rebased onto `c301f98`; the two manuals rebuilt from the merged builders; merged into fix/criticals and master), because two other sessions were editing static/asv.html in ASV-fix at the time. `aisListUpdate` now drops from `order` every contact whose report puts her beyond the range - live from beyond it (a test contact), held on a last report beyond it, or reported in the server's `beyond` - and she is acquired again AT THE BOTTOM the next time she reports in range (her place is gone, as the x's is). Deleted only on a REPORT, never on absence (a failed poll arrives empty). The deletion is not put in `removed`: a contact not in `order` is a newcomer when she next reports in range, which is exactly that. Rows are {k, r, state} with state live / lost only; the `beyond` field, the "out" state, `AIS_OUT_LINE` and its stripe, the headline's "out of range" count and the tip's OUT OF RANGE text are gone. `held`/`beyond` stay: they are what deletes one that sails out. ais_table 50 (6b/6c/6i-6l/21b/22/22b rewritten; the shipped page fails all eight; 12/12 sidecar mutations killed; the old "x arms her on reporting only" mutation is now EQUIVALENT - no row out of range to press x on - noted in the suite). Live on scratch 8803 (`asv-ais-del`, dead `--ais`, own state): ALPHA/BRAVO/CHARLIE at 1/2/3 nm; 1.5 nm left ALPHA only ("1 vessel in 1.5 nm", saved order trimmed); DELTA at 0.5 nm joined below ALPHA; 5 nm again -> ALPHA, DELTA, BRAVO, CHARLIE. Verified by hand on the rebased tree: ais_table 50, ais_avoid 159, page_strict 4, ui_tooltips 12, panel_drag 42, ais_range 28, docs_valid 8, spelling 6, sanitization 4; operations + technical manuals rebuilt and read back.
**OPEN.** (a) PRE-EXISTING, not touched: after a page reload `#aisRange` shows its authored 5 while the server's range persists (seen on 8798: field 5, headline 1.5 nm) - setAisRange writes the field only after the operator's own change. (b) His old stored sort no longer applies on an update, by design: a header click now sorts once.

### THE ARRIVAL: SHE COMES IN SLOW (Andy, 2026-10-08: "AS the ASV approaches end of RTH or GOTO, it hits the final waypoint at full ordered speed. AS these home points may be close in to a dock or ship or whatever it would be best to slow gradually on approach until it is at or near dead stop prior to triggering the loiter command or whatever the next command may be", then, offered the coast or staying in gear at 4 kn: "build it with the coast")
**Why.** Every Go-To and RTH in his sessions 20261007-215805, 20261008-082101 and 20261008-083605 went out with `coast_from_m` null: through coast.js solveCoast (scratchpad `nwps/why_no_coast.cjs`, the logged route, set and speed) each was refused "the release range (74-150 m) is longer than the final leg (28-56 m)" - the drift-in armed on the LAST LEG only, and a laned route is ~60 m legs. So she flew the last leg at 14 kn, flipped to station-keeping at the waypoint and only then shed way, carrying past it (coast.js's own note: 33.1 m at 14 kn, calm).
**The fix - four pieces, all existing machinery.** (1) THE LEAD (static/asv.html leadFor): a Go-To, RTH or transit (`S.behavior`) has one slower "leg", its END - idx route.length, `arrival: true` - at the hold role's speed (roleSpeed("hold"), the slowest that makes way: LOW 4 kn in calm), starting where the drift-in releases (`st.coast_from_m`, the range the vessel publishes armed) or at the hold point with none (`coast: false`); leadWant/slowLeadM do the rest (14 -> 4 kn in gear: 74 m, 20 s; lead 81 m calm with the 1 s latency). Readouts: the RUN "for" row and the command bar say "before the drift-in" / "before the hold point". (2) THE SOLVE (solveCoastFor): the route left from her position (`path`), v0 = the arrival speed on a law hull when `routeM - groundM >= slowLeadM(vHigh -> arrival)` (`slowTo`); else from max(transit, sog) as before; a REFUSED solve from the arrival speed returns null (NOT a 14 kn solve - that would release her ~100 m out at LOW). coast.js solveCoast takes `path` (release laid back along it, chord heading for the set, walked along it; with no path the old hdg/legM answer byte for byte); coastWorthIt is `groundM > COAST_MIN_M` (5) - the hold disc no longer decides. Intent card: arrivalSay (its own function so end_action's world can stub it). doTransit and the resume path send coast_from_m for a transit too. (3) THE SIM (asv_console.py): the latch is `_route_left_m(dist_b, cap) <= _coast_from_m` on any leg; the status frame publishes `coast_from_m` (None once spent or disarmed); Engine.transit + /api/cmd/transit carry coast_from_m. (4) TWO LATENT COAST FAULTS, found driving it: the spent-coast cap (COAST_END_KN, 1 kn) applied during the HOLD - she could not hold station in a set over a knot (now `not self._holding`); and on the approach it sat below a head set - 2 kn on the nose, coast spent short, she was set back to 260 m from the berth within 10 min, never holding (now max(1 kn, head set + HOLD_MAKES_WAY_KN)). Also the mission card's "to end" read "arrived" whenever drifting - now "N m · drifting in".
**Designs not taken.** Coasting from 14 kn along the route (no in-gear phase): 98-150 m and up to 68 s+ of prop-out, refused by COAST_MAX_S in a following set. Arrival for uploaded SURVEY plans: not built - slowing in gear and coasting would start inside the last line's coverage (~95 m from 7 kn), and Engine.upload carries no coast; a plan ending in RTH gets the arrival at home.
**Measured / tested.** coast.js 8e-8h, 8g2 (the release and the walk round a bend; refused only longer than the route left; straight route = the old answer), 12 (worth-it rule), 29-32 (the page's solve in a world of the real coast.js: from LOW 51.9 m on a 600 m route; 120 m route -> from 14 kn 97.9 m; a beam-set pier only the 4 kn overshoot walk reaches -> null; no-law hull -> 14 kn). coast_sim 16-16c (a bend: released 49.5 m along the route, 41.1 m straight; armed 50.0 published, None after; 1.37 kn at the hold vs 4 kn powered), 17 (2 kn following set: held within 2.8 m after the coast, no routed re-approach), 17b (2 kn head set: arrives and holds at 296 s), 18 (no coast: nothing armed), 7c (transit over the wire, state publishes 42.0). corner_slow 19p (LOW first 130.0 m before the end with 50 m armed: 50 + 81.2), 19q (80.0 m with none), 19r (no law: HIGH to the end); 19i reworded. Mutations (scratchpad `nwps/mutate_arrival.py`, scratch copies, worktree hashed unchanged): 14 of 14 killed, each by its own check (the chord-walk survivor became 8g2). hold_point 9b/9d extended to the transit; end_action stubs arrivalSay.
**Verified** (hand-run; the hook NOT run, nor tests/precommit_hook.py or tests/ais_range.py): every other suite, 112 of 112 (74 node, 38 Python); the ten that read the documents or their builders, 10 of 10 on the final build. LIVE on a throwaway console (8797, DriX, New Castle, slack water, transit at 7 kn, its own state dir and ports file, no AIS service): a ~600 m Go-To went out with a 50.6 m drift-in solved from LOW; LOW was commanded 95.6 m left along the route (50.6 + 46.3 expected), the prop stopped 49.9 m out at 3.8 kn, and the hold began 5.2 m from the point at 1.02 kn (the RUN row read "SLOWING to low 33 m before the drift-in", the card "DRIFT ... 42 m from plan end" and "TO END 42 m · drifting in"); the RTH it chained (the fresh mission ends in RTH) the same - LOW 98.8 m left, prop stopped 53.0 m out at 3.9 kn, the hold begun at 1.13 kn 5.8 m off and 2.0 m off at 0.15 kn 17 s later. His tree, mission.json and ports.json untouched. Documents: technical manual (coast.js, coast_sim.py, corner_slow.js entries), operations manual ("SHE COMES IN SLOW"), README; Word only. **Known, not changed:** the drift-in is solved with the set at COMMAND time (the coast's old limitation); a page that is not supervising leads nothing, so she reaches the release faster than solved (from 14 kn over ~52 m she still sheds to ~3.4 kn); the arrival speed key is asked live (roleSpeed("hold")) while the coast was solved from the command-time one.

### THE REACH LANE'S GRAZE HELD WHERE IT IS (Andy, 2026-10-08: "the ASV shies away from Pierce and Goat islands and violates the stay-right protocol. Why is this happening? Can it be adjusted in the basic settings or is there a basic coding issue?")
**Why.** His RTH of 09:19 (Adams Point to New Castle, "Aids & hazards" on, buffer 5, floor 5.0 m, a 2.36 kn set at 200 deg, standoff 26.78 m) rode the Seavey Island side past Henderson Point outbound. Replayed through the page's own modules on the extract read before the plan (scratchpad `nwps/replay_plan.cjs` with `rthT_cfg_haz.json`; the set from the state frame): the buoyed reach lane was laid and then DROPPED for the whole route by channelLaneRoute's `grazes` test - one dock (a shore-construction line at 43.07904,-70.75303, the foot of the Memorial Bridge) passed 24.2 m off by the laned route and 29.7 m by the route without it, the floor 33.8 m (the set's standoff + 7). No setting moved it: a 2.9 m floor for his 5.0, or a 7 kn transit, and it was still dropped; only with no set at all did it stand.
**The fix (static/js/routing.js).** channelLaneRoute's veto is split into `judge` (ok / `other` / `grazed`) and a loop: a lane that fails ONLY the graze test is laid again by `layReach(hold)` with the grazed hazards as buoyedReachLane's `opts.hold` [{f, r}], up to REACH_HOLD_ROUNDS (3); a round with nothing new to hold ends them; still grazing, or any other failure (worseFor, abandoned, crossed, newLaneTurn - never answered locally), drops it whole as before. In buoyedReachLane, after the `owned` cap: per held hazard, cap 0 at every sample where clearance < r + min(cap, T); `close()` eases the lane down to it and back up at LANE_SLEW. The route without the lane is finished once (`plainOf`) for every judging.
**Designs tried and dropped** (the RTH replay and 91b's river): a MEASURED hold (each sample's starboard ray stepped out to the floor) cleared the RTH only once spread over KH and extended to T-0 samples, and never cleared 91b's bridge support - the smoothing cuts the dip's corner where every sample is 9 m or more off; measured-first then hard gained only 19 m of starboard over 300 m below the bridge. Growing the floor each round did nothing (her path already inside it). A zone sized by the lane's largest shift anywhere instead of the sample's own T moved the RTH by 7.4 m at most and 91b not at all.
**Measured** (the 09:19 RTH replay, shipped vs this): the lane kept, 14 marks kept, 0 wrong; up to 110.7 m to starboard past Pierce Island and Henderson Point (Henderson Point Light 10 passed ~100 m off instead of ~50), up to 186.8 m in Little Bay; the dock 27.6 m off (the route without the lane 30.2 - inside the 3 m slack); 9.982 -> 10.072 nm; the replay's plan 4.8 -> 6.5 s (one more laying and judging). 91b's river: the lane kept in all five support placements (the shipped code: three), on its line from n -500 to 250 and from 2750 on.
**Tests.** enc_channel 91c - 91b's five placements against the same river with no support: the lane kept, the support at the floor or more, |de| < 1 m at n 0 and n 2750, REACH_HOLD_ROUNDS pinned. It fails on the shipped routing.js and on 5 of 5 mutants (the hold a no-op; no rounds; the zone r only; rounds that hold nothing; the hold zeroing the whole lane), each time 91c alone (scratchpad `nwps/mutate_hold.py`, scratch copies only). rule9_scope 8's source pin follows `finish` into `judge`; buoy_lane's eval list carries REACH_HOLD_ROUNDS.
**Verified** (hand-run; the hook NOT run, nor tests/precommit_hook.py or tests/ais_range.py): all 74 node suites, 74 of 74 (the 21 that read routing.js among them), and the ten that read the documents or their builders, 10 of 10 (docs_valid, spelling, sanitization among them); no live console - a pure function of routing.js, replayed through the page's own modules on his chart instead. Documents: the technical manual (the reach lane's veto paragraph, enc_channel's entry) and README; Word only. **Known, not changed:** a sample with no cross-section (T 0) is not held itself - layLine carries the lane across it at its neighbors' shift; should that graze, the judging sees it again and drops the lane, as before.

### THE BEND CUT AND THE SHIP AT HER BERTH (Andy, 2026-10-07: "build Solution 1 in the worktree, and Solution 2 as well")
**Why.** His RTH of 19:33 outbound past the Newington pier (session 20261007-165907, "Aids & hazards" off) left the charted channel for 525 m and passed NORD LOGOS - 132 m, moored at the pier - 79 m off her AIS fix at 10.3 kn, perhaps 20-30 m off her stern. Replayed through the page's own modules on the extract read 8 s before the plan (scratchpad `nwps/replay_plan.cjs`, `rth_*.cjs`): within 0.4 m across the swerve once the plan-time set was in (1.87 kn - the state frame carries it, the telemetry record does not). The search's shortest path cuts the inside of the bend past the pier; the chart's lane should have taken that bend cut back, and took it only at a standoff of 21.4 m or less - his set's 21.74 m flipped it, 173 m of route for 1.1 m of standoff.
**Solution 1 (static/js/routing.js chartOwnership's bend cut).** The cut began only right after a MEASURED sample, and the path stepped out over ONE sample inside the channel that the along test declined ('in'), so it was never bridged; and every sample in a cut was asked the along test, which no bend cut passes (the first sample out had the channel 31-259 m to port). Now the bounding measured samples may lie past up to CHART_TAN_M of declined water at either end (left 'in' for the carry), and a cut's samples need only `chord` within CHART_BRIDGE_REACH_M over open water. Measured: his RTH 1,043 -> 440 m outside the channel, keep-out clearance 27.4 -> 28.8 m; his inbound Go-To 448 -> 453 m (27 waypoints moved up to 47 m, inside the channel); the 13:51 Go-To identical; 0 marks wrong everywhere; the swerve gone at every standoff 20.6-25 m. **Test:** enc_channel 11b - the charted rings round that bend (7 dredged, 3 fairway) and the path the marks stage handed the chart's lane, inline, meters about her fix: 0 of 35 samples dropped; the code before it 16; either half alone 16. (A synthetic 40 degree bend was bridged by the old code too - no teeth - so the real geometry it is.)
**Solution 2 (moored ships in a passage's model).** ais_keepout.js `aisMooredKeepouts`: every contact `aisMotion` calls not under way, as the guard models her (unswept hull, or the disc), anywhere in the chart box - not AIS_KO_RANGE_M - a stale or absent read none, with its reason. passage.js `passageKo` folds them into a COPY of nogo.ko for planNogoRoute (and its holdTarget) and routePlan's TRANSIT legs only (`kL = transit ? koT : ko` - a pattern's lines and hops untouched, his 2026-09-25 rule); `mooredPassed` names those the route passes within MOORED_SAY_M (250 m) as `plan.moored`. The page's `readPassageAis` (in planInsideChart, before aisKeepoutsNow) reads /api/ais along the plan's own legs - the proxy answers within its display radius of ONE center, so centers 1.5 radii apart, PASSAGE_AIS_MAX_READS 8, PASSAGE_AIS_TIMEOUT_MS each, merged by MMSI, one read on a lake - into `nogo.ais`; a failed read leaves it null and the plan is the chart's alone. `mooredNote` puts "clear of X (L x B m, moored) (AIS)" on the Go-To / RTH / Transit banners. ais_keepout.js's header rule ("never the planner's model") now says: never a contact UNDER WAY. Measured on his RTH with the six contacts his console held: NORD LOGOS's hull 53 -> 145 m with Solution 2 alone (the route still out of the channel - Solution 1's job), 145 m with both and in the channel. **Tests:** ais_keepout M1-M8 (the model; the read's age; Go-To/RTH laid round at the standoff and named; nogo.ko untouched; under way not; stale not; a transit laid round; a survey line flown as drawn) - 6 of 6 mutants each killed by its own check; chart_box 10 (the read along 18 km, merged, capped, a lake, a dead proxy) - 5 of 5; the stub worlds of command_result.js and pause_resume.js given the read (a stand-in that reads nothing) and mooredNote; survey_order 8's source pin follows `kL`. **LIVE** on a throwaway 8797 (`--state-dir`, `--no-stream-predictions`, its own ports copy): a 60 x 12 m moored test contact across a 1 km RTH's route - the page read the live proxy, routed round her 18.1 m off her hull (the standoff there 10.3 m: transit at survey speed), and the banner said "clear of CG47273 (14 x 4 m, stopped) and MOORED-1 (60 x 12 m, stopped) (AIS)" - CG47273 a real Coast Guard boat from the live feed.

### ⚠⚠ THE STREAM IN THE SIMULATOR, FUSED (Andy, 2026-10-07: "move forward with implementation as you suggest. The bottom line goal is to simulate wind/wave/current effects on the passage of a given ASV through the water.")
**Why.** His Little Bay session (2026-10-06) ran with NO stream: the New Castle port's model, gomofs, publishes 3-hourly frames this build cannot read - 1,966 of the session's readings say so - so the 0.15-0.88 kn "set" was wind leeway alone, while NOAA predicted 3.8 kn of flood (07:49) and 4.0 kn of ebb (14:07) at the General Sullivan Bridge. Measured the next day (scripts in the session scratchpad `nwps/`): gomofs has NO water cells from the Memorial Bridge to Furber Strait and read 0.10 kn against a predicted 1.43 at the harbor entrance, so no reader fix would ever have filled the Piscataqua; NOAA's current-prediction stations cover his busiest water densely (26 locations within 25 km of New Castle, 18 of Portland, 16 of Lewes, 15 of Bellingham). The review he asked for first (water.noaa.gov, tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov, oceanservice.noaa.gov, Delft-FEWS) is in the chat of 2026-10-07; its bottom line: the station predictions add the most, water.noaa.gov's river flow adds ~0.01 kn in tidal water (the Lamprey's 10-day peak through a nominal 2,500 m2 Dover Point section), Delft-FEWS is the NWS river centers' forecasting framework (its US output IS water.noaa.gov's official forecasts), and the S-111 / RTOFS feeds are HDF5 (no stdlib reader).
**What (stream_fusion.py, CurrentsMonitor in asv_console.py).** (1) NOAA's tidal current PREDICTIONS (CO-OPS) for every station within 25 km, at each location's SHALLOWEST bin, weak-and-variable stations out, a week ahead in `charts/coops_currents/` (a shared cache, like the chart's), refetched when a table reaches under two days ahead; a SUBORDINATE station answers only its events (max / slack) - interpolated in the tide's shape (slack to strength a quarter sine, strength to slack a quarter cosine, strength to strength a half cosine), measured 3-6x closer to the full 6-minute series than linear (RMS 0.24-0.29 kn against 0.69-0.88 at four Piscataqua stations, 0.06 against 0.37 at Cape Henlopen). Between stations inverse distance squared, nearest 3, out to 3 km. (2) A gridded model: the OFS the port names, or a PacIOOS ROMS window served by ERDDAP (Oahu South Shore for Honolulu, Samoa for Pago Pago, the main Hawaiian Islands, the western North Pacific - each verified by its /info record and a point query; Samoa's inner harbor is land at its resolution). Where stations lie in it, the model is CALIBRATED per station - the lag (+-90 min) and gain that fit it along the station's axis, kept only at r >= 0.6 and gain 0.4-2.5 (measured at Lewes: dbofs 30 % weak at the bay mouth, error 0.47 -> 0.29 kn after the gain) - and the calibration at a position is the inverse-distance-squared mix of the stations within 15 km. (3) The blend: exp(-d / 1 km) on the distance to the nearest station. None, never zero, where nothing has a value. The station tables and the PacIOOS window live on `StreamSources`' OWN thread (a station fetch is ~7 s, a PacIOOS window up to 25 s); readers take immutable references. `CurrentsMonitor.field_at` is the answer at any position; **SimVcu.tick now asks it at her own position every tick** (it read the minute's single reading at the boat); `_sample` is the minute's reading, field for field the OFS reading where no other layer reaches (13), and carries `stations`, `model`, `w_stations`, `sources`, and `model_note` - the model's reason on a GOOD reading, kept out of `note`, which the page reads as the projection warning (16). The page's Current row tooltip names the basis (`currentBasisTxt`). Live on the throwaway (8797): within a minute of spawning at New Castle the readout read NOAA predictions from Fort Point (323 m, 69 %) and two more stations, the simulator's set following it (plus leeway); no server errors.
**⚠⚠ WHAT THE FIRST FULL RUN CAUGHT (108 of 112), AND THE TWO RULES IT ADDED.** (1) `state_dir` and `build_id` start a console from a COPY of the program and copied its modules from a HAND-KEPT LIST without `stream_fusion.py`: the copied console died at import, `state_dir` waited out its start loop against a dead port to the runner's 600 s limit. `stream_fusion.py` is now in `BUILD_PY` (the build fingerprint missed it too: a change to it would not have read as a new build), and both suites READ `BUILD_PY` from the server's source rather than restate it. Both holds were the guard's projection steering the model boat back toward a waypoint ASTERN:
- **10:25:04**, 13.6 kn on waypoint 130 of a 236-point Go-To, the route dead straight there: she was 0.6 m PAST waypoint 130 (inside the 1 m approach radius) and the vessel's index - carried in every 4 Hz state frame, advanced by its own two tests once a tick, so a frame can show her up to 1.8 m past the waypoint it still names - still named it. `projectRoute` asked those tests only AFTER its first step, measured from HER OWN position (its `prev` began as `p`), so after its 3.5 m first step (4.1 m past) the along-track read negative, `turnToward` swung the bow back toward the waypoint, the loop entered the rock's disc in 5 s: a hold with 30.4 m of clearance at the hold ("HOLD 21.4 m off a keep-out · entry in 5 s" is the bar 3.7 s later, as she ran on). With index 129 the same frame reads EDGE (2.5 m to starboard), with 131 CLEAR. The replay reproduces it to the second on three model variants.

**The fix (`static/js/guard.js` projectRoute, `static/asv.html` guardTrack; and from the review round the same evening routeCmd / legStart / spliceAt on the page, SimVcu.amend_plan / Engine.amend on the server).** (1) Before the first step `projectRoute` consumes every leading target the vessel's own rule already counts as reached - `hypot(tg - p) <= approach || along >= segLen - approach`, along measured from `opts.prev`, where the leg began (without it her own position stands in, so only a target inside the approach radius is read as reached) - and the walk begins toward the first target she has NOT reached; a route every waypoint of which is reached ends CLEAR (the motion is over; hold.js certifies the point; a boat already INSIDE a hazard there is t = 0, as everywhere). (2) `guardTrack` projects no route whose length is not the state frame's `wp_total` (`S.wp_total != null && S.wp_total !== runRoute.length -> null`): an index that does not count into the route the page holds is another plan's; a frame with no `wp_total` (an older console) projects as before. (3) THE REVIEW ROUND, three fixes. `guardTrack` projects no route while a Go-To / RTH / transit / re-approach POST is in flight (`routeCmd` counts it from send to reply; the frame answering it is the new plan's whatever its length - the length alone could not see two plans of the same length in the 80 ms swap window, LT-2; the straight projection stands in). The leg's start handed as `prev` is the VESSEL's `_seg_start`: runRoute[idx-1] once she has advanced onto a leg, but HER POSITION at a start and at every amend, which `legStartsHere` records from the command's reply and `trackLegStart` (onState, every frame) keeps until the index moves - SR-1 at index 0, and SR-2: a Pause/Resume's backtrack point lies astern between runRoute[idx-1] and her, read as passed from that waypoint, so the look-ahead ran up the line while she turned to run 12 lengths down it, a false hold on anything beyond the pause mark and a miss on the reversal (new in the first commit; the shipped prev = p happened to coincide with the vessel's at an amend). And an amendment is spliced where the VESSEL spliced it: `SimVcu.amend_plan` returns the index it spliced at (its LIVE index - one later than the page's whenever she advanced a waypoint between the frame the page planned at and the landing), `Engine.amend` sets `wp_total` from it in the reply and drops the frame read across the command (`_commanded()`, so no frame carries the old count - LT-4), and the page's `spliceAt` takes the reply's count less the tail at all four amend sites (the edge rung, resumeRun, resumeFromHere, the way round) - before, the drawn route was one shorter than the plan aboard for the rest of the motion and the length gate left the guard with no route (LT-1). Both live frames read CLEAR on the fixed tree and reproduce on the shipped one (`replay_hold.cjs --root D:/Claude/ASV-fix`).

**Fixed in the code (3):** LT-2 the equal-length race (`routeCmd` / `routeCmdsInFlight`; clearance_guard 19c, 19f); SR-2 with SR-1 the page's leg start against the vessel's `_seg_start` (`legStart` / `legStartsHere` / `trackLegStart`; 19d, 19e); LT-1 with LT-4 the amend splice at the vessel's index and the plan's count in the reply (SimVcu.amend_plan returns its index, Engine.amend sets `wp_total` and calls `_commanded()`, `spliceAt` at the four amend sites; 19g, amend_plan 10b).
**Fixed in the tests (3 gaps, 5 wordings):** T1 the length gate's shorter direction (19b); T2 the leg start on the second leg (19); T3 the already-inside check's order (28c's pile). T5-T9: the 4.5 s / 5 s pair said as two measurements, 28b's claim narrowed to what it observes, "short of" -> "past", a teeth note beside the block (the header table is the original sweep's record, the suite's convention since), the four near-equivalents N6 / N8 / N9 / N12 recorded there.
**Fixed in the words (every number re-measured by a refuter from the recording):** W1 80 m astern, not 130; W2 and LT-6 the index arrives in every 4 Hz frame - the once-a-second was the RECORDER's cap - so the skew is 1.8 m, not 7; W3 two rocks 46 m apart, the 10:32 route 5.9 m off its own; W4 the RTH slow-down 2.3 km away off a third rock, not "the same water"; W5 a 28 degree bend and a 51 degree overshoot over four seconds, not 50 degrees in two; W6 the 10:32 cause chain (an earlier press's chart read, two targets 60 m apart); W7 the old route from index 1 read EDGE, not clear; W8 and T4 8 of 9 mutants with one equivalent, not 9 of 9; W9 and T7 0.6 m PAST the waypoint, not short of it; W10 the 21.4 m bar was logged 3.7 s after the hold (30.4 m at the hold); W11 the entry point 2.3 m short of the disc's edge, inside the buffer, not inside the disc; W12 the 24.7 m notes were stand-downs three minutes on, the release read 32.2 m; W13 no line numbers in the handoff; W14 and LT-3 the "lengths agree" claim narrowed - three states where the straight projection stood in for a whole run (a blocked transit or Upload drawn over a running plan, an RTH to a moving home's one-point plan, the amend race - the last now closed; the first two project the straight line where the shipped page projected the WRONG route, and the Intent card says why); W15 4.5 s; W16 CANCELED.
**Refuted (4):** LT-5 (the real link is inert in Phase 0 on both trees; a Phase-1 codec suite should pin wp_total == len(route)), SR-3 (turnFlyable's chain is thinned at the approach radius first, so the start loop cannot fire there), SR-4 (the end-of-route reading is the shipped design: past the last waypoint the hold point's water is hold.js's), SR-5 (the sub-1 m degenerate leg: pre-existing, and the frame it needs exists only above 22 kn).
**OPEN - his call:** the amend protocol's stale-index seam. When an amend lands a tick late the vessel's own splice puts the via in front of the waypoint she has just passed (plan ... P2, VIA, P2 ...), so she flies to the via and BACK to P2. The page now mirrors that plan exactly, so the guard sees what she will fly; the cure is a protocol change - the amend carries the vias and the index they were planned at, and the vessel splices at its live index dropping the points she has passed - proposed as its own round.
**NOTED:** cache_writes 1's bound (fewer than 60 replaces refused while a reader loops on the file) trips under a parallel suite run - 70 with three suites at once, 9-11 alone. The hook runs suites one at a time, so it does not bite a commit; a parallel runner of mine must not read its failure as the change's.
**Lessons:** five numbers in the first handoff were wrong because they were written from memory of the replay rather than re-read from it - a number in a handoff comes from the command that printed it, or it is not written; a resumed workflow re-runs every agent after the first call whose ORDER changed (a pipeline's second stage runs in completion order), so a resume is a second pass of refuters, not a cache hit - plan for it or stop the run; "a FIX to a value must reach every PRODUCER" again - the splice index had four writers and the leg start three, and a name added inside a lifted function (`spliced`, `routeCmd`, `legStartsHere`, `spliceAt`) is a new dependency of every eval world that lifts it (six worlds this round), and a `const at` inside the edge rung's reply callback shadowed the rung's own `at` - renamed before it bit.

### ⚠⚠ THE BUOYED REACH AND BUOY TO BUOY (Andy, 2026-10-04, with a screenshot at New Castle, DriX H-8, buffer 5, floor 3: "through this section along Seavey Island, the ASV moves to the far side of the channel both outbound and inbound ... lets fix this issue without breaking the excellent path planning we now have"; then, of Fox Point: "The red buoy N4 seems to have been ignored. The ASV should have routed to the left of it so that its on the right as the ASV passes"; then "both these fixes are specific to this mission area. Can the solutions be generalized to be more universally applied" - yes: both are general rules; and, on the review, of the rock it left on her path's side: "hold the lane and pass the rock wide ... treat it as land that may be avoided to either side", "maybe treat a rock as sea bottom - a shallow point to be avoided", "model either way for testing purposes")

**The two defects.** (1) Past Seavey Island the river is marked by single marks, its starboard-hand marks BEACONS on the shore (Henderson Point Light 10, Seavey Island Daybeacons 12A/12B). markPassRoute keeps each mark on its proper hand and no more - a mark kept to port gets a berth, a beacon on the starboard hand is never brought close - so nothing put her on the starboard side of the water: bound up she rounded green buoys 11 and 13 thirty meters off on the PORT edge, bound down she cut the inside of Henderson Point. (No deliberate reason; the real constraint there is the Naval Shipyard's charted restricted area along Seavey Island, 33 CFR 334.50, which the old outbound route ran 100 m into.) (2) The Rocks Buoy 4 at the 5 m buffer: the run round Fox Point Rock Buoy 3 was laid along the SEARCH's track (due south, across The Rocks), the east side of buoy 4 was then a 51 degree join, the pass was refused and the red counted on her wrong hand.

**What it is now.**
- **`buoyedReachLane`** (routing.js), run AFTER the chart's lane on its path (`owns`: in chart water no further than that lane's slack). A reach is the stretch between two marks no more than MARK_NEIGHBOR_M apart, one hand read. She rides three quarters across the water the marks buoy, ONLY EVER TO STARBOARD. Edges: the bank (a ray per sample to REACH_EDGE_M 600 at clr, PLUS `obs` - every keep-out corner, charted line vertex, point hazard less its extent and local restricted-area corner on her starboard hand, read at the samples either side of it - the bank's: rocks are left out, below), side water by the WATER's WIDTH against its window median; a LOCAL charted restricted area (<= RESTRICTED_LOCAL_M2, 1 km2, judged over the whole of a named area cut at cell seams) wherever she is outside it (`within`; inside one she is moved only toward its nearer edge, `deeper`); that hand's marks (the line between two where the water's course runs straight, REACH_STRAIGHT_COS 10 deg; the line through a mark along the water's course out to the next mark of either hand, REACH_RUN_COS 20 deg). A cross-section needs the TYPICAL edges within REACH_MAX_WIDTH_M (an obstruction in wide water is no edge) and a stretch of at least REACH_MIN_M 150 m (T capped at LANE_SLEW x its length); a port-hand mark to starboard of her gives none. THE CONE: every lateral mark on her starboard hand (hand read or not; D for a buoy kept to starboard, BEACON otherwise), the half-plane cap, HOLD round a placed starboard run's pass points, the `bare` hold, every one-sample limit held flat over KH samples; the hold past a stretch's end asks `room` (incl. obs) a smoothing step either side at the EASED value.
- **channelLaneRoute `finish`** runs smoothing/gate/prune on the lane's path and on the path without it (`plain`); ships `plain` where the lane's route has a mark wrong that plain has right (mark by mark), was abandoned where plain was not, has an UNCOUNTED mark (no number, junction) between the two routes, a turn over 45 deg plain has nothing as sharp within NEW_TURN_NEAR_M 30 m of (`newLaneTurn`, exported), or passes a keep-out nearer than the lane's floor (clr + STANDOFF) and by more than min(buf, 3) m nearer than plain (`grazes`: the smoothing cuts the V the lane makes round a rock). Otherwise hands back `withoutReach`; `reachLaid` says the lane was laid, kept or not.
- **passage.js `keepStandoff`** (now exported) re-gates `withoutReach` too in a set and ships it (how.reach false) where the laned route is worse there - the re-gate's splices have no notion of a side (seed 4154: a green 15.5 m on her wrong hand).
- **markPassRoute: BUOY TO BUOY.** Where a mark is on its WRONG hand only for want of a join, the pass before it (then after) and its own are laid again aimed at each other - only where that line runs along her route (MARK_ALONG_COS; two marks abeam across the channel are a gate). A NO_JOIN refusal is asked again when the count placed changes, until a round places nothing (MARK_STAGE_ROUNDS 8), within the leg budget.
- **keepouts.js** carries `restricted: [{ring, bb, area, ringArea, name}]` as FACTS whatever the area toggle says (pieces of one named area joined across cell seams). passage.js/asv.html say "right of center in the buoyed channel" (banner, Intent row; a drawn transit merges it over its legs).
- **A ROCK IS A SHALLOW POINT, NOT AN EDGE** (his call on the review, 2026-10-05: "hold the lane and pass the rock wide. do not use a rock as an assumed buoy for path planning purposes. treat it as land that may be avoided to either side", then "maybe treat a rock as sea bottom - a shallow point to be avoided", then "model either way for testing purposes"). In buoyedReachLane a ROCK is a keep-out <= ROCK_MAX_M 150 m across of a NATURAL kind (`natural`: 'a charted hazard', 'land', 'the shoreline', 'water shallower than ...') AND, where it carries a chart class (keepouts.js now copies `cls` onto every keep-out), a class in ROCK_CLASSES (Underwater_Awash_Rock, Obstruction, Wreck, Land_Area, Coastline, Depth_Area): a pile, a dolphin, a pylon, a hulk, a shore construction, every aid charted as a hazard point (cardinal, isolated-danger, safe-water, special-purpose buoys and beacons), anything built and any kind not named is the bank however small. A cluster is items closer than 2 x FLOOR, and "water all round" is 2 x FLOOR to every other keep-out - BOTH measured OUTLINE TO OUTLINE (`gapTo`; the bounding circle read a 100 m shoal with 40 m of water to the bank as the bank) - and no lateral mark within ROCK_MARKED_M 50 m (a hazard a mark stands beside is the edge it marks). Rocks are left out of the lane's banks (`koWall`), the hold past a stretch's end and the last-point shrink (`koKeep`); after the line is laid, a rock the route brings nearer than FLOOR - asked of the line AND of the route as `smoothTrack` will round it (the smoothing passed rocks 0.2-3.9 m off at bends and knees) - and nearer than her path was, is passed on the SMALLER MOVE (width from its outline) by MOVING THE LANE'S OWN LINE (the gap round, 2026-10-06: capped flat at the rock's offset from her path, a rock on the lane's line short of a charted fairway - where the chart's lane eases her path across the river on a diagonal - held the lane 61-73 m toward her path for hundreds of meters): far side T raised over the window by `upBy` (the most any ABEAM sample needs) and the abeam samples to `hiAt` (inside a reach, within cap); near side cap lowered over the window by `downBy`, measured to the rock's limit even PAST her path (clamped at her path, the abeam samples sat on it after one round and the widening never lowered the approach again - the lane lost at a rock 125 m short of the fairway, 93w), and the abeam samples to `loAt`; `win` = its length + FLOOR + 2 x HOLD + STEP, `abeam` = within its length + STEP/2, each sample reading the rock across its OWN cross-section. A near-side rock her own path passes inside its floor: the rounds stop on her path (no nearer than it), but `finish` compares with the route without the lane - gated and smoothed, wider - and dropped the whole lane (four rocks of the fairway sweep), so such a rock is RIDDEN ON HER PATH over its whole window, once (`onPath`; 93x - what the old flat cap did for it). A far pass another rock's near cap made impossible gives way to near (two rocks either side of the line lost the whole lane, 29 of 32 pairs); a pass the smoothing still cuts into is widened by the cut; up to ROCK_ROUNDS 12 (8 lost the lane on 93n's seven-rock run once the line was moved). FLOOR is the model's: opts.rockModel from passage.js's wrapper (V.REACH_ROCK, state.js, 'land' by default), set by the survey card's **Channel rocks** select under Turn shape (Land / Shoal; not saved with the mission; changes no keep-out, rebuilds nothing): 'land' = clr + STANDOFF; 'bottom' = clr + MS (at bare clr the smoothing and the gate made a 31 deg jog round a rock on the line). `finish`'s `grazes` judges a rock at reach.rockFloor. The Channel rocks floor is THIS lane's only: the chart's lane, the pair lane and the banks' lane pass a rock at the ordinary keep-clear in either model (the banks' lane even reads one a ray passes within the buffer of as its edge - pre-existing; HIS CALL, 2026-10-06: "keep the rock rule to single marks only", pinned by 93y - Land and Shoal the same route in a cut, a fairway, a fairway with pairs and a pair channel, and not in the single-marks lane; it fails on Channel rocks let into the pair, banks' or chart lane, and for the pair and chart lanes it is the only check that does). Checks 93-93y (75c, 80, 80b, 80d re-specified; 80e-80g and 91b ask the bank's rules of built things, because every isolated hazard in 80, 80b, 80c, 80d and 91 became a rock and five bank rules lost every check - G2, G4, G4b, G18, R2b lived until then). The transit/RTH estimate is keyed on V.REACH_ROCK (appended AFTER the array's join - chart_box.js 7d reads the key's source).

**The review, and what it changed.** ROUND 1, four lenses (workflow wf_6e6f6d5d-d49; the pipeline lens and every refuter died on a usage limit, so each finding was re-run by hand before it was fixed): 25 findings, all reproduced, all fixed, each with a check that fails on the reviewed code (79-89): a one-sample notch cut by the smoothing (72c's own pier shipped 3.5 m off - I had told Andy "about 9 m", the lane's limit, not what shipped; it now ships 15-20 m); what stands between two rays unseen (an islet 14 m long passed on its FAR side); marks with no hand read out of the cone (an unnumbered red crossed); a restricted area excused whole for one sample inside it (1,460 m inside); one rock making a channel in wide water; a port-hand mark she is on the wrong side of steered at (5.6 m); buoy to buoy across a gate (108 deg off her route) and for courtesy passes (the leg budget spent, a red 95 m wrong); a refused pass never asked again (190 m wrong); a re-aim costing a mark its distance; a 54 deg turn at a kept pass point; the set re-gate (89). ### ⚠⚠ THE CHART FIRST, THEN THE BUOYS: THE ENC-FIRST RULE 9 LANE (Andy, 2026-10-03, on his live Go-To up the Piscataqua: "the ASV does not run to the right side of the ENC marked channel for most of the run ... Any given ASV should recognize a channel from the ENC before relying on buoy placement", then "Often, there are not paired buoys but single buoys of a particular color"; 2026-10-04: "Build the Rule 9 v3 redesign next")

**His calls:** a channel on the ENC is a charted FAIRWAY or DREDGED AREA only (not the deep-water band), at any width; it is recognized before any buoy; marks are secondary to it and primary without it; red right returning, single buoys too; a buoy kept to starboard is passed at max(10 m, 2 x buffer) (outside the guard's standoff in a set).

**The defect:** the lane rode right of the channel only where buoy pairs made one. The charted fairway was not a channel to it, and single marks were not read at all.

**What it is now (`channelLaneRoute`, static/js/routing.js):** the buoy-pair lane and the banks' lane as before, then `chartOwnership` (which samples the chart owns, and the lane three quarters across the POLYGON, square to her course over CHART_TAN_M), then `markPassRoute` (single marks in water the chart does not own: each read from its own hand's numbered neighbors along her route, its own named channel first; a pass run put in one at a time, kept only if no mark she already has right ends on its wrong hand; wrong hand first; joins judged at kept vertices; bounded by WORK, MARK_STAGE_LEGS - a hard stop, the buoy-to-buoy re-aim too, his call, check 94), then `chartedChannelLane` LAST (overrides only owned samples, holds discs round mark runs outside owned water), then smoothTrack, gateLegClear, pruneStitch, and `marksKept` / `chartedRide` on the route that ships driving `how` and PARTIAL. A maneuver (charted:false, marks:false) is the pipeline of 2026-10-02 but for the gate's own law. The page words the banner and the Intent rows from `plan.how` (passage.js `buoyageNote` / `laneHow`, asv.html `setPlanIntent`).

**Review, and what it changed.** v2 (2 of 6 lenses) found 3 blocking defects and the v3 redesign replaced it. v3 was then reviewed by four lenses with a refuter each (workflow wf_f4c2db96-bf5): 18 findings, every one confirmed, every one fixed (`enc_channel` 53-64 and 14c, `gate_endpoint` 7-9 each FAIL on the reviewed code):
- marks: a gate partner crossed obliquely read as before/after (`gatePartner`, MARK_GATE_M); a single mark read from another named channel's count (`continues`); an entrance gate named apart (Ala Wai) unwatched.
- charted: a turn within 75 m of an END dragged the lane to the port edge (`CHART_END_SLIVER`); a mark's run held inside owned water pinned the lane 20 m off the port edge for 1.7 km (the hold pin skips owned samples); a fairway into a basin had no end (`endRing`: the lane leaving the END'S OWN ring) - and then Pearl Harbor's destination 100 m short of an end hooked back round (`pathLeaves`: a ramp only where her PATH leaves the run's end water before her route ends).
- pipeline: the cone's inverted band put the lane up to 1,048 m outside its chord (keep T[i]); in a set the chart lane at the buffer and an 89 m gap patched 10.6 km round the land (`clr` prefers standoff-clear lane points; `GATE_PATCH_RATIO`/`GATE_PATCH_SLACK_M` splice the search's own way); from a berth the gate waved the whole first leg past a pile and through a dolphin (the exempt water is the blocked run contiguous with the endpoint, never nearer the hazard than it less buf/4 - capped at 2 x buf instead it spliced a real Go-To into a 110 degree turn, so not capped); the wall-clock budget made marks depend on CPU load (MARK_STAGE_LEGS, legPath `quick`); kept run ends blocked the knot prune (`pass`).
- safety: a wrong-hand mark near a leg end went uncounted, and on a drawn transit every waypoint is a leg end (`markCounted` / `nearStart` / `nearEnd`); `how.narrow` claimed where the chart replaced the banks (`stands` for pairs AND banks); "passed close" said of buoys that were not (`buoys` / `close`, the Intent row words it).

**Re-verified, and what that changed.** The fixes were then re-reviewed by the same four lenses with a skeptic each (workflow wf_2477d0d1-1c1): every original finding re-checked, and 11 more found and confirmed, none refuted - five of them regressions of the fixes themselves. All fixed:
- the transit recount judged each mark by its first leg's hand against the nearest point of the WHOLE plan (an out-and-back read "6 marks NOT left on the proper hand"): now `markVerdicts` per leg on its own part of the route, every pass counted, a mark beside the waypoint two legs share once; a mark near the route's OWN start or end - her berth, his destination - is excused the count only where it lies BESIDE it (MARK_BESIDE_RATIO: no further along than 1.5 x its distance off; counted there, Cod Rock 5 off the start of his Go-To read wrong; excused regardless, a red 900 m on from her start was never counted - 25b, 25d), and a transit's interior waypoints always count (`markCounted(k, ends)`);
- CHART_END_SLIVER trimmed a real narrowing at a channel's end (an entrance channel ridden on its port side): now only within CHART_TAN_M of the end, and only a section that is not thin square to the run's own direction (`across`);
- the cone, measured across the SEARCH's path, narrowed without inverting where that path stepped off the channel (90 m to port of the middle for 870 m): see THE CONE below;
- `gatePartner` was judged against HER heading (a gate crossed more than 30 degrees off square still misread): now number, hand and MARK_GATE_M alone; a laned mark is not asked offChannel's questions;
- `continues` let a count restarting below a single speak for it (Bellingham, Starr Rock Buoy 4, crossed both ways): now the count must be numbered on FROM the mark (`facing`), and the same the other way for a single and a count;
- legPath shipped the leg from a snapped free cell into a goal inside its margin unasked (a real Portsmouth resume-from-here crossed 12 m of land, pre-existing in HEAD): now `clearButEnds` at END_CLEAR_M refuses it, and the planners route at the buffer;
- the berth exemption's splice from an endpoint inside the standoff hooked round it (101-172 degrees) and maneuvers stopped matching HEAD: the standoff re-gate now asks "never nearer" of its floor (the buffer, `opts.floor`), routes and knot-prunes an endpoint's patch at the endpoint's own clearance (gate_endpoint 11, 12);
- minors: "passed close" judged against MARK_PASS_M (`k.min`), not the found offset; keepStandoff re-measures `chartedRide` on the route it ships (`chartOwn`; 64b).

**THE CONE, and what the mutation sweep and a last review found in it.** The cone brings the lane inside any narrower stretch ahead or behind by the time she reaches it, easing at LANE_SLEW. It is read in each sample's OWN frame: a sample's band is the nearest of its own limits (chord edges, standoff in) and of every SETTLED owned neighbor's within CHART_CONE_REACH_M (600 m) - her path running straight through it (CHART_CONE_STRAIGHT_COS, 3 degrees) and its cross-section holding her - as that neighbor measured them across its own track: the offsets chartedChannelLane eases the lane in (`slewField`, along her path), so the cone reads them as the lane is built. The middle yields only to the stretch she runs straight along (`hStraight`): a narrowing there may take the lane to port of the sample's own chord's middle (the narrowing is real, and staying in the charted water needs it); any other neighbor's eases it to the middle and no further (INVARIANT 4). An inverted band keeps the sample's own point. Five designs were wrong first: measured across the search's path (a jog moved the band; inverted, 1,048 m out); projected into one plane (a winding fairway laned left of its middle; R.7); read from the neighbors running within 3 degrees only - the MUTANT that dropped that filter survived every suite, and probing why showed the filter was the defect: a width step round a bend of 5-45 degrees left the lane 12-25 m out of the charted water (67); then, found by a last three-lens review of that fix with a skeptic per finding (workflow wf_3adab6d6-367: 5 findings, all confirmed, all fixed): reading EVERY neighbor, the cross-sections where her path turns at the join of two charted rings - cut short by the end of the ring she leaves, or in the gap a corner of it wholly to one side - held the lane at the middle 250 m either side and the blend took the route 23-42 m to port of both channels' middles at a 40 degree port dogleg, under "right of center" (68, 68b); and clamped at the middle everywhere, a narrow part whose starboard edge steps in past the wide part's middle was reached 8-33 m out of the charted water (66b - which had pinned that clamp on the cone's own T, where it held; it now measures the route that ships). The reach, the inverted band and the bend each have a check that kills their mutant (66, 59b - the band inverts at the join of two charted rings, where the split middle put the lane 41 m outside its chord - and 67, now within a meter: 0.6 m for 2 m at 20 degrees, where the samples still turning are not read). (A jog of her path across a channel moves the frame the far side's limits are read in: the lane is held toward the middle beside it - never to port of it.)

**Verified:** enc_channel 94, gate_endpoint 13, buoy_lane, and all 74 suites that load a touched file, run by hand and never the hook (ais_range.py skipped: it starts a server); docs_valid, sanitization, spelling; the acceptance harnesses 47/47 (charted) and 35/35 (marks); on the final code the fuzz - Go-To and fly-through in a 1.75 kn set 0 of 393 hooks and 0 legs through a keep-out each, maneuvers 1 of 393 differing from HEAD (one vertex, as before), the pin 0 of 40 through, the cone fuzz 0 of 295 worlds with a lane point outside its chord at 3 m and at 19.5 m, the claim fuzz 0 false claims of 692 at 3 m and at 19.5 m; and a mutation sweep of every fix (below). ### ⚠⚠ A ROUTE STAYS INSIDE THE CHART THAT WAS READ (Andy, 2026-10-03: "Fix the chart box defect next")

**The defect (found on the live check of the ENC-first Rule 9 lane, on a fresh console).** The keep-out model holds the features of ONE box - `nogo.bbox`, the extract's own - and outside it holds NOTHING, which every clearance test reads as clear water. A command reads the chart over a box round the boat and the target, padded 300 m and joined to the operating area (`ensureNogoCovers`); the router's swing regions reach 900 m to 8.1 km past the leg. A fresh console's Go-To New Castle -> Adams Point (operating box north edge 43.1179) routed 429 m past it, and on his full chart 21 of its 402 legs were not clear: 10 land, 7 shallow, 4 hazards. His own console flew the same Go-To clear only because an earlier command had widened his box to 43.1915.

**What it is now:**
- **The planners judge the route against the box** (passage.js): `beyondChart(pts, box, edgeM)` / `insideBoxM` - null when every point stands `CHART_EDGE_M` (100 m) inside every edge, else {at (where the route LEAVES the box, or its first margin point when it never does), outM (the farthest BEYOND the box), edgeM, pts}; `beyondChartSay(u, fmt)` (`u.subject` for a command refused before any route: "the target lies ..."). `planNogoRoute` judges `[from, ...route]` AFTER the lane pass and refuses with `{error, reason: {mode: "uncharted", near}, uncharted: {...out, route}}` and NO `route`; `routePlan` returns `uncharted` beside its route, and its two callers refuse on it. No `nogo.bbox` (the suites' worlds) = no judgment. The hold disc is capped inside the box, less the buffer (`discInChart`).
- **The page reads over the refused route and plans again** (asv.html `planInsideChart(pts, opts, plan, what)`). First the command's OWN points: past the box and not readable (wider than `ENC_MAX_SPAN_DEG`, or the read failed) = refused WITHOUT planning - planning a target 1.5-2 deg off over an empty model measured 15-31 s of the page's only thread. Then plan; while uncharted: the union box's span (`sizeWhy` names the water already read when that is what makes it too wide), `ensureNogoCovers(pts + route, CHART_WIDEN_PAD_M = 1 km, {say, keep})`, the command's own water again (`{...opts, keep}`), `aisKeepoutsNow()` (a new extract MOVES THE FRAME), re-plan; at most `CHART_WIDEN_ROUNDS` (3) reads. A plan still uncharted gets `uncharted.say` / `.cause` (size / failed / rounds; `unchartedTip` advises by cause), and `error` for planNogoRoute's shape. Go-To / RTH / Transit (holdTarget INSIDE the plan closure, `ht !== null && ht.error`) / Upload / Resume-from-here (her and koIn taken again INSIDE the plan, after its read) plan through it; Transit and Upload refuse `plan.uncharted` before they draw or post. `tautRoundHer` hands a route past the box to the router. The other planNogoRoute paths (AIS way-round, held resumes, re-approach) get the planner's refusal, said through `planWhy` (fmtDist).
- **refreshNogo** never asks for a box the server refuses (`ENC_MAX_SPAN_DEG` 1.5 = asv_console.py's; `encSpanRefusal`) - its 400 used to set `nogo.ready = false` and the next plan went out degraded and straight with the guard blind. Its third argument `ask` = {say (the banner while it reads), keep (a failed read - no band, a throw, a partial extract - leaves the model and sea.enc as they were, writes ask.failed), failed}. A WIDER extract of the same chart (contains the last box, same band and floor) keeps `chartReads` and refolds them. The no-band note carries the server's `d.error`.
- **The passive transit estimate** shows an uncharted route as an estimate (beyond, or near the edge), never "unroutable"; its cache key carries the box. `drawViolation`: "past the water the chart was read over" / "near the edge of the chart read". Upload's no-model confirm re-asks `nogo.ready` before it sends anything unrouted.

**The review** (4 lenses - logic, coverage, a 96-command fuzz on his chart, tests - and a skeptic per serious finding; 9 agents). Found and fixed: a failed widening read dropped the whole model (guard blind; the pre-check then planned degraded - my 4j stand-in kept the model the real code dropped); a widening extract dropped the chart-image reads; resumeFromHere planned on the model from BEFORE its read while the backstop judged against the new box (pre-existing, 49 foul legs in the reviewer's repro); taut routes never judged; the hold disc reaching 500 m past the box; the Transit/Upload/chained-RTH refusals pinned by text only (now DRIVEN: command_result 51-53, pause_resume 1y); words (planner meters, wrong causes, the incident's two counts). The skeptics re-ran each blocking/major repro on the fixed tree with a control that reverts the fix: all reproduce on the control, none on the fix. The fuzz: old code sent foul legs on 28 of 96 commands; new routes 0 foul, all inside, lengths 0.992-1.019 of the full-chart plan; reads 0 (51) / 1 (26) / 2 (4), and the 1 km pad removed every second read it saw.

**Verified:** offline on his chart (scratch `box_replay.cjs`): old 21 foul of 402; new refused, one read, 410 legs, 0 foul, 18.03 km against 18.01 on the full chart; reverse direction unchanged. LIVE on a throwaway console (8797, fresh state dir, New Castle): FOUR runs on a throwaway console (8797, a fresh state dir each, New Castle) of a Go-To to Adams Point: each read the chart once along the refused route (box north edge 43.1179 -> 43.1252 at the first 300 m pad, 43.1309 at 1 km) and sent 419 / 411 / 410 / 410 waypoints - 0 legs foul on his full chart, the 106-120 legs north of the old edge all clear. The command's own first read took ~57 s from NOAA and each plan 7-11 s (the stall and TELEMETRY STALE banners stand during a plan - pre-existing). The read's own banner was covered by the stall watchdog's on runs 1-3; planInsideChart now waits out the watchdog's tick (STALL_TICK_MS + 100) before each read, and on run 4 the read's words held the screen through the read. Mutation sweep: 86 mutations in a scratch copy of the tree, all killed (an 85-mutation sweep left two survivors - the loop's own union check and the 1 km pad - which got checks 4o and 4p; then they and the extract size's rounding were run again); the stall-watchdog wait is verified live only.

**Tests:** tests/chart_box.js (42); nogo_readout 26-28b (45); command_result 51-53 (53); pause_resume 1y (63); chart_ink 14f and 22f, survey_order 8 re-pinned; ais_avoid / guard_resume / pause_resume / command_result worlds take the real planInsideChart / beyondChart / planWhy. Suites run by hand: chart_box (42, new), nogo_readout (45), chart_ink (54), command_result (53), pause_resume (63), ais_avoid (156), guard_resume (54), survey_order (13), planner_guard_seam, hold_point (38), end_action, measure_tool (39), berth_grant (47), buoy_lane, gate_endpoint (6), corner_slow (52), speed_recalc (22), survey_table (68), survey_transit_roles (40), turn_channel (36), turn_refusal (39), wreck_clearance, rule9_scope, off_track, strike_run (39), drawn_lines (11), line_stats (17), line_table_patch (12), port_slew, speed_modes, turn_geometry, ink_reads (14), spelling (6), page_strict (4); precommit_hook.py (8), docs_valid.py (8), sanitization.py (4).

**NOTED, NOT CHANGED:**

### ⚠⚠ THE GUARD'S MODEL OF SLOWING DOWN (Andy, 2026-10-03: "Do 1, fix the guard's model of slowing down" - item 1 of the open list after the lead shipped)

**The problem: on a hull that slows in gear (the DriX) the clearance guard took a slow-down as instant, three ways.**
- **The slow-instead-of-hold** (rung 3) and its every-frame re-check (`stillAnswers`) walked her at LOW from the instant they decided. In gear she takes the console's 1 s delay, a 3.3 s dead time and ~12 s of decay: at 7 kn it accepted a slow-down 41 m from the buffer edge where she needs ~54 m, so in between the hold fired late, ~7 m closer.
- **"Already slow"** was judged by the KEY she had been told (`slowKeyFor(st.speed_key)`). The governor's lead puts LOW on the wire ~15 s before she is at LOW; in that window the SLOW rung latched nothing (the governor kept the throttle and raised it with no release check) and rung 3 offered nothing (a hold reading there held her).
- **The AIS reach** left out the console's own command delay: a contact first in reach at 7 kn read 20.1 s to entry against the 20 s HOLD_S.

**What it is now:**
- **The walk:** coast.js `slowProfile(v0, v1, law, latencyS, elapsedS)` - her through-water speed t s from now, held for the delay still to run, then the exact in-gear decay, caught at the target (it IS speedStep read at any time, coast.js 26). guard.js `projectRoute(..., {twAt})` walks it, each step at its START speed (the faster end), the crab from the speed she is doing. asv.html `slowingOpts(v0, key)` hands it to rung 3 and the re-check; `{}` on a hull with no measured slow-down (exactly as before).
- **A cut runs only on evidence** - `cutAge(key, tw)`, seconds since the console sent `key`, and null unless: a law; the console's OWN last command (`speedWant`) is `key`; the vessel reports `key`; and her THROUGH-WATER speed is on the curve (no more than IN_CUT_MS over slowProfile from `speedWant.tw`, her speed when it was sent - `commandSpeed` records it on a law hull, via `twNowMs`). `cutUnderWay` adds that she is still over the key and the key is the slowest that makes way. Then: the SLOW rung latches a cut under way without re-sending; a FASTER want still on its way is replaced by sending the slow key again; rung 3 offers the slow-down to a cut under way, and is still asked AFTER the SLOW rung's own LOW (`cutOpen` - an approach reads SLOW first, and "slowed" then means only that LOW is on the wire); and the cut's elapsed time comes off the delay (`slowingOpts` credits `cutAge`).
- **The reach:** `aisReachM(..., latencyS)` adds (tw + set) x latency, ramped in over the half knot above LOW as the dead time is (charged in full it jumped 50.0 -> 52.1 m at 4.001 kn). The page passes SPEED_CMD_LATENCY_S at the ladder AND the release (reachBack). DriX: 90.4 / 96.3 / 131.2 m at 6.2 / 7 / 14 kn.

**⚠⚠ THE FIRST CUT OF THE EVIDENCE RULE WAS WRONG, AND THE REVIEW SAID HOW** (4 lenses, a skeptic per finding; 19 confirmed, 1 refuted). It judged "a cut is under way" by the reported key and speed alone, and credited the elapsed time once her SOG was 0.2 kn below the SOG at the send. So: a LOW sent long ago that she never came down on got the offer and the credit (the hold fired 16-23 m later); a faster want still pending was latched as SLOWED with nothing sent; a turn against the set faked or hid "she has come down"; a cut flown exactly to the model lost its credit for the quarter second after its dead time; the SLOW rung's own latch shut rung 3's new offer out on the ordinary SLOW-then-HOLD approach; the delay term broke the reach's continuity at LOW; and no-law hulls reached the new rungs. All fixed by the rule above. Also from the review: the ops manual's stale reach figures, and eight test gaps (credit inside the dead time, the delay pinned, mid-decay and a head set, the step-start convention by position, the profile from mid-cut speeds, 24g2's margin, continuity with the delay).

The three worlds that rebuild clearanceGuard (clearance_guard, ais_avoid, guard_resume) grab IN_CUT_MS, cutAge, cutUnderWay, slowingOpts, twNowMs and require slowLaw/slowProfile/SPEED_CMD_LATENCY_S; ais_avoid also defines `__setSpeedWant` (its eval'd `let speedWant` is NOT the test file's - an assignment from the test made a second, unread global and an earlier LOW in the world's own record credited 4 s to a cut that never ran: that is how the credit bug was found). corner_slow's 19b world grabs twNowMs. **MUTATIONS: three sweeps. ### ⚠⚠ THE IN-GEAR SLOW-DOWN IN THE SIM, THE CORNER WALK AND THE GOVERNOR'S LEAD (Andy, 2026-10-03: "Model the in-gear slow-down in the sim" - then, asked, "Sim + corner walk", and once the measurement showed what that does without one, "Lead + walk + sim")

**Why it grew.** The page's corner walk (turns.js `flownTrack`, the judge behind Punch Out's `judgeJoin` and Upload's `cornerSlowPlan`) mirrors the sim's 1.5 kn/s ramp, and the speed GOVERNOR commanded a turn's speed on the frame she reached the turn. In gear the DriX needs ~43 m to come from 7 kn to 4, so she entered every LOW turn at survey speed. A 4-agent scoping workflow measured it on synthetic DriX plans: with the law in the walk and no lead, Punch Out barely moved (1 of 321 wall positions) but every corner Upload answered by slowing came back "EVEN AT THE LOW SPEED" (10 m spacing: 15 slowed / 6 unanswered became 0 / 21); with a lead the punch verdicts were the ramp's and Upload answered more (21 / 0). Both scope calls were Andy's (asked, with those numbers).

**What it is - one law in four places:**
- **The step:** asv_console.py `speed_step_kn` (the sim's tick) and coast.js `speedStep` (the walk) - the same step. A cut to a target at or above idle + 0.25 kn on a hull with `maneuvering.slowdown` holds her speed for the dead time (lag ramped in over 0.5 kn above the target, fixed when the cut begins, never restarted by a deeper cut or a re-sent key), then the exact solution of dv/dt = -(v^2-U^2)/Lg, caught at the target. Everything else is the ramp: a speed-up, a STOP (never measured - she cannot be cut below idle in gear), every hull with no law. Coming down on the ramp leaves the dead time at 0, so a cut that follows a stop (the station-keep asking LOW half way through her stop) has no fresh 3.3 s. The floor is tested in the page's own arithmetic in both languages (m/s; in knots it fell the other way at an exact tie for 58 of 399 idle speeds - review), and both parse only REAL numbers (float() and JS `+` coerced different strings and lists - review). SimVcu sets `_slow_lag`; the prop-out coast branch is untouched.
- **The lead:** coast.js `slowLeadM(v, v1, law, latencyS, setMs)` = slowRun's water + a FOLLOWING set (along her track, never a head set) carried for the cut's time + the latency at her ground speed; `leadWant(want, v, ahead, law, latencyS, latched, setMs)` takes the slowest leg ahead within its lead, MEASURED FROM max(v, want) - from her own speed alone it let go near the end of every cut that charged a latency (401 of 401 run-ins in review) and raised a run already at LOW only to cut it again - and holds a `latched` leg.
- **The governor (asv.html):** `leadFor(want, prev)` (PURE; null at once with no slowdown block, null off a survey run) from her through-water speed (ground less set), `SPEED_CMD_LATENCY_S`, the set along her track and `runLegKeys` (routeSpeedKeys + Upload's corner set, memoized in `_legKeys` - it walks the whole plan, at 4 Hz); `leadSpeedKey` is the governor's door and keeps `govLead` (the latch, cleared at the top of every frame so any stand-down drops it); `speedGovernor`: `planned` -> `lead || planned`. `leadShown()` is the readouts' door: govLead in the supervising tab, a read-only `viewLead` with its own latch elsewhere (a view-only card read DISAGREEMENT for every lead - review). The RUN block's "for" row says "SLOWING to low N m before the leg to waypoint W - in gear she needs that water to come down"; the command bar's agree test and its tooltip name it.
- **The walk (turns.js):** `hullSlowLaw()`; `flownTrack(..., legMs)` steps with speedStep on a law hull and, given `legMs` (the plan's targets, pure), flies leadWant with latency 0 and no set (the governor spends the latency; the walk has no drift model) and a `leadAt` latch (unlatched it let go twice through a 165 deg reversal before a slowed leg - mutation). `cornerSlowPlan`: pass 1 passes `planMsAt` as legMs; the slowed pass passes `slowMsAt` as both - NO per-leg withholding on a law hull (each withholding raised the target, ended the cut and restarted the dead time: a slowed arc was walked at 7.00 kn). `joinBreaches(..., legMs)` passes through. `judgeJoin` (asv.html) lengthens the run-in by slowLeadM(survey, low) on a law hull and flies its LOW retry from the lead.
- **The table (routeSpeedKeys):** a slow-radius turn is keyed LOW into and out of ITS join (the governor always flew it LOW; Upload judged it at the turn role); the line before a turn point is lineOfLeg's nearest match (first match named the line before on 5 m patterns - review); and a routed HOP's vias - commitPattern flags them `turn` like a reversal's - are keyed TRANSIT when the gap is not isReversalGap, as the governor flies them. ⚠ That last was an UNDER-FLAG OF HOP CORNERS SINCE 2026-09-24 (judged at the turn speed, flown at transit), and with the lead it was a 7-4-14-4-14 kn sawtooth across every hop (review, end to end). These two keying fixes move a few Z-Boat/BEN Upload verdicts too; their commanded speeds and their walk's stepping are unchanged.

**Verified:** the walk against SimVcu on three DriX corners with and without the lead agrees to 0.0005 m of departure (fixtures from scratch `gen_ingear_fixture.py` through the real SimVcu.tick, pinned in corner_slow 28); speed_step_kn and speedStep agree to 5e-15 kn over 362 scripted ticks (coast_sim 14 runs Node); Upload's in-gear verdicts pinned by real cornerSlowPlan runs (29c).
