### ⚠⚠ THE DriX's SLOW-DOWN, MEASURED (Andy, 2026-10-03: "Do 1, measure the DriX slow-down from the logs" - item 1 on the open list - then, on the finding: "Build the fix with the 3.3 s lag")

**What was measured.** Her own bags, `D:\Claude\Fuel\D8_2040` (READ-ONLY; 16 sessions Aug 4-15 2026, EM2040 gondola, Lewes and Delaware Bay), by a 10-agent workflow: three methods (true neutral coasts, commanded in-gear cuts, physics and timing), two skeptics each, then a synthesis. Every speed is THROUGH THE WATER - the set was removed with a current fitted session by session to her own powered running on many headings (it predicts the coasts' sideways drift to 0.00 m/s median, n=145).
- **The prop-out coast held.** Clutch to neutral, 6 -> 2 kn in **40.3 m** (IQR 38.2-41.9, n=16, 6 sessions), Lc 36.7 m; the old estimate (44 m from 7 to 2 kn, Lc 35.1) was right in form. `maneuvering.coast` now carries the measured bin. Lc rises with speed (~22 m at 1-2 kn to ~45 m at 5-6 kn), so one number runs long below 4 kn and short above it - the COAST_LC_TOL comment now says so.
- **⚠ The guard's SLOW is NOT a coast.** 20 of 20 commanded cuts from her 7-kn setpoint to her 4-kn LOW kept the clutch IN GEAR: she decays toward her idle-in-gear speed (3.6-3.7 kn), not toward zero, and LOW sits only ~0.35 kn above that floor. Her "7 kn" is an rpm (1656) = **6.2 kn** through the water. To 4.0 kn: **32.5 m / 13.0 s** (IQR 29.1-35.5 m); to 4.5 kn 21.0 m / 7.4 s. The rpm starts down 0.3-0.7 s after the setpoint message; real deceleration starts 1.2 s after a single STEP and 3.3 s after a guidance RAMP.
- **The console was OPTIMISTIC.** The coast law allowed 15.4 m / 6.1 s in the live call (it is fed through-water speed), so the AIS reach was 65-70 m against the 82.5 m measured (94 m in a 1.75 kn set). A bigger Lc does NOT fix it: the equivalent Lc is 57-92 m depending on the band, and it would break the drift-in (COAST_MAX_S). The shape is wrong, not the constant.

**The fix: a second law, for slowing down in gear.**
- **coast.js `slowLaw(block)` / `slowRun(v0, v1, law)`:** a dead time `lag`, then quadratic drag against the idle prop's thrust, `v dv/dx = (U^2 - v^2)/Lg` with U = idle: x = v0*lag + (Lg/2) ln((v0^2-U^2)/(v1^2-U^2)), t = lag + (Lg/2U) ln(((v1+U)(v0-U))/((v1-U)(v0+U))). With U = 0 and no lag it IS coastRun. v1 is raised to idle + SLOW_IDLE_MARGIN_MS (0.25 kn) - in gear she never gets below idle, and the log would blow up at it - and a v0 at or under that sheds nothing (null). `slowLaw` refuses a block with idle or length not positive and finite, or a negative lag (null -> the coast law).
- **SLOW_LAG_RAMP_MS (found by the review):** the dead time ramps in over the half knot above the target. Charged in full, the reach JUMPED at LOW - 50.0 m at 4.000 kn, 56.8 m at 4.001 - so a hundredth of a knot of speed noise at LOW moved the ladder's horizon 7 m and could flicker a SLOW. Now 50.049 m at 4.001 kn, and the lag is whole from 4.5 kn on.
- **vessels/drix08.json `maneuvering.slowdown`:** {idle_kn 3.65, length_m 23.8 (two methods fitted 23.9 and 23.8 independently), lag_s 3.3, measured, source}. **lag_s 3.3 is HIS CALL:** it is the ramp's lag, because nobody knows yet whether a console SLOW reaches her as a step or a ramp. With each cut's own lag the law reproduces the 20 cuts to +0.1 / +0.3 / -0.7 m at 4.5 / 4.25 / 4.0 kn; with 3.3 s on every cut it needs 37.2 m to 4.0 kn against the measured 32.5 - long, the safe side (the step's 1.2 s would be 30.5 m, about 6.7 m less reach).
- **ais_keepout.js `aisReachM(man, ...)`** now takes the WHOLE maneuvering block: the in-gear law where it declares a `slowdown`, else the coast law (a bare coast block - `from_kn` set - still works as before, and so does a malformed slowdown), else 50 m. **asv.html** hands `slowMan` (`V.VESSEL.maneuvering`) to BOTH the ladder's `aisReach` and the release's `reachBack` - one law for both, or the release asks a smaller reach than the ladder used and lets her speed up into the contact it slowed for. The Z-Boat and BEN declare neither: 50 m, unchanged.

**THE DriX's REACH NOW** (⚠ superseded the same day by THE GUARD'S MODEL OF SLOWING DOWN, above: the page asks it with the console's 1 s command delay - 90.4 / 96.3 / 131.2 m - and ais_avoid 24c was re-pinned, a hull 95 m ahead now ANSWERED at 7 kn): 87.2 m at 6.2 kn (her real speed at the 7-kn setpoint), 92.7 m at 7 kn (the sim's), 124.0 m at 14 kn - EXTRAPOLATED, she never exceeded ~10.6 kn through the water in the logs; in a 1.75 kn set at 6.2 kn, 100.0 m (the run takes 14.3 s). At LOW, 50 m, continuous. It was 66 / 70.5 / 96 m.

**⚠ RESTART THE CONSOLE to take it:** the vessel JSON is read when the console starts; a refresh keeps the old datum and no slowdown block (the page then runs the coast law, the old 70 m).

**Tests:** coast.js 13-18 (23 checks: the closed form against its ODE integrated by RK4, the reduction to coastRun, the dead time once half a knot over the target, the idle clamp, the refusals, and from 6.2 kn never short of the measured MEDIANS at 4.5 / 4.25 / 4.0 kn where the coast law was short of all three); ais_keepout 11b re-pinned to 5 mm (87.166 / 92.700 / 124.019, the set +14.284 - the review found the first pins, 92.67 and 123.97, passing by under a millimeter), 11b1 continuous at LOW, 11b2 a coast-only or malformed block keeps the coast law, 11c extended (46 checks); ais_avoid 24c on her whole block (a hull 85 m ahead answered at 7 kn, 95 m not, 85 m at LOW not), 24d renamed (it runs on the coast datum alone), **24e NEW: slowed to LOW with a hull 80 m ahead she is NOT released** - between the coast reach and the slow reach, so only the release asked by the same law holds her (142 checks); coast_sim 1 (LC = 40.3/ln 3). **MUTATIONS 20 of 20** in a scratch export (graded on coast, ais_keepout, ais_avoid, coast_sim; real files hash-checked unchanged). The first sweep left ONE survivor - "the release asked with the coast block only", the exact wiring that lets her speed up into the contact - and 24e is what kills it. **Review** (math / integration / claims, two verifiers per finding): fixed the jump at LOW, the near-miss pins, drix08's "validated to within a meter" (true only with each cut's own lag), "the rpm goes to idle 0.3-0.7 s after" (it STARTS down then), README_SIM still saying ESTIMATED, the COAST_LC_TOL comment's overclaim, and the names of 18 and 24d.

**NOTED, NOT CHANGED (his calls):**
- ~~**THE SIM SLOWS FAR FASTER THAN THE GUARD NOW BUDGETS.**~~ DONE the same day - see THE IN-GEAR SLOW-DOWN IN THE SIM above. SimVcu shed a commanded speed change on the engine's 1.5 kn/s ramp - 7 to 4 kn in ~2 s and ~5.7 m - where the real DriX takes 13 s and 32.5 m. So in a sim rehearsal the DriX now slows ~90 m out and creeps the rest at LOW. Modeling the in-gear decay in SimVcu would make the rehearsal honest; it would also move the timing of every sim suite that slows her.

### SEQUENCED SURVEYS, PHASE 3b: THE HOLD BEFORE A SURVEY (Andy, 2026-10-02: "Start the hold before a survey" - his call, made at 3a: she waits AT THE HELD SURVEY'S START until the operator presses Continue; nothing releases her by itself)

**Why a split.** The vessel has no mid-route dwell, only an action at the END of a route (complete / loiter / RTH / repeat, the link's `_completion`). So a hold is a SPLIT UPLOAD: the plan up to and including the held survey's first waypoint, ending in LOITER; Continue uploads the rest.
- **surveys.js `splitAtHold(wps, surveys, release)`** -> {part, held, cut} | null: the FIRST survey with `hold === true` (not `release`) that the list enters, cut at its first waypoint inclusive; a held first survey cuts at 0 (she goes to its start and waits).
- **doUpload(opts):** `wpsAll` (the plan, or from `fromSv`), `hold = splitAtHold(wpsAll, mission.surveys, opts.release)`, `wps = hold ? hold.part : wpsAll`; the routed POST adds `completion: "loiter"` for a split; success sets `pendingHold` ({sv, at}, localStorage `asv_pending_hold_v1`; every successful upload rewrites it) and banners "UPLOADED UP TO S2'S START ... the rest of the plan is NOT aboard yet"; it now RETURNS true when taken (Continue waits on it).
- **Console:** `Engine.upload(route, hold_clear_m, completion)` - completion may only be "loiter" (anything else: VcuProtocolError -> 409, nothing uploaded); the run takes it, `plan_completion()` (the setting) untouched. `_check_surveys` types `hold` (bool).
- **Continue** (`continueHold`): only on the pending survey's row (`svr<i>_cont`, its own line, open only while `holdWaiting()` - holding and NOT paused, else "Holding at its start - on her way"); `doUpload({fromSv: id, release: id})`, then `startRun()` - the Start button's handler, now a named function (its confirmation, its fresh-run clears) - only if the upload was taken.
- **Hold toggle:** the picked row's fifth action `svr<i>_hold` ("Hold: off/on", saves); ⏸ on the row's figures and the chart label ("S2 Ledge ⏸ hold"); an edit keeps `hold` (the survey's, not the drawing's); a delete or CLR PLAN drops the pending hold.
- **⚠⚠ FOUND ONLY LIVE: THE END-OF-PLAN RTH CHAIN FIRED AT THE HOLD.** "loiter" is a HOLDING end and a survey is chainable, so with End of plan RTH the page's chain (onState, ~"End of plan — chaining Return-to-Home") sent her home from the point she was told to wait at. `heldSplitRun(s)` = pendingHold && survey && run_completion "loiter" && setting not "loiter"; the chain AND `rthPending()` skip it. ⚠ NOT the frame alone: the same frame with no hold pending is a plan uploaded under Loiter and switched to RTH while it ran, which has always chained home (end_action 5d caught my first, frame-only version; 5e pins both). And a guard-held resume of the way there (`resumeHeldRun`'s upload) keeps the loiter when its tail ends at the held start (`tailEndsAtHold`).
- **⚠ ALSO FIXED (found reading the unrouted branch): an UNROUTED upload of a PART** (3a's Upload from, or a split) posted no route, and the console then flew the WHOLE saved plan. A part is now always sent as its own route (`partial`); the whole plan unrouted still posts nothing (1e).

### SEQUENCED SURVEYS, PHASE 3a: RUNNING THE SURVEYS (Andy, 2026-10-02: "Start phase 3", with his three calls)

**His calls (asked first):** build (a) Go-To a survey's start, (b) run from a survey, (c) done/partial, (d) Punch all, (e) the water level per survey NOW - and the hold before a survey NEXT, on its own; the hold waits AT THE HELD SURVEY'S START until the operator presses Continue (nothing auto-releases her); "reverse" means the WHOLE SURVEY BACKWARDS (entered at the far end of its last line, lines in reverse order, each the other way). ⚠ The vessel has NO mid-route dwell - only an end-of-route action (complete/loiter/RTH/repeat, `Engine._run_route`) - so the hold must be a SPLIT UPLOAD: send up to the held survey's start with "loiter", Continue sends the rest. That is the next feature's design.

**What 3a is:**
- **The picked row's actions** (a third and fourth line on the row `cardSurveyId()` names; ids `svr<i>_go|_from|_rev|_clr`; labels shortened to fit two to a line - "Go-To start / Upload from here / Clear progress" took four lines and a 113 px row): `goToSurvey` (canCommand gate, `doGoTo` to `mission.waypoints[surveyStartIdx]`), `uploadFromSurvey` (behind `#b_upload`'s disabled/title, then `doUpload({fromSv})`), `reverseSurvey`, `clearSurveyProgress`.
- **doUpload(opts):** `const wps = fromSv ? waypointsFrom(mission, fromSv) : mission.waypoints || [];` and a survey with no waypoints is REFUSED before the empty-plan branch (an empty slice there = "upload an empty plan" = clear the plan aboard). The banner says which surveys were left out. `opts` is the click event otherwise.
- **Backwards:** `patReverse` + `#sp_reverse` (reset by resetPattern; recorded as `settings.reverse`, put back by ✎); in punchOut `if(patReverse) ro.ordered = runBackwards(ro.ordered);` right after `regionOrder` - only `ro.ordered` is read after it, and the clip memo caches the runs BEFORE ordering. LIVE: S1's new first waypoint was its old last to 0.0 m and its new last its old first.
- **repunchSurvey / withCardKept / punchAll:** load the survey as ✎ does, flip if asked, await the real `punchNow`, commit with the real `commitPattern` ONLY when `patClip` is set and `punchRefusal` passes (a punch that did not finish leaves patClip null, and commitPattern would then commit the drawing UN-punched); the card's settings captured before and put back after; `punchAllBusy` disables the button.
- **Line progress:** `trackLineCoverage` (after accumLineTime in the telemetry tick - NOT inside it, which ~6 suites grab verbatim) adds the step along `mission.lines[runLineIdx]` to `lineCov[key]` (`addCoverage`, gap 1 m); a step over COV_STEP_MAX_M 40 m or a frame off the line breaks the run. `lineCovFrame`: the key orders the two ends, so the same line run backwards keeps its coverage. `lineDoneFrac` leaves the leads out; DONE at LINE_DONE_FRAC 0.9 (the first meters after a turn are flown before she is aligned). `saveLineCov` every 5 s to localStorage `asv_line_cov_v1`, pruned to the plan's lines, NEVER before `missionLoaded`. `surveyProgress(id)` by drawn line. LIVE: S2's first 73 m line read 46.6-72.5 m covered at the first look (mid-line), 2-73 m when she had run it (one ~2 m hole at 69-71 m, a frame off the line), and the row went "S2 0/4" -> "S2 1/4".
- **The water stamp:** commitPattern records `water_m` (sea.waterOffset - the punch is thrown away whenever the level moves, so the level at commit IS the level it was cut at) and `punched_at`; `surveyTideMoved` flags |Δ| >= SURVEY_TIDE_FLAG_M 0.25 m, signed; the row shows ⚠ and the tip says fallen/risen and what it means.
- **Console:** `water_m` (finite), `punched_at` (string <= 40), `settings.reverse` (bool) type-checked.

**The table** (`#sv_table` at the top of `#linePanel`, built by `renderSurveyTable`): one row per survey in run order - `S#`, a name field, `nL coverage`, ▲ ▼ ✎ ✕. ### THE LINE A LEG RUNS IS THE NEAREST MATCH (Andy, 2026-10-02: "fix the line matching for tight patterns" - found and reported, not changed, during sequenced surveys phase 1)

**What it was.** `currentLegLine` named the line under way by the FIRST committed line whose two ends lay within LINE_MATCH_M (5 m) of the route leg's, either way round, and `legOfLine` found the leg that runs line k by the FIRST leg joining line k's ends within 5 m. On a pattern spaced 5 m or less the line BEFORE - run the other way, each end one spacing off - passes too and comes first. Probed on the page's own function: at 4 m every line after the first was credited to the one before it (0,0,1,2,3,4), at 5 m every other one (0,0,2,2,4,4); correct from 5.5 m. Consequences: the LINES card timed the wrong lines, "line N of M" named them, `slow_turn_out` and the pause mark keyed to them, and Resume from here took the line before's leg and its direction - running the chosen line BACKWARDS. The small boat's default pattern is 5 m.

**The fix.** `lineOfLeg(a, b)` -> `{line, fwd, e}` | null, the ONE place it is decided: the full pass takes the smallest worst end distance (ties keep the first, as before); the remainder pass (a resumed leg: on the line, ending at an end) the nearest end - its end test FIRST, onLineM only for a line whose end the leg reaches, the old evaluation order (corner_slow's world has no onLineM and never needed one). `currentLegLine` returns its `.line`; `legOfLine`'s `endOf(j)` answers `fwd` only when `lineOfLeg` names k. A route's waypoints are exact copies of the line ends, so the true line matches to the millimeter.

**Also: the plan-time walk.** `committedRoleLengths` took the first waypoint within 5 m of a line's start and gave up (null - the card falls back to one speed) when the next was not its end. The core's own turn generator puts a turn's last point 1-3 m from the next line's start at every spacing (measured at 5, 8, 10, 20 and 80 m with `teardropTurn`); the turns the punch COMMITTED on the phase-1 live check stayed 9 m or more clear (the run trims), so NO REAL PLAN WAS SEEN FAILING - said so in the code. It now searches for the line's two ends as a PAIR, which can only meet this line's own (the line before is behind `at`, the line after runs the other way).

**Tests:** survey_transit_roles 17 (4 m and 5 m name every line; the old rule, written out, gives 0,0,1,2,3,4 and 0,0,2,2,4,4), 17b (flown on the real accumLineTime: line 4 of a 4 m pattern clocked as line 4, the activity says so), 17c (a resumed remainder on a 4 m pattern is its own line; the old rule says the line before), 17d (a turn point 1.8 m from the next start: the walk returns 900 m survey + the turns; the old walk null); pause_resume 18c (the leg for line 4 of a 4 m pattern is its own, fwd +1; the old search takes line 3's, fwd -1). Seven worlds learned `lineOfLeg` (ais_avoid, corner_slow, guard_resume, off_track, pause_resume, survey_order, survey_transit_roles). **Mutations 9 of 9 caught** (the first-match defect itself by exactly 17, 17b and 18c); the real files byte-identical after.

**LIVE on throwaway 52832** (his 8791 closed; the vessel there has an 80 m minimum line and a 14.4 m turn radius): a 4-line pattern at 4 m spacing, 127 m lines, three teardrops, uploaded (40 waypoints) and STARTED. Line 1 clocked 0:38 on row 1; through the turn nothing was credited; on line 2 the LINES card's marker moved to ROW 2 and line 2's actual ran 0:07 -> 0:34 while line 1's stayed 0:38 - the old rule credited that run to line 1. (The first draw, 60 m lines, was refused by yesterday's empty-punch rule, naming the 80 m minimum.)

**Known limit, unchanged:** two lines in EXACTLY the same place (a survey drawn twice over the same water) still tie, and the first wins.

### SEQUENCED SURVEYS, PHASE 1: THE GROUNDWORK (Andy, 2026-10-02: "Recommend feature structure to create sequenced surveys. Multiple surveys can be created and named/numbered in Survey card. Then the user can select the order in which the survey blocks are completed. GOTO function for inter-survey travel." On the recommendation: "Start phase 1, keep the number with the survey")

**The structure he was given** (in chat, not built beyond this phase): surveys are named blocks INSIDE the one flat plan; ONE Upload flies the sequence (not page-chained runs - the end-of-plan RTH chain is where Eastport and New Castle came from); the leg into each later survey is routed as the approach already is (standoff, Rule 9 lane, transit speed); Survey card table (number, name, order, state) with Go-To start / Run from here. Phase 2 = the table and editor, reordering, chart labels, the Upload compile with Go-To-routed transits, LINES grouped by survey. Phase 3 = Punch all, done/partial + Run from here, the water level stamped per survey, a hold before a survey (split the upload so she loiters on her own), reverse a survey by re-punching. **His calls (ANSWERED 2026-10-02 for phase 2 - per survey as recommended, Rule 9 on the transits, no hold yet; see the phase-2 block above):** which settings are per survey (recommended per survey: pattern, boundary, Max depth, leads, turn shape; plan-wide: buffer, the three speeds, End of plan and Min depth - Min depth is the routing floor every behavior and the guard use); the Rule 9 lane on the transits between surveys (his 09-05 rule says they are transits; the 08-31 correction keeps the lane off legs inside a pattern); a hold between surveys. **His answer given: the number stays with the survey.**

**Part 1 - the surveys in the plan** (`static/js/surveys.js`, NEW). `mission.surveys` lists the surveys in RUN ORDER, `{id, no, name, pattern: {A, B, C, align} | null, punched}`; every line, and every waypoint a survey put in the plan, carries `sv` = its id; a waypoint with no tag is FREE (WPT, a search pattern); each survey's entries are contiguous in both lists, in the listed order.
- `commitPattern`: each committed pattern is a survey, `no` = 1 + the highest held (never a count, never re-used: S1 + S5 -> S6; a hand-edited file's colliding id is skipped), tags exactly what it pushed (from `firstLine`/`firstWp`, recorded BEFORE `const leads` so corner_slow's verbatim slice of the push loop is untouched), records the drawing from `surveyPattern`'s new `anchors` (plain positions). `surveyPattern` returns `anchors: {A, B, C, align}`.
- `loadMission` carries `surveys` (the `speeds` lesson: name it or lose it) and runs `normalizeSurveys`: lines and no surveys -> ONE survey S1, everything tagged (silent - every existing plan); sound -> kept, list put in run order; broken (an untagged line, a tag naming no listed survey, a survey's lines or waypoints split, the lists in different orders) -> FOLDED into the first-listed survey and bannered "PLAN LOADED AS ONE SURVEY - ... (why)". Nothing is guessed: two patterns added before today stay one survey.
- `clearPlan` and `resetMission` clear `surveys`; a waypoint DRAG now keeps the point's fields (`{...old, ...np}`) - it used to put a bare `{lat, lon}` there, dropping the survey (a free waypoint inside a survey's run, which the next load folds) and a turn point's `turn` flag.
- Console: `_check_surveys` in `check_plan_body` (TYPES ONLY - ids, unique whole-number `no`, name length, pattern corners, align 0-2, punched bool, `sv` a survey id); `surveys` in load_mission, its no-file default and save_mission; `_keep_previous_plan`'s geometry() ignores `sv`, so tagging a plan takes no backup slot (a reorder still does).

**Part 2 - each survey judged by its own lines** (asv.html). `reversalScaleM(k)` and `turnZoneM(k)` measure only pairs INSIDE line k's survey (the tag read inline as `sv || ""`, so untagged lines - every fixture, every older plan - are one survey; inline rather than an imported helper because ~16 suites grab these functions verbatim); `isReversalGap` answers false for any gap BETWEEN two surveys; accumLineTime asks `turnZoneM(lastRunLine)`; `linePartContinues` never joins two surveys' lines; `lineSetKey` carries the tag. MEASURED on the real accumLineTime (survey_transit_roles 16b): an 80 m survey after an 8 m one, its reversal swung 60 m wide - tagged: turn the whole way at LOW (4 kn); untagged (the old judgment): TRANSIT at HIGH (14 kn). A one-survey plan judges identically (16d).

**Part 3 - every chart read kept** (`static/js/inkreads.js`, NEW). The page held ONE read: a refused or other-water read EMPTIED it, so every pier found before left the planners' and the guard's model; an Upload read ONE box over the boat and every waypoint, refused past 256 tiles (~3.5 km at z17, 43 N), so a spread plan read nothing and dropped the punches' piers. Now `chartReads` keeps every read of the extract (cap INK_READS_MAX 64, oldest out); `refoldInk` merges them into `chartInk` (same shape - readout, `foldChartInk`, the drawn layer and the punch memo key unchanged; the key names every read) via `mergeReads`: finest first, at one zoom latest first; a line both ends within 15 m of one taken, or a footprint whose centroid lies in one taken, is the same; NOTHING dropped for not being found again (an unread tile is blank paper). `ensureChartInk` skips water a read holds at its zoom or at z18 (`coveringRead`, the grid from the extracted `inkTileGrid` the scan now shares); a refusal or throw adds nothing and takes nothing (`inkRefused` on the readout until a read holds that water); `refreshNogo` drops every read. `readPlanInk`: an Upload (`ensureNogoCovers(..., null, {plan: true})`) reads its box, or - too big - its transits leg by leg (`pathThroughSurveys`: boat, each survey's first and last waypoint; `pathBoxes`: grow while it fits, the next opening at the last point, long legs halved, at most 16, a banner for the rest), then each survey's water (`surveyPoints`, padded 100 m - inside the punch's 120 m + lead box, so normally reused). Go-To / RTH / transit / Set Home read their one box as before (their prompt refusal kept).

**Tests:** survey_blocks NEW (14), ink_reads NEW (14); survey_transit_roles 16-16d (every case runs untagged as its CONTROL); drawn_lines 2b; plan_save 10 (surveys cleared) + 12; mission_store 16-16c; chart_ink 14 (executed now - the old source grep pinned the line that emptied the read), 14b rewritten, 14c-14f new, 22f re-pinned; nogo_readout's world learned `readPlanInk`. **Mutations 67 of 67 killed** in a scratch clone, the real files byte-identical after. Four needed a stronger fixture or a corrected expectation first: numbering by COUNT survived (S1+S3 lets the id check hide it - now S1+S5 -> S6); the Upload reading survey interiors as transits survived (a 5-line test survey's first and last points spanned it - now 4 lines); turnZoneM per survey and the box-overlap rule each needed a new check (16b's wide swing with 30 m S1 lines; ink_reads 4e). ### A GATE IS TWO MARKS OF ONE CHANNEL (Andy, 2026-10-01: "fix the cross-channel buoy pairing" - noted on the live check of the buoy-corridor fix)

**What it was.** `pairGates` (keepouts.js) took each port mark's nearest starboard mark 15-400 m away, whatever channel it marked. Over the Portsmouth extract (read-only GETs of a throwaway's `/api/enc`), 4 of 7 gates crossed channels:
- three Sagamore Creek / Northward Channel pairs where those channels meet, already dropped by `gateSweep` because they bracket charted water;
- Goat Island Ledge #9 / Henderson Point #10, 307 m across. No charted channel touched its 612 x 678 m corridor, so it STOOD. Seven survey lines drawn across it had a channel cut out of them (the span rule over the old list); with the fix, none.

**The fix.** A mark pairs only with marks of its own channel: `markId`'s `sys` (the name less its tail), grouped by `markRoots`. That is the prefix merge `markSystems` always applied, a word prefix whose numbers do not collide, pulled out so both read ONE rule. Unnamed marks ('') pair only with each other. keepouts.js drift #6.
- `markSystems` on `markRoots` is checked IDENTICAL to the HEAD body on 20,000 randomized mark sets (names built to provoke merges, collisions and duplicates) and on the real marks of Portsmouth (41), Lewes (3) and Bellingham (20).
- After the fix, Portsmouth makes 5 same-channel gates and keeps 1 corridor (Little Harbor #11/#10). Lewes and Bellingham pair exactly as before. The lane A/B (Node, real modules, old list vs new) gives identical routes; the lane engaged at Lewes and Bellingham, not on the Portsmouth paths.
- Noted, not changed: `pairGates` does not dedupe, so Bellingham's twice-charted buoys make each gate twice (identical corridors, harmless).

**Tests:** turn_channel 17-17f:
- 17: own channel over a nearer other;
- 17b: no own partner in reach, no gate;
- 17c: the entrance marks still pair;
- 17d: colliding numbers stay apart;
- 17e: unnamed only with unnamed;
- 17f: `markSystems`' whole output - dedupe, merge in number order, a colliding name, a letters-only prefix, an unnamed mark - which NO suite had called before (two only imported it).

**Mutations 7 of 7 killed** in a scratch clone, graded on turn_channel + rule9_scope + buoy_lane. The lane suites never went red: they build their systems by hand, which is why 17f had to exist.

**Also corrected:** this file's lane glossary still named `gateProject()` and `channelEndExtend()` as steering a Go-To through the outermost gate. Neither exists; the note there says so.

### AN EMPTY PUNCH IS NOT "ADD TO PLAN" (Andy, 2026-10-01: "fix the empty punch saying Add to plan" - noted on the live check of the buoy-corridor fix, where the DriX punched 7 lines to 0 segments and still read "Add to plan")

**What it was.** An empty `patClip` is `[]`, which is TRUTHY, so `punchRefusal`'s `!patClip` test passed it, and with no red reversal nothing below it refused. `commitPattern` then took `lines = patClip || patSourceLines()` = `[]`: it committed nothing, set `planKind` to survey, `resetPattern`'d the drawn pattern away and saved. Meanwhile the summary ended "clear of keep-outs ... Survey ~--. Add to plan." (no counter set means "clear").

**The fix.** `punchOut` records `patFunnel = {drawn, clipped, struck, slivers, short, minLine, chans}` beside `patClip` (`slivers` = `ro.ordered.length - shortened.length`). `punchRefusal`, after the unfinished-punch test, returns `emptyPunchRefusal(patFunnel)` for an empty `patClip`. The causes, in the order the stages took the lines, each with only its own fix:
- the chart, when NOTHING at all was left (every line in a keep-out or outside the depth window, with any channels excluded named): draw the box over water this vessel can survey, or check the survey depth window;
- the operator's strikes: put the struck runs back;
- slivers under a meter: the box over water again;
- the hull's minimum: draw lines long enough to keep that much coverage each;
- with channels cut out of the coverage, also "uncheck Shipping channels, if ... meant to be surveyed".

The summary says "NOTHING LEFT TO SURVEY, so nothing to add to the plan — the note under Add to plan says what took the lines." It drops "clear of keep-outs" and the survey time. `resetPattern` clears the funnel; that is hygiene, inert like `patRed`.

**⚠ Found on the way, and NOT what I first wrote:** I took the `> 1 m` filter after `shortenSeg` for a silent "shorter than the turn margins" drop and wrote a summary clause saying so. `shortenSeg` hands a run too short for both margins back WHOLE, so that clause named a cause the code cannot produce. It was removed before any test ran. The filter only ever drops sub-meter slivers, and those need lines a meter or two long, because `clipLine` keeps only pieces spanning a whole ~2 m sample step.

**Verified live** (throwaway 52829, the DriX at Bellingham, z16): a 20 x 301 m pattern wholly inland (checked solid land in the page's own model first) punched to "20 lines → 0 segments ... NOTHING LEFT TO SURVEY". Add to plan was disabled, titled "Refused: the punch left no survey line", with the note naming the chart. The pattern stayed.

**Tests:** turn_refusal 20-20f, through the page's own punch:
- 20 / 20b: the chart, when a dock covers the box, and the commit then changes nothing;
- 20c: the hull's minimum, at 500 m;
- 20d: every run struck off;
- 20f: slivers, from 1.5 m lines;
- 20e: a kept punch still ends "Add to plan.".

`survey_order`'s commit world now declares `patFunnel` and grabs `emptyPunchRefusal`. **Mutations 10 of 10 killed** in a scratch clone, plus 1 expected-inert (Reset keeping the funnel). The TEETH list is in the suite header.

### ⚠⚠ A DASH THAT ENDS IN A DOT IS A LINE SYMBOL (Andy, 2026-10-01, with a screenshot of his console at Bellingham: "The path planner punch out for this survey has identified a cable way as a shore attached feature to be avoided. This particular feature is visually identified as a cable way by the segmented line, but each segment has a dot on one end. Correct the visual algorithm that mis-identified this.")

**What it was.** His console showed "+3 chart": three magenta "structures" read off the chart image. They were a 1,440 m line running southwest from the Whatcom Waterway (48.73877 N, 122.51265 W to 48.74832 N, 122.49940 W) and two east-west runs where it turns in to the shore (126 m and 51 m at 48.7484 N). Reproduced exactly in the pane on a throwaway (52828), with the page's own mosaic and mask painting over the same tiles and features: z18, 238 tiles, 3 structures. The ink is a 2 px stroke 31 px long with a 5 px dot on one end, every 36 px (35.5-36.8). NOAA's vector service carries no object along it (read-only `/api/enc`: only a depth area and contour touch it; the console already fetches every published layer), so nothing explained it. CHAINING - Andy's "segmented linear" rule for piers in pieces - joined 103 of the dashes into one mark that passed every shape gate. ⚠ The proportional attachment allowance (`ATTACH_FRAC` x length) then counted it ATTACHED 311.5 m off anything charted: a 1.4 km chain earns a 1.4 km allowance. **Noted, NOT changed (his call):** capping that allowance would also refuse a real structure far off a generalized coastline, which is the dangerous direction; the dot rule alone answers this case.

**The fix (chartink.js).** `endDot(xs, ys, fit)` bins a piece's pixels one pixel at a time along its own axis. The stroke's width is the MEDIAN across-extent over the middle half. A dot is a run of end bins at least `DOT_MIN_EXTRA_PX` (2) wider than the stroke, at least `DOT_MIN_RATIO` (1.75) times as wide, and COMPACT: the run is at least half the blob's width, which a T-head's crossbar is not. It is looked for within `DOT_END_FRAC` of either end, on pieces at least `DOT_MIN_LEN_PX` long. `chainMarks` carries `dots`. `dashDotWhy` refuses a chain with at least `DASHDOT_MIN_DOTS` (2) dotted pieces making up at least `DASHDOT_FRAC` (half) of its pieces: the verdict is overridden AFTER `classify`, so the reject keeps its measurements, and it carries `symbol: "dash-dot"`. A symbol is never a footprint (a bending dash-dot line chains wide and its hull would be a marina; 23f's control shows that it IS one with the rule off), and its why never says "not attached", so the page never reports it as detached. One dotted piece is left to the sieve.

**Measured, A/B in one module** (`{dashDotMinDots: Infinity}` turns the rule off):
- Bellingham: 3 structures → 0. Four dash-dot rejects: 100/103, 8/10, 7/10 and 3/4 pieces dotted.
- Kittery Point (154 tiles, z19), New Castle town and Fort Point (208 each): BYTE-IDENTICAL structures and footprints with the rule on and off (11 lines + 1 footprint, 10 + 2, 3 + 0). No kept structure has a single dotted piece.
- Live through the page: a 17 x 1,339 m survey across the cable way punched with the read at z18 (160 tiles). The row reads "690 zones · floor 2.3 m · +136 seabed", with no "+N chart". 10 of the 11 coverage lines that cross the cable inside the pattern run straight across it; the eleventh crosses 30 px from the pattern's edge, where its end was pulled back for the turn.

**Tests:** chart_ink 23-23g (the cable way refused; the same line without dots still one pier in pieces; one dotted piece still a pier; 2 of 8 dotted still a pier; `endDot`'s eight cases plus a blemish; the curving line's footprint control; and the existing scene unchanged). **Mutations 13 of 13 killed** in a scratch clone (the TEETH list in the suite's header is the printed run). D13 ("the stroke's width is its widest bin") first SURVIVED: every fixture's dash was clean. 23e's blemish is the case where median and max differ. With the ratio gate removed, 17, 17d and 6 went red too: the ratio is what keeps an ordinary pier's ends from reading as dots.

### ⚠⚠ A BUOY CORRIDOR YIELDS TO THE CHART (Andy, 2026-09-30: "fix the buoy corridor so charted channels win" - the item found on the live check of the disregard options, below)

**What it was.** `channelPolys` (keepouts.js) is the one list of channel polygons: the charted dredged areas and fairways, then a corridor for each gate `pairGates` makes (a port mark and its nearest starboard mark 15-400 m away), its line swept one gate width each way along the axis. Its doc said "where no dredged polygon is charted"; the code swept EVERY gate. At the Northward Channel (Portsmouth), gate 2 is buoys #3 / #4, 244 m apart either side of a charted strip about 20 m wide. Its 541 x 396 m corridor held the strip and both banks. The span rule takes the UNION, so a survey line drawn across the charted channel began and ended inside the corridor, read as contained, and was never cut. Measured over the live extract (read-only GETs of a throwaway's `/api/enc`): 5 of 7 gates bracket charted water. 3 of them pair a Sagamore Creek mark with a Northward Channel one (`pairGates` pairs across systems; noted, not changed). Gate 2's CENTER is outside the narrow strip, so "the center inside a charted polygon" would have missed it; it has to be the gate line. At Lewes the one gate (the Roosevelt Inlet jetties) also brackets charted channels.

**The fix: `gateSweep(P, gx, gy, ax, ay, w, Le, rings)`** (keepouts.js, drift #5). In the gate's strip coordinates (u along the gate line, t along the axis), a ring first touches the swept line at the smallest |t| of its boundary inside 0 <= u <= w. That is an endpoint of an edge clipped to the strip, so the answer is exact and O(edges), with a box prefilter. A clipped edge reaching t = 0, or the gate's midpoint inside a ring, means the gate line touches charted water, and the gate sweeps NOTHING. `GATE_SWEEP_MIN_M` = 1. A gate touching nothing keeps its old corridor vertex for vertex. A mouth beyond a charted end keeps its seaward corridor, stopped at the end, which is the overlap a mere "does the gate line cross it" rule would still let hide the channel. Corridors yield only to CHARTED rings, never to each other. Live extracts after: Portsmouth 11 charted + 2 corridors (gates 1 and 5, unchanged at 612 x 678 and 336 x 458 m); Lewes 15 + 0; ~0.4 ms a call.

**The lane reads the same list** (`narrowChannelLane`'s `inChartedChannel` and `extendCenterline`). A/B in Node, with the real modules over the live extracts, old list against new: every route identical (0.00 m apart). The lane engaged on the Lewes routes at buffers 3 and 6; on the Portsmouth paths tried it engaged under neither list.

**Verified live** (throwaway 52827, the Z-Boat, Min depth 1 m, 3 m buffer, zoom 17, the boat at 43.0628 N, 70.7373 W): the failing pattern from the disregard-options check, 7 x 349 m east-west lines through the boat's position.
- Before the fix (52826, 22:20): "7 lines → 7 segments", no exclusion.
- After, with Shipping channels on: "7 lines → 14 segments ... 2 channel(s) excluded (survey spans across)". On the canvas, none of the 14 coverage pieces has a sample inside a charted channel ring. It is NOT READY: runs 10-11, the short pieces against the bank, have every loop entering water under 1.0 m.
- With Shipping channels off: "7 lines → 8 segments ... shipping-channel rules OFF", and 7 of the 8 pieces run through the charted channel. That path never calls `channelPolys`; it is 1.86 km against 22:20's 392 m because the set (0.24 kn), the tide and the re-extracted model differ.
- The DriX on the same pattern: "7 lines → 0 segments ... 14 line(s) under 80 m dropped (this hull's minimum), 2 channel(s) excluded ... Add to plan". ⚠ Noted, NOT changed: a punch that leaves nothing still says "Add to plan".

**Tests:** turn_channel 16-16j (the Northward shape, the survey it swallowed, a gate bracketing nothing keeps its corridor exactly, the mouth stopped at the charted end, a line near that end cut while the mouth still spans, a gate inside a wide fairway, a channel ahead shortens one side, a ring beside a DIAGONAL corridor's box does not, consecutive uncharted gates each keep theirs, a diagonal crossing in both windings). **Mutations 9 of 9 killed** in a scratch clone, its control green and the real files byte-identical after, graded on turn_channel + rule9_scope + buoy_lane (the lane suites never went red).
- C3 (the explicit "reaches the gate line" test removed) first SURVIVED. I had argued it was equivalent: a straddling edge's far endpoint drives fwd or back negative. It is not, wound clockwise, when the crossing edge leaves the strip through its side just past the line. 16j is that case.

### THE SURVEY CARD'S TWO "DISREGARD" OPTIONS (Andy, 2026-09-30: "on the survey settings card add options to disregard shipwreck avoidance and shipping channel avoidance to the existing 4 options. Then implement that feature change.")

**Two boxes after the four, both CHECKED on a fresh page**, so nothing changes until he unchecks one: `#enf_wreck` "Shipwrecks" and `#enf_chan` "Shipping channels". They ride in `nogo.enf` (`NOGO_ENF` in state.js and `ENFORCE_DEFAULTS` in keepouts.js both gain `wreck: true, chan: true`), and `enforcement()` refuses an unknown key, so `wrecks: false` throws instead of leaving every wreck armed. `applyNogoControls` reads both; the change list rebuilds and re-punches as for the other four; `patStrikeKey` already names `JSON.stringify(nogo.enf)`, so a clip taken under one setting is never served under the other. `contracts.nogoEnforcement` (vendored from asv_core) still names four keys, and nothing calls it.

**Shipwrecks (`wreck`) belongs to every behavior.** `buildKeepouts` drops `Wreck_point` (hazard_point, gated by `haz`) and `Wreck_area` (hazard_area, isLand, gated by `land`) AFTER the class gates and `hazPassable` (keepouts.js drift #4), so it only narrows: a wreck haz/land switched off is not counted and cannot be armed by it, and a passable wreck counts as `passed`. It returns `wrecksOff`. The guard, Go-To, RTH, search and both punch models are built from that one `enf`. It is said on the no-go row (`· wrecks off`), in its tip (the model's count, and a sentence at zero too) and on every punch ("Shipwrecks OFF: N charted wreck(s) in the area are not keep-outs"). The picture follows: `drawNogo` leaves a disregarded `Wreck_area` unfilled (`nogoLayerKeyNow` carries `enf.wreck !== false`), and `drawENC` keeps a disregarded wreck point's cross but drops its dashed keep-out circle (`encLayerKeyNow` carries it too). **The circle was found reviewing this change**: it is "the circle the router actually keeps out of", and it was still drawn round a wreck nothing kept out of.

**Shipping channels (`chan`) belongs to the SURVEY only.** In `punchOut`, `chanExcl = enf.chan === false ? [] : channelSpanKeepouts(...)`, and the same for `turnExcl`. Go-To, RTH and transits keep right under Rule 9 whatever it says (`channelLaneRoute` is untouched). The punch says "shipping-channel rules OFF (...)", and the tip says it too.

**Verified live** (throwaway 52826, the Z-Boat at a 1.0 m floor):

ON: "5 lines → 10 segments ... 1 missing turn(s) refused by a navigation channel ... 2 channel(s) excluded (survey spans across)", with every coverage segment stopping short of the strip (read off the canvas). OFF: "5 lines → 5 segments ... shipping-channel rules OFF ...", all five across it.

So a survey drawn across the channel there is "contained" in the union, and the span rule never fires: the first live pattern (7 x 349 m lines through the boat's position) punched 7 → 7 with the channel uncut, with Shipping channels on.

### ⚠⚠ THE SEABED'S OWN GAPS (Andy, 2026-09-30, with a screenshot of his console at Pepperrell Cove: "The ENC check routine that catches features not represented in layers missed these dock features and ran transits and survey lines across them. review the routine and improve.")

**What the floats are.** The yellow shapes off the two Kittery Point town piers (43.0817 N, 70.7032 W) are PONTONS - pontoons. NOAA's chart renderer draws them; ENCDirect publishes no pontoon layer in any band (the `Pontoon_line` note in `ENC_ROLES`), so the extract held nothing. Found by: his session log's 20:38 plan (the survey ran 43.0765-43.0822 N, 70.701-70.712 W, Fort Point to Pepperrell Cove) and the scan's own banner, "143 tiles at z18".

**Why the chart-image read missed them** (the routine he named, `scanChartInk` / `chartink.js`). Measured on the tiles it read, in a replica of the page's painting: 85-93% of each float's gray outline ink lay inside the EXPLAINED mask - under the rings of `Depth_Area`, `Quality_of_Data_area`, `Sea_Area_Named_Water_Area` ("Pepperrell Cove") and the anchorage. S-57's Group 1 (depth areas, dredged areas, land, floating docks, hulks, pontoons, unsurveyed areas) tiles the seabed with no gaps and no overlaps, so every pontoon is cut out of the depth areas round it, and their rings trace it exactly. The sieve got fragments: at z18 a 7 m piece "not attached" and a 3 m one "not thin enough"; at z19 an 8.4 m and a 5.1 m line, never the footprints.

**The fix: read them off the seabed's own topology (`static/js/skin.js`, `skinGaps`).** Every Group 1 ring is oriented with its polygon on the left. Each edge two polygons share runs once each way and cancels (by sorting packed keys; the vertices sit in an open-addressed typed hash). The survivors chain into rings, taking the smallest counter-clockwise turn at a shared vertex. The clockwise rings are the holes, and a hole wholly inside the extract box is a gap. **Measured exact:** 92.1% of New Castle's 183,639 edges cancel and every vertex balances (Lewes 89.8%, Los Angeles 97.8%). Gaps: New Castle 3 (the two floats, 62 m² and 194 m², plus one beside a pier at the shipyard), Lewes 0, LA 7 along the San Pedro waterfront. The two Kittery floats and one LA float were checked against the tiles. 156 New Castle holes cross the extract's edge (islands beyond it, unfetched) and are not judged. A partial extract missing a Group 1 layer is REFUSED, in words, on the row; `fetchENCBbox` now keeps `partial`. `Unsurveyed_Area` arrives as `extra` and counts as seabed. **Cost:** ~60 ms warm, ~280 ms cold (string keys were 650 ms), in a turn of its own in `refreshNogo`. The extract is captured BEFORE that turn, because `sea.enc` can be replaced while it waits.

**As FEATURES, not a fold** (`skinGapFeature`: role `dock`, cls `Skin_Gap_area`, `kind` = `SKIN_KIND`, `derived: "skin_gap"`), appended to `nogo.features`. So rebuildNogo, punchOut's two models, the guard, and the chart read's explained mask and attachment pool all have them with nothing to remember. `buildKeepouts` takes `f.kind` before `nogoKind` (keepouts.js drift #3), so a refusal names the float. They follow the structures toggle, are outlined in orange dashes in `drawNogo`, and are counted on the row as `+N seabed`, from the MODEL by kind.

**Tried and REVERTED - do not redo:** painting only the outlines the chart DRAWS into the explained mask (an `outlineExplains` whitelist). Over his survey at z18 it added 5 lines and 13 false "float system" footprints up to 115 m: the hachured drying lines round the ledges, which the undrawn depth-area and zone rings had been explaining. Excluding only the magenta limits changed nothing. Every ring is still painted; comments at EXPLAIN_PX and in `scanChartInk` say why.

**Also, found reviewing the routine:** `ensureChartInk`'s catch KEPT its key, so a read that threw was cached as a clean read for the session and said so only on the readout. Now no key, a rebuild, and a banner, the same rule a refusal obeys. (The "chart read failed: TypeError" in his 20:31 log was the ENC EXTRACT failing during a restart, `refreshNogo`'s note, not this.)

**Verified live** (throwaway 52825, the Z-Boat at a 1.0 m floor, his conditions): the row read `1191 zones · floor 1.0 m · +3 seabed`, and the floats are filled as structures. A Go-To due west across both floats was "routed around nogo zone(s) via 9 waypoints"; the boat's track passed south of them and the chained RTH came back the same way. A 9-line survey drawn across both was punched with every line that crossed them cut at the floats.

**Tests:** skin_gaps.js NEW (19: the hole, the Z gap between two polygons, the fillers land / dredged / unsurveyed / floating dock, windings, a pier over a hole, the box edge, partial, gaps touching at a corner from every starting vertex (64 ways) and a hole touching the outer limit (20 ways), a sliver, the feature and its kind and toggle). nogo_readout 20-20e (the row) and 21-21c (the fold, partial, the capture); chart_ink 14b (a thrown read). **Mutations 18 of 19 killed** in a scratch clone. The survivor is "take the FIRST edge at a shared vertex": not killed in 246 layouts, because ids are handed out ring by ring, so the ring a chain arrives on owns the lowest-keyed edge there. "Take the LAST" is killed by 7 and 7b.

⚠ **Noted, NOT changed (his call):** `Offshore_Platform_area`, `Fishing_Facility_area`, `Marine_Farm_Culture_area` and `Dry_Dock_area` arrive as `extra` and are not keep-outs (none in his New Castle area). `Land_Area_point` islets (110 at New Castle, all in water) are not enforced, but every one sits in a drying depth area that is.

### THE AIS CARD OPENS AT 5 nm (Andy, 2026-09-30: "change AIS default range to 5km", then "I mean default range on the AIS card", then "push, merge and commit when ready" - and after `a969fc6790` shipped 5 km: "oops. I meant 5nm not 5 km")

`AIS_SHOW_RADIUS_KM` 50 → **`5 * 1852 / 1000.0` = 9.26 km, 5 nm** (`asv_console.py`; `--ais-radius-km` defaults to it, and its help now says "default 9.26 - 5 nm on the card"). **`a969fc6790` set 5.0 km on his literal "5km"; he meant nautical miles** - the unit the card reads in (his own earlier call). The collect radius stays 150 km, so widening from the card is still instant. The field reads a tenth of a mile below 10 nm and whole miles above, the contact list's own rule (`fmtNm`): `nmField` in `static/js/units.js`, and `nmRound(km)` is `nmField(nmFromKm(km))`; the label, the echo, "n of m in X nm" and "nearest X nm" all go through it. That came in for the 5 km misread - whole miles would have shown 5 km as "3", which is 5.56 km, and the first Enter would have moved the filter there - and it STAYS at 5 nm, which reads 5 either way, so a range under 10 nm can be set and read as finely as the list reports one. The markup opens at `value="5"` with `step="1"` (with `min="1"` a step of 5 went 5 → 6 → 11). `setAisRange` cuts a typed value to `nmField` BEFORE sending, so the echo reads back what was typed. A blank entry takes the field's own `defaultValue`; it used to take a literal 27, which with the new default would have widened a cleared box to 27 nm.

**⚠ The range is NOT display-only** (the tech manual's constants table said "DISPLAY filter only"; corrected, and said in the ops manual too). `pollAIS` is the one poll, and `aisKeepoutsNow` builds the guard's keep-outs from `aisVessels`, which is what the filter let through. The guard needs far less: its horizon is 45 s, and a contact closing at 30 kn covers under 700 m in that. A far destination's hold disc is re-measured against the contacts once she holds there (`holdDiscTick`).

**Verified live, twice** (throwaway 52823, no radius flag, a stub feed with contacts due east of the spawn - the server merges TEST contacts unfiltered by range, so they cannot test the filter). At 5 nm (contacts at 1 / 5 / 9 / 9.5 / 20 / 40 km): the card opened at 5, "3 of 6 in 81 nm", `show_km` 9.26, R1KM 0.5 / R5KM 2.7 / R9KM 4.9 nm and R9.5KM (5.13 nm) out; typed 5.3 → 9.8156 km, R9.5KM in (4 of 6); cleared → 5, 9.26 km. On the 5 km build before it (1 / 3 / 4.8 / 5.3 / 8 / 20 / 40 km): 2.9 → 5.3708 km; 2.75 → the field 2.8, 5.1856 km; cleared → the default; the up-arrow → 3, 5.556 km (snaps to the step); 12.4 → 12, 22.224 km; 100 → clamped to 150 km, the field 81. Neither console logged an exception.

**Tests:** ais_range 11 (a SECOND console, no radius flag, reports `show_km` 9.26 and `collect_km` 150 - the first is booted with `--ais-radius-km 50`, so it could never see the default), 8c (the markup equals the REPORTED default as the field shows it, 5 - not a copied constant), 8h (the fallback is the field's `defaultValue`, no literal `||27`); 3 renamed, because the first console's 50 km is the flag's, not the default; 26 checks. units_toggle 13 (nmRound: 9.26 → 5, 5 → 2.7, 50 → 27, 150 → 81; a typed 5 / 2.7 / 1.6 / 9.9 / 10 / 27 / 81 round-trips the wire's km; 14 checks). **Mutations 7 of 7 killed** in a scratch clone, its control green, the real files byte-identical after: the default back to 50 km (11, 8c), the misread's 5 km (11, 8c), `nmField` in whole miles (13), `nmRound` bypassing it (13), the markup left at 2.7 (8c), `setAisRange`'s old line (8h), the typed value sent uncut (8h).

### ⚠⚠ TWO DRAWINGS OF ONE SHIP, AND SIX FROM HIS LIST (Andy, 2026-09-30: "Do 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8. push, merge, commit at the end" - then, mid-work: "The AIS targets at the pier in Los Angeles show 2 separate states. **Los Angeles: two drawings, two rules.** The keep-out (`aisKeepout`, `static/js/ais_keepout.js`) turned a contact by `aisHeadingDeg` - her heading, her course only while under way, a disc when neither; the AIS layer (`drawAIS` in the page) by `v.cog != null ? v.cog : v.heading` - her COURSE first. A moored ship's course is GNSS noise. **Measured on his feed round Pier 300** (a read-only GET of 8791's `/api/ais`): CMA CGM AMAZON moored at 0.0 kn, heading 251 (her berth), cog 327.5 - drawn 76° across the pier; 21 of the 45 contacts nearest it drawn more than 10° off their own keep-out; the ones with no heading (CABRILLO: cog 223) drawn along their noise while the keep-out was a disc. Now **`aisMotion(v, {now, polledAt})` is THE rule** - `moving` is the keep-out's own test (AIS_MOVING_KN with a course, not nav-stopped under AIS_NAV_TRUST_KN, not slow-and-old), `hdg` is `aisHeadingDeg(v, moving)`, `from` is "heading" / "course" / null - and both call it: `aisKeepout` destructures it; `drawAIS` draws the hull or glyph at `mo.hdg`, or `drawHullDisc` (dashed, radius `aisDiscM(box)`, the keep-out's disc) when it is null, and the speed stalk along the COURSE from the bow, only when `mo.moving`. **Found on the visual check, not in the suites:** once the two agree, a moored ship's hull lies exactly on her red outline, and `render()` drew the keep-outs FIRST - her hull painted her outline out. `drawAisKeepouts` now runs after `drawAIS`. `updateAisTip` says which way she is drawn and why ("Drawn along her heading, 251°" / "Drawn along her course, 90° — under way, no heading reported" / "No heading reported and not under way — drawn as a circle: she can lie any way round") and marks a stopped ship's COG "(noise while she is stopped)"; the AIS button's title explains the two drawings, and drops "Situational awareness only" (false since 2026-09-25). **Verified visually** on a throwaway console at LA with test contacts - AMAZON-T (heading 251, cog 327.5, 366 x 48), CABRILLO-T (heading 511 = not available, cog 223), UNDERWAY-T (8 kn on 090, no heading): the hull along 071/251 under its red outline, the dashed circle inside the red disc, the hull along its course with the red sweep ahead; the three tips as quoted. ⚠ **Recorded, NOT changed:** `aisDiscM` is half the hull's diagonal about the ANTENNA, which covers every orientation only for an antenna amidships (a 300 m ship with her antenna 50 m from the stern swings her bow 250 m from it) - growing it changes the guard's model, not a drawing. ### ⚠ THE ALERTS CARD DRAGS AGAIN, AND EVERY LINE IN IT WRAPS (Andy, 2026-09-29: "The alert card when on the chart browser window locks to the left of the frame and cannot be moved around. also, not all the lines wrap")

**Measured first** (a throwaway console, the in-app pane at 1600x900, split mode with the card ON CHART): the card authored at 400..1200 (left:50% + translateX(-50%), 800 wide); a 100 px drag right put its left edge at **51**, and the first 10 px of movement threw it to -39, because `makeDraggablePanel` released the bottom anchor but never the translate, so the card was drawn half its width left of the `left` the drag and `clampPanelPos` work in. `width:auto` on an absolutely placed box is the room right of its left edge, so it grew to 898 once dragged, and the clamp (`left <= chart - width`) then held it in a band at the left edge with half of it off the chart. A stored v1 position was the card's CENTER. **Not the cause, checked:** the controls window's copy is a mirror whose listeners do not survive the sync, so a drag there writes nothing to the key.

**The fix (`static/asv.html`):** `unanchorPanel` releases the translate for a panel registered `uncenter: true` (the alerts card), on the drag and the restore alike; `.alertcard` is `width:max-content; max-width:50%` (the width it had before a drag, now the same wherever it is); `.alertrecent .arow .ax` wraps (`min-width:0; overflow-wrap:anywhere`, the nowrap and the ellipsis gone); `ALERTCARD_KEY` = `asv_alertcard_v2`, so a v1 center is never read as a left edge (the card starts at its authored place once). The controls window is untouched: `.uicard>[id]` and `body.ui-controls .uicard .rsz` override the width, the cap and the translate (measured: 708 of a 710 px wrapper, before and after).

**Verified live** (same console): every step of a 100 px drag within 0 px of the mouse, the width constant at 800; all four edges reached with the card fully on the chart; stored = on screen; a reload restores it exactly; narrowed to 380 px, every line wraps with 0 px overflow (the guard reason, the banner, the note, the recent rows); a corner resize tops out at half the chart. **Tests:** panel_drag 7 now reads class rules too (`authoredFor`: the card is anchored by its class, which the inline-style read could not see), 28 (a translate-centered panel declares uncenter, derived from the stylesheet), 28b (`unanchorPanel` releases it and leaves another panel's transform alone), 28c-28f (the page's own drag code run against a model of the card's CSS with its real registration options: it moves with the mouse, reaches every edge, restores where it was left, stores where it is), 29 (the width), 30 (no nowrap or ellipsis for the card), 31 (the key). **Control: the old build fails all nine; mutations 10/10** (`scratchpad/mut_alertcard_0929.py`). Page only: a refresh, no restart.

### ⚠⚠ EVERY FRAME COSTS A FIFTH: THE KEEP-OUT LAYER CACHED, AND BOTH LAYERS SURVIVE THE VIEW FOLLOWING THE BOAT (Andy, 2026-09-29: "#1", then "definitely push and merge")

**Measured first** (an instrumented scratch copy of the page, a throwaway console with his `mission.json`, 200 wpts): a telemetry frame 23.9 ms idle, `render()` 22.9 of it, **`drawNogo` 18.6** (every feature of the extract re-projected and re-filled at 4 Hz, hidden or not: the page read `hidden` and still rendered 83 times in 20 s), tiles 2.4, lines 0.8, the rest ~1. Under way at 7.7 kn with follow on: 27.0 ms a frame, nogo 17.5, ENC 1.6 (the ENC layer was keyed on the view to the pixel, and `onState` re-centers on the boat every frame).

**Why not rAF (my recommendation #1 said so):** enc_cache 8 pins the 2026-09-22 decision that the telemetry path renders DIRECTLY (a covered, or wrongly-occluded, window would freeze a chart the operator may be looking at), and at 4 Hz rAF saves nothing while the page is visible. Caching the heavy layers cuts the cost in EVERY case instead, and check 8 stands.

**The fix (`static/asv.html`):** `makeLayer` / `layerHolds` / `drawLayer`: a layer drawn over the view plus `LAYER_PAD_PX` 256 a side, blitted at the view's whole-pixel offset into it, redrawn only when its key, a source (by identity) or the view's containment fails. The ENC layer uses it (key: zoom, floor, wreck radius, buffer, tide; the origin and size left the key). `drawNogo(toScreen, ctx)` takes its context and `drawNogoCached` holds it: key = zoom, enf.land, enf.depth, nogoDR min/max, depthRange min/max (the survey window, the amber tier), `!!currentPattern()`, tide; sources = nogo.features, chartInk.lines, chartInk.areas. A cached vertex can sit up to half a pixel off the live layers (whole-pixel blit), which the view-keyed cache did too.

**Result (same console, same plan):** idle 23.9 -> **5.1 ms** a frame (render 4.1, nogo 0.03); under way at 7.7 kn, follow on, z13 27.0 -> **7.3 ms**, z17 **8.0 ms**; **0 layer misses in 30 s** each (a 6 kn boat crosses the margin in ~100 s at z17). Checked by eye at z13 and z17: the shading on the land, the hazard circle, marks and structures in place.

**Tests:** enc_cache 2 (a pan inside the margin: nothing drawn, the blit moves by the pan), 2b (past it: a redraw), 5b (the ENC key names the zoom; the origin used to carry it), 9 (now on `encLayer.cv`), 10 (the keep-out layer cached; off or 0x0: nothing drawn or blitted), 11 (every input redraws: both toggles, the floor, the survey window both ways, a pattern up, the tide, the zoom), 12 (sources by identity), 13 (the cached draw IS the direct draw moved by its blit: every vertex, exact at a whole-pixel origin, within 0.5 px at a fractional one), 14 (render goes through `drawNogoCached`); chart_ink 15's slice now starts at `function drawNogo(` exactly. **Mutations 15/15** (`scratchpad/mut_layers_0929.py`). All 68 JS suites by hand; hook not run (his rule). Page/module only: a refresh, no restart.

### ⚠⚠ THE ROUTING FREEZE WAS THE CHART READ (Andy, 2026-09-29: "Fix the routing freeze, push and merge")

**Measured, not assumed:** planNogoRoute for his line-8 RTH is 40 ms and routePlan for his 25-line plan (`D:\Claude\ASV\mission.json`, 200 wpts) 100-300 ms. The freeze was `scanChartInk`: after the tile wait, everything ran in ONE task (the browser's long-animation-frame record attributed a 3,005 ms script to the last tile's `onload`, line 9659, which is `scanChartInk`'s synchronous tail plus `ensureChartInk`'s rebuild and RTH up to its first network await). Its phases on the RTH box (204 tiles, z19, 13.4 MP): `classify` 970 ms a round x 2 rounds (`nearestSeg` walked all **97,753** structure segments of the whole extract twice per mark, for 70 marks; 2,904 near the canvas); painting all 5,530 features 249 ms; two `getImageData` 298 ms; inkMask 112, components 91, unexplained 40.

**The fix:** (1) `segIndex` (chartink.js): a grid over the segments (`SEG_CELL_PX` 64, long ones in a list every query reads), queried ring by ring, stopping only when the best is STRICTLY nearer than anything unread can be, ties to the LOWEST index (the walk's strict `<`), and a walk once the square would exceed the occupied cells (a far point swept 15,000 rings otherwise). `classify` takes the index or a list; `scanChart` builds one and `add`s each round's winners. **Exact:** on his chart the old and new scan outputs are byte-identical (JSON), and 5,642 probes (3,000 random + 2,642 vertices) gave 0 differences in distance or segment; 1,687 -> 268 ms. (2) A `scanSteps` generator with two drivers: `scanChart` (sync, the tests') and `scanChartSliced` (awaits `pause` after inkMask, unexplained, components). (3) The page: `featureLLBox` (a WeakMap per feature object) + `onCanvas` paints only what can light the canvas (Mercator is axis-aligned; `INK_PAINT_REACH_PX` 16 covers the 14 px sounding disc) but gathers structure segments from EVERY feature in the same order. Measured on his chart: 214 of 5,530 painted, the mask identical in all 53.5 M bytes, the segs identical. The paint loop yields every `INK_SLICE_MS` 40; `inkYield` (= turns.js `breathe`, setTimeout 0) between the two reads and before the analysis; `ensureChartInk` yields after the scan, before the rebuild; `doUpload` yields after `ensureNogoCovers` (fenced by the same `was` snapshot; Go-To and RTH already took 50 ms there). `CHART_INK_MAX_TILES`'s comment said "about 4 MB of pixels"; it is 16.8 M pixels, 67 MB of RGBA per canvas.

**Result (long tasks, the browser's own record):** RTH line 8 -> home 3,005 ms -> **137 ms**; his plan's Upload 4-9 s -> **378 ms** (what remains is routePlan + certifyDeparture + the corner walk's first slice, the routing itself; a rebuilt model does NOT slow the next route: 137 / 147 / 182 ms warm / after rebuild / again). **Not this commit's:** ~~each telemetry frame costs 30-70 ms of `onFrame` (the chart render per frame)~~ FIXED in the next commit (EVERY FRAME COSTS A FIFTH, above); in a hidden tab each `inkYield` can wait ~1 s (timer throttling), so a background read takes a few seconds longer; the frames themselves are not throttled.

**Tests:** chart_ink 22 (the grid vs the walk: polylines' shared vertices, long, zero-length, far, NaN, empty), 22b (classify's verdicts identical), 22c (growth by `add`; a cross-cell tie still goes to the lower index; without that case the explicit tie clause could be deleted with every check green), 22g (a far point: ~1 cell visited, not 2.4 M), 22d (20,000 off-canvas segments: the same result, 20 distances read against 120,012), 22e (sliced == sync, pauses between steps), 22f (the page wiring). **Mutations 16/16** (`scratchpad/mut_freeze2.py`: tie to the higher index; no tie clause; a whole cell of stop margin; the long list unread; a cell keeping its last segment; a loose stop; the walk again; no pause; no yield; no far fallback; off-canvas structures losing segments; segments only where painted; the analysis in one task; no turn before the rebuild; none before the Upload's routing; no paint slicing). ⚠ chartink.js and chart_ink.js are CRLF in the working tree: a sweep's multi-line anchors need `\r\n` (two SKIPs the first time).

### ⚠⚠ THE FOUR OPEN ITEMS: THE CRAB IN THE LOOK-AHEAD, THE HOLD SPEED AT EVERY STATION-KEEP, THE CONTACTS IN EVERY HOLD DISC, THE FORECAST SET (Andy, 2026-09-29: "Fix the open items, push and merge")

The four `e16ed82853` left open.

**(1) The deviation CHATTER (open since 2026-09-26).** `projectRoute` (`static/js/guard.js`) swung the bow straight at the waypoint and ADDED the set, so in a cross-set it predicted a boat that pursues the waypoint and is carried off it, while the vessel's line-follower (SimVcu.tick's crab feedforward; any real autopilot's cross-track control) solves the drift triangle and holds the line; the edge rung read a phantom entry and deviated her off a line she was holding. **Measured** through the page's own guard (`scratchpad/chatter_probe.js`, now ais_avoid 22), a boat crabbing at 7 kn through the water down a line 8 m off a pier (clear of the 5 m a deviation wants): 2 / 3 / 4 amends in 90 s at 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 kn of set toward the pier before, 0 after (calm to 2.5 kn); a line 2 m off (inside the buffer) still gets exactly 1. His 2026-09-26 record (`logs/asv_20260926-075847.jsonl`: 62 amends, the 08:05:11 burst 37 in 115 s, "8.0 m off", hdg 25-37 deg off cog) FITS but was an older build (`5950ea9d75`) and was NOT replayed. Now `h = turnToward(h, (brg - asin(clamp(dCross / twMs, ±CRAB_MAX_SIN))) / D2R, swing)`: the bow that puts the GROUND track on the waypoint. `CRAB_MAX_SIN` 0.9 (~64 deg, the simulator's clamp); a set beyond it still carries her. `twMs > 0` is the function's first test. With no route (station-keeping, paused, RC) `guardTrack` is null and the straight projection is unchanged.

**(2) The hold speed at EVERY station-keep.** `speedGovernor` stood down on `st.holding` from its first line, so a boat station-keeping at a Go-To point, at home after an RTH or at the end of a plan kept the speed her last leg ran at (HIGH after a Go-To/RTH) for the whole hold; `e16ed82853` gave behavior "hold" the `hold` role, which acted only in the instant before she reported holding. Now the act gate excludes only an ESCAPE's hold (`!(st.holding && S.behavior === "escape")`: that throttle is `escapeThrottle`'s claim), and `currentActivity`'s non-escape holding branch returns role `hold` → `roleSpeed("hold")` = `slowestMakingWayKey(setMsNow()) || "low"`. Still behind `indexedRoute()`: Go-To and RTH set `runRoute` on the page that sent them; a page reloaded mid-hold stands down as before. A speed selector pressed during a hold sets the NEXT leg's speed (`setRoleSpeed` nulls `commandedSpeed`; the governor re-asserts the hold speed on the next frame): like `depart`, the hold role is not the operator's to set.

**(3) The CONTACTS in every hold disc.** `hold_clear_m` was measured against `nogo.ko` alone, so a moored ship near the hold point sat inside the certified disc (held 51 m short of FRIGGA, the disc sent was 64 m) and a boat set past her would drive a straight chord back through her. Plans still never see a contact (Andy's rule). ⚠ The disc is certified at COMMAND time: a contact that arrives later is the guard's to answer, frame by frame, not the disc's.

### ⚠⚠ THE HOLD STANDS UNTIL SHE LEAVES IT: THE THREE OPEN ITEMS (Andy, 2026-09-29: "Fix the three open items, push and merge")

The three his FRIGGA run left open after `a97e660bb6`, all measured in `logs/asv_20260928-204123.jsonl`:

**(1) The latch and the throttle while she holds.** The clear branch fired 6 s into the guard's own hold ("Clear ahead again (43.3 m) — speed back to high (transit)") because its counterfactual projects the plan's speed along the station-keep's bow, which points up-set, away from the hazard; it wiped `guardActedAt`/`holdWant`, so every later HOLD frame was a first action. Now `if(S.behavior === "hold" && guardActedAt > 0)` returns before any release (arriving, on station, paused or stopped on the guard's hold); the record ends with a new commanded motion — `resumeHeldRun`'s success path resets `guardActedAt`, `holdWant`, `guardLevel = "clear"`, `holdBackAt`, and `setPlanIntent` for any new plan. The HIGH came from the instant between the hold command and her arrival on station: `currentActivity` classified behavior "hold" as a TRANSIT, the governor acted in that instant (it stands down once `st.holding`), and the transit speed stuck for the whole hold. Now behavior "hold" → role `hold` → `roleSpeed("hold")` = `slowestMakingWayKey(setMsNow()) || "low"` (not the operator's to set, like `depart`).

**(2) The station-keep creep (the SIMULATOR, `asv_console.py`).** SimVcu's station-keep drove the way back at `SPEED_KN["low"]`, bow straight at the point; the small-class boat's LOW is 1.5 kn, so in his 1.75 kn set every return lost 0.25 kn: 0.1-0.13 m/s toward FRIGGA for the whole hold (measured again: 17.5 m in 120 s). Now `hold_speed_kn(|_drift_en|)` — the slowest of low/survey/high beating the set by `HOLD_MAKES_WAY_KN` 0.5 (the page's margin), the fastest if none does — and the bow crabbed with the line-follower's drift-triangle feedforward. Calm water is LOW exactly as before; the hold radius (command nothing inside 2 m) and the certified disc (`hold_wants_route` beyond it) are untouched. A real vessel's station-keeping is its own.

**(3) A Pause during the guard's hold.** Each Pause let the set carry her and the (latch-released) rung answered with /api/cmd/hold — "at PRESENT position" — ratcheting the point 48 → 41 → 33 → 25 m off FRIGGA. Now, in the hold rung before the latch test, `pausedOwn` (run paused, behavior hold, `guardActedAt > 0`) with the ladder reading HOLD sends /api/cmd/start ("Resumed." — the paused hold back to ITS OWN point) with "BACK ON STATION", paced by `holdBackAt`/`SLOW_ANSWER_MS`, counted by `guardMove("put her back on station")`. NOT with `S.plan_staged` (a Start would apply the staged plan): then `backDue` joins the latch test and the old hold at present position goes, paced — which also keeps a held resume stalled past its stand-by after its upload answered (20g). A STOPPED boat is neither (only helm).

### ⚠⚠ THE TREADMILL (Andy, 2026-09-28: "There is no obvious way to increase speed again" / "I have to acknowledge warning pop-ups many times why is that?")

**His 08:34 log (`logs/asv_20260928-083455.jsonl`), read press by press:** 58 presses in fifty minutes against FRIGGA — 35 PROCEED (21 of them recorded at level CLEAR: the bar showed SLOW, the click landed a frame later on a clear frame, `guardOverrideOk` nulled it on `level === "clear"`), 7 CONTINUE AT LOW, 16 RESUME AT LOW after holds. Three mechanisms: (1) the override lapsed on `OVERRIDE_GIVE_M` (5 m) every ~6 m of progress, because a hazard ON the track shrinks the clearance by exactly the distance run (the stair in the log: pressed at 36.4 m, 30.3, 24.1, 18.0, hold); (2) the ladder chatters SLOW/CLEAR every ~10 s around the horizon, and the release's counterfactual was gated on `clearance.slowed`, which every press CLEARS (PROCEED and continueAtLow hand the throttle back by that flag) — so after a press the release fired on the first clear frame with no counterfactual, restored HIGH, and SLOW came back; (3) the LOW latch (`resumeSlow`) had ONE release, `setRoleSpeed` (a selector in another panel that only fires on an actual value change); CANCEL OVERRIDE left it; the banner said "until you change it" without saying where; his boat crawled at 1.5 kn for minutes with the bar down. And FRIGGA herself: 0.4-0.8 kn, reports twenty minutes apart, at anchor — at 0.8 kn (≥ AIS_MOVING_KN 0.5) modelled as UNDER WAY: DR 60 s + a 45 s sweep = 43 m of phantom hull up her course, which reached the way round her (12:28:00 SLOW at 17.6 m on the route that had just been built clear of her). **Four fixes (`this commit`):** (1) `releaseLow()` + `#gb_release` "RELEASE LOW — BACK TO THE PLAN'S SPEED" on the bar in every rung state while `resumeSlow && running`, and a bar of its own ("LOW — OPERATOR'S AUTHORITY") when the ladder reads clear; `#gb_cancel` releases the latch too; the release note says "still at LOW on your authority" when latched; every "until you change it" names the button. (2) `guardOverrideOk(level, clearM, key, closing)`: a clear frame starts `clearSince` and does not spend it; ended by helm, by a DIFFERENT hazard (`guardHazardKey`: the contact's kind, else the readout's feature, else the nearest charted kind via `blockedInfo(p, koAll, c.m + 0.5)`; said with both named), by the RELEASE (clearanceGuard's clear branch returns before the override is consulted, so a clear FRAME never reaches guardOverrideOk - the release, counterfactual then dwell, is the "behind her" ending, and always was), by `OVERRIDE_STALE_MS` 45 s for a press that meets no hazard (a press against clear water is not a standing permission), or by the 5 m give ONLY when `closing` (the NEAREST hazard is a contact under way: `aisNearestPoly(p, aisKo).moving` and her distance equals `c.m` — the adversarial review caught the first draft gating it on `aisCaused`, so a contact closing on her never lapsed it while a charted feature was also in the track; the same review caught `releaseLow` leaving a CONTINUE AT LOW override standing with the hold rung suppressed at the plan's speed — it ends it now, 18j/18k); a press against the bar's last frame adopts the first key it sees. ### ⚠ THE 09:38 MISSION REVIEW (Andy, 2026-09-26: "review latest mission. Determine reason for path planning that required user intervention to move forward and tune path planning algorithms to reduce or eliminate the need for user intervention")

**What intervened** (`logs/asv_20260926-093810.jsonl`, New Castle, sim, 21 kn from 050, the stream source unreadable): six automatic escapes (09:40:50, 09:45:28, 10:27:45, 10:38:20, 10:45:41, 10:45:59), each followed by his RESUME / PROCEED or a Stop; seven PROCEEDs on SLOW during the 10:05 approach; a Stop + RTH after the last pair. **The cause, replayed against the real extract** (`scratchpad/replay_guard.js`: the guard reproduced to the meter and the second at four of the six): the sim published `env_set_kn` 0.00 at the berth — the LEEWAY half of the set was still gated on `_running` (the stream half had been un-gated on 09-02 under a comment claiming REPORTED ALWAYS) — so every punch clipped at `guardStandoffM(3, 0)` = 3 m; the set read 1.75 kn (`LEEWAY_CAP_MS`) the instant she started and the guard's standoff became 19.5 m. Four escapes were the helm rung 6.8—10.7 m off a keep-out at line ends and in turns ("on drift ALONE it is 7—12 s from within 1.5 m"). **And the turns were the larger half:** 26 of 56 line ends but 91 of 207 turn legs of the 09:40 plan sat inside 19.5 m; a fly-through of the uploaded route at that set read helm 115x in the turns against 28x on the lines — the seam's promise ("not ON A LINE") was kept and she was escaped from the turn. (2) `static/asv.html` — `edgeSearchAt`: `searchDue = now - edgeSearchAt >= EDGE_REASSESS_MS` in `wantEdge`, stamped when a search is asked for; guard_resume 23 (three frames in one instant ask ONCE, a frame 2.1 s later asks again). Worlds that run clearanceGuard learned `edgeSearchAt` (guard_resume, ais_avoid, clearance_guard). ⚠ Not seen live: he must RESTART his console (it served the old page) — watch `client:page_stall` in his next log. ⚠ Still open: 62 amends in 6 min this morning (1.5-4.5 m dog-legs to port, every ~6 s) — the deviation CHATTERS; with the search clocked and cheap it no longer freezes anything, but that hysteresis (`want = buf + margin`) is its own change. ⚠ **THE HOOK'S TIME LIMIT RUNS THROUGH `tests/lib/limit.py` NOW** (found by precommit_hook.py 4 refusing this very commit): MSYS `timeout` killed a hung suite at the limit and RETURNED ~45 s LATER on this machine, python and node alike (measured: the process gone at 7 s, `timeout` back at 47 s; a plain `sleep` 4 s), so the hook runs `python $HOOK_DIR/../tests/lib/limit.py $SUITE_LIMIT_S <runner> <suite>` — Python's own wait, `taskkill /T` for the tree, exit 124 — with GNU timeout the fallback.
